              Demuestre analíticamente por qué un sistema trifásico equilibrado entrega una potencia instantánea total estrictamente constante en el tiempo p_3phi(t) = 3 P, eliminando las oscilaciones a 2 omega presentes en sistemas monofásicos y evitando vibraciones mecánicas en generadores.
              Solución:
              En un sistema trifásico equilibrado:
              p_a(t) = P + P cos(2 omega t) + Q sin(2 omega t).
              p_b(t) = P + P cos(2 omega t - 240°) + Q sin(2 omega t - 240°).
              p_c(t) = P + P cos(2 omega t - 120°) + Q sin(2 omega t - 120°).
              Potencia instantánea total: p_3phi(t) = p_a(t) + p_b(t) + p_c(t)
              p_3phi(t) = 3 P + P [ cos(2 omega t) + cos(2 omega t - 120°) + cos(2 omega t + 120°) ] + Q [ sin(2 omega t) + sin(2 omega t - 120°) + sin(2 omega t + 120°) ].
              Por simetría trigonométrica de tres fasores desfasados 120° en el plano complejo:
              sum_{k=0}^2 cos(alpha - k * 120°) = 0, y sum_{k=0}^2 sin(alpha - k * 120°) = 0.
              Ambos términos oscilatorios se anulan idénticamente a cero para todo t.
              Por lo tanto:
              p_3phi(t) = 3 P = constante.
              Esto demuestra la superioridad fundamental de los sistemas trifásicos en generación y motores industriales: entregan torque continuo y libre de pulsaciones mecánicas de doble frecuencia. Q.E.D.
            bloque_sugerido: "Laboratorio 50 min • Potencia instantánea a doble frecuencia y ventaja trifásica"
            slides:
              - numero: 1
                seccion: "INSTANTÁNEA"
                titulo: "Descomposición de p(t)"
                puntos:
                  - "Término constante de potencia activa P = V_rms I_rms cos(phi)."
                  - "Fluctuación a frecuencia doble 2 omega debida a intercambio reactivo."
              - numero: 2
                seccion: "TRIFÁSICA"
                titulo: "Invarianza Temporal Trifásica"
                puntos:
                  - "Cancelación analítica de oscilaciones de 120 Hz en redes equilibradas."
                  - "Torque electromagnético constante libre de vibraciones de fatiga."
          - numero_tema: 28
            corte: 3
            modalidad: "tecnica"
            titulo: "Potencia Compleja, Activa, Reactiva y el Triángulo de Potencias"
            objetivo: "Modelar el balance de potencia compleja S = P + jQ y aplicar el Teorema de Conservación de la Potencia Compleja."
            concepto_clave_latex: "\\mathbf{S} = \\mathbf{V}_{\\text{rms}} \\mathbf{I}_{\\text{rms}}^* = P + jQ = |\\mathbf{S}|\\angle\\theta \\quad ; \\quad |\\mathbf{S}| = \\sqrt{P^2 + Q^2} \\quad ; \\quad \\text{FP} = \\frac{P}{|\\mathbf{S}|} = \\cos(\\theta)"
            ejemplo: |
              CLASE MAGISTRAL: EL TRIÁNGULO DE POTENCIAS Y POTENCIA COMPLEJA
              1. Definición Formal de la Potencia Compleja S:
              S = V_rms * I_rms^*, donde I_rms^* es el conjugado complejo del fasor de corriente (el conjugado es matemáticamente necesario para que la potencia reactiva inductiva sea positiva Q > 0).
              - Parte Real: Potencia Activa P en Vatios (W).
              - Parte Imaginaria: Potencia Reactiva Q en Voltio-Amperios Reactivos (VAR).
              * Cargas inductivas (motores): Q > 0 (absorben reactivos).
              * Cargas capacitivas (bancos de condensadores): Q < 0 (generan reactivos).
              - Magnitud |S|: Potencia Aparente en Voltio-Amperios (VA).
              2. Factor de Potencia (FP = cos phi):
              Razón entre la potencia activa que realiza trabajo útil y la potencia aparente total demandada a la red (FP = P / |S| in [0, 1]).
              3. Conservación de la Potencia Compleja (Teorema de Boucherot):
              En cualquier red eléctrica AC, la potencia compleja total entregada por las fuentes es igual a la suma fasorial de las potencias complejas absorbidas por cada rama:
              sum S_fuentes = sum S_cargas => sum P_fuentes = sum P_cargas, y sum Q_fuentes = sum Q_cargas.
              4. Problema Resuelto 1 (Aplicación Directa):
              Una instalación comercial se alimenta a V = 220 angle(0°) V RMS y absorbe una corriente I = 25 angle(-36.87°) A RMS. Calcule la potencia compleja S, la potencia activa P, la potencia reactiva Q, la potencia aparente |S| y el factor de potencia FP indicando si está en adelanto o atraso.
              Solución:
              Conjugado de la corriente: I^* = 25 angle(+36.87°) A.
              Potencia compleja:
              S = V * I^* = (220 angle(0°)) * (25 angle(36.87°)) = 5500 angle(36.87°) VA.
              En forma rectangular:
              P = 5500 * cos(36.87°) = 5500 * 0.80 = 4,400.0 W = 4.40 kW.
              Q = 5500 * sin(36.87°) = 5500 * 0.60 = + 3,300.0 VAR = + 3.30 kVAR.
              Potencia aparente: |S| = 5,500 VA = 5.50 kVA.
              Factor de potencia: FP = P / |S| = 4400 / 5500 = 0.80 en atraso (inductivo).
              5. Problema Resuelto 2 (Nivel Examen Parcial):
              Una fábrica en la zona industrial de Santa Marta tiene dos cargas en paralelo alimentadas a 440 V RMS a 60 Hz:
              - Carga 1: Motor de inducción que consume P_1 = 40 kW con FP_1 = 0.707 inductivo (en atraso).
              - Carga 2: Horno de resistencia eléctrica pura que consume P_2 = 30 kW con FP_2 = 1.0.
              Aplique el Teorema de Boucherot para determinar: a) La potencia activa total P_total; b) La potencia reactiva total Q_total; c) La potencia aparente combinada |S_total|; d) El factor de potencia global de la planta.
              Solución:
              1. Para Carga 1:
              P_1 = 40 kW.
              Como FP_1 = cos(phi_1) = 0.707 ==> phi_1 = 45.0°.
              Q_1 = P_1 * tan(phi_1) = 40 kW * tan(45°) = 40.0 kVAR.
              S_1 = (40 + j 40) kVA.
              2. Para Carga 2:
              P_2 = 30 kW.
              Como FP_2 = 1.0 ==> phi_2 = 0° ==> Q_2 = 0 kVAR.
              S_2 = (30 + j 0) kVA.
              3. Balance de Boucherot:
              P_total = P_1 + P_2 = 40 + 30 = 70.0 kW.
              Q_total = Q_1 + Q_2 = 40 + 0 = 40.0 kVAR.
              Potencia compleja total: S_total = (70.0 + j 40.0) kVA.
              4. Magnitud aparente total:
              |S_total| = sqrt( (70)^2 + (40)^2 ) = sqrt( 4900 + 1600 ) = sqrt(6500) = 80.62 kVA.
              5. Factor de potencia global:
              FP_global = P_total / |S_total| = 70.0 / 80.62 = 0.8683 en atraso (86.83% inductivo).
            bloque_sugerido: "Laboratorio 50 min • Triángulo de potencias y teorema de Boucherot"
            slides:
              - numero: 1
                seccion: "POTENCIA COMPLEJA"
                titulo: "Definición S = V I*"
                puntos:
                  - "Uso del conjugado de corriente para convención de signo inductivo Q > 0."
                  - "Descomposición rectangular S = P + jQ y magnitud aparente |S| en kVA."
              - numero: 2
                seccion: "BOUCHEROT"
                titulo: "Teorema de Boucherot"
                puntos:
                  - "Conservación independiente de potencia activa P y reactiva Q."
                  - "Cálculo directo de factor de potencia global en redes industriales."
          - numero_tema: 29
            corte: 3
            modalidad: "tecnica"
            titulo: "Compensación y Corrección del Factor de Potencia"
            objetivo: "Dimensionar bancos de condensadores para corregir el factor de potencia a FP >= 0.95 y evitar penalizaciones CREG."
            concepto_clave_latex: "Q_C = P [\\tan(\\theta_1) - \\tan(\\theta_2)] \\quad ; \\quad C = \\frac{Q_C}{\\omega V_{\\text{rms}}^2} \\quad ; \\quad \\text{Penalización CREG: } Q_{\\text{ind}} > 0.5 P"
            ejemplo: |
              CLASE MAGISTRAL: COMPENSACIÓN REACTIVA Y REGULACIÓN CREG 015
              1. Justificación Técnica y Económica de la Compensación:
              Un bajo factor de potencia (FP < 0.90) obliga al operador de red a transportar corrientes elevadas que saturan transformadores y aumentan las pérdidas Joule sin generar trabajo facturable. La regulación colombiana (Resolución CREG 015 de 2018) penaliza severamente el consumo de energía reactiva inductiva cuando supera el 50% de la energía activa (tan phi > 0.5, equivalente a FP < 0.894), y penaliza la inyección de reactiva capacitiva a cualquier nivel horario.
              2. Principio de Compensación en Paralelo:
              Se conectan condensadores en paralelo con la carga. Como el condensador suministra reactivos localmente (Q_C < 0), la red externa sólo tiene que suministrar la diferencia neta reducida Q_2 = Q_1 - Q_C, elevando el factor de potencia a cos(phi_2) >= 0.95 sin alterar la potencia activa P consumida por la maquinaria.
              3. Problema Resuelto 1 (Aplicación Directa):
              Una pequeña industria tiene una carga de P = 120 kW con FP_1 = 0.75 inductivo (tan phi_1 = 0.8819) conectada a V = 220 V RMS a 60 Hz. Se requiere elevar el factor de potencia a FP_2 = 0.95 inductivo (tan phi_2 = 0.3287) para eliminar cobros de energía reactiva en la factura. Calcule la potencia reactiva Q_C del banco de condensadores y la capacitancia total C necesaria.
              Solución:
              Potencia reactiva del banco de condensadores:
              Q_C = P * [ tan(phi_1) - tan(phi_2) ]
              Q_C = 120 kW * [ 0.8819 - 0.3287 ] = 120 * [ 0.5532 ] = 66.384 kVAR.
              Cálculo de la capacitancia C (asumiendo conexión monofásica equivalente a 220 V y omega = 376.99 rad/s):
              Q_C = omega * C * V^2 ==> C = Q_C / (omega * V^2)
              C = 66,384 VAR / [ 376.99 rad/s * (220 V)^2 ]
              C = 66,384 / [ 376.99 * 48,400 ] = 66,384 / 18,246,316 = 3.638 * 10^-3 Faradios = 3,638 uF.
              4. Problema Resuelto 2 (Nivel Examen Parcial):
              Demuestre cuantitativamente el impacto de la compensación anterior sobre: a) La reducción de la corriente demandada a la red; b) La reducción porcentual en las pérdidas Joule I^2 R en la acometida eléctrica de alimentación.
              Solución:
              a) Corriente antes de compensar (FP_1 = 0.75):
              S_1 = P / FP_1 = 120 kW / 0.75 = 160.0 kVA.
              I_1 = S_1 / V = 160,000 VA / 220 V = 727.27 A.
              Corriente después de compensar (FP_2 = 0.95):
              S_2 = P / FP_2 = 120 kW / 0.95 = 126.316 kVA.
              I_2 = S_2 / V = 126,316 VA / 220 V = 574.16 A.
              Reducción de corriente: delta_I = 727.27 - 574.16 = 153.11 A (reducción del 21.05%).
              b) Pérdidas Joule en el conductor de resistencia R:
              Pérdidas antes: P_loss,1 = I_1^2 * R.
              Pérdidas después: P_loss,2 = I_2^2 * R.
              Relación de pérdidas:
              P_loss,2 / P_loss,1 = (I_2 / I_1)^2 = (574.16 / 727.27)^2 = (0.7895)^2 = 0.6233 (62.33%).
              Reducción de pérdidas en la acometida:
              Ahorro = (1 - 0.6233) * 100% = 37.67% de reducción permanente de pérdidas térmicas.
              Se liberaron 33.7 kVA de capacidad en el transformador de distribución y se redujo el calentamiento de cables en más de un tercio.
            bloque_sugerido: "Laboratorio 50 min • Dimensionamiento de banco de condensadores y análisis CREG"
            slides:
              - numero: 1
                seccion: "COMPENSACIÓN"
                titulo: "Corrección de Factor de Potencia"
                puntos:
                  - "Ecuación de dimensionamiento Q_C = P [tan(phi_1) - tan(phi_2)]."
                  - "Suministro local de reactivos sin alterar la potencia activa P de trabajo."
              - numero: 2
                seccion: "BENEFICIOS"
                titulo: "Liberación de Capacidad y CREG 015"
                puntos:
                  - "Reducción de más del 35% en pérdidas Joule de acometidas."
                  - "Eliminación de penalizaciones tarifarias por energía reactiva inductiva."
          - numero_tema: 30
            corte: 3
            modalidad: "tecnica"
            titulo: "Seguridad Eléctrica en DC/AC: Efectos Fisiológicos y Puesta a Tierra"
            objetivo: "Aplicar la norma técnica RETIE e IEC 60479-1 sobre zonas de riesgo eléctrico y dimensionar sistemas de puesta a tierra."
            concepto_clave_latex: "R_{\\text{pat}} \\le 10\\,\\Omega \\quad ; \\quad I_{\\text{body}} = \\frac{V_{\\text{toque}}}{R_{\\text{cuerpo}}} \\quad ; \\quad t_{\\text{disparo}} \\le 30\\,\\text{ms a } 30\\,\\text{mA (RCD)}"
            ejemplo: |
              CLASE MAGISTRAL: SEGURIDAD ELÉCTRICA, EFECTOS BIOLÓGICOS Y RETIE
              1. Efectos Fisiológicos de la Corriente Eléctrica (Norma IEC 60479-1):
              No es el voltaje lo que mata a una persona, sino la intensidad de corriente que atraviesa el cuerpo humano y su duración temporal t:
              - Zona 1 (< 0.5 mA): Imperceptible.
              - Zona 2 (0.5 mA a 10 mA): Umbral de percepción y cosquilleo; sin efectos dañinos.
              - Zona 3 (10 mA a 30 mA): Umbral de no soltar (tetanización muscular); la persona no puede abrir la mano para soltar el cable energizado; dificultad respiratoria.
              - Zona 4 (> 30 mA para t > 0.5 s o > 500 mA instantáneo): Fibrilación ventricular del corazón (descoordinación irreversible del miocardio que detiene el bombeo sanguíneo, mortal en pocos minutos sin desfibrilador).
              2. Tensión de Contacto (Paso y Toque):
              - Resistencia del cuerpo humano: Típicamente considerada en 1000 Ohmios bajo piel húmeda según RETIE.
              - Disyuntores Diferenciales (RCD / GFCI): Detectan corrientes de fuga a tierra desconectando en menos de 30 milisegundos cuando I_fuga >= 30 mA.
              3. Sistemas de Puesta a Tierra (SPT):
              Proporcionan una trayectoria de bajísima impedancia (R_pat <= 10 Ohm en subestaciones y edificios) para disipar corrientes de falla a tierra y descargas de rayos, limitando las tensiones de paso y toque a niveles no letales.
              4. Problema Resuelto 1 (Aplicación Directa):
              Una persona con piel húmeda y pies descalzos (resistencia total equivalente R_cuerpo = 1,000 Ohm) toca accidentalmente la carcasa metálica no conectada a tierra de una bomba que presenta una falla de aislamiento a V = 120 V AC. Calcule la corriente que atraviesa el cuerpo, clasifique la zona de riesgo según IEC 60479 y dictamine si existe peligro mortal.
              Solución:
              Corriente a través del cuerpo:
              I_cuerpo = V / R_cuerpo = 120 V / 1,000 Ohm = 0.120 A = 120.0 mA.
              Clasificación de riesgo:
              120 mA supera con creces el umbral de tetanización muscular (10-30 mA) y penetra directamente en la Zona 4 de Fibrilación Ventricular (para t > 100 ms).
              Dictamen de seguridad:
              Peligro mortal inminente por paro cardíaco en menos de 1 segundo si el circuito no cuenta con un interruptor diferencial RCD de 30 mA.
              5. Problema Resuelto 2 (Nivel Examen Parcial):
              En la instalación anterior, se conecta la carcasa metálica de la bomba a un Sistema de Puesta a Tierra con resistencia R_pat = 5.0 Ohm. El circuito está protegido por un interruptor termomagnético de 20 A y aguas arriba por un interruptor diferencial RCD de 30 mA.
              a) Cuando ocurre el contacto a masa de 120 V, calcule la corriente de falla a tierra que circula por el electrodo.
              b) Calcule la tensión de contacto residual V_toque que aparece en la carcasa.
              c) Determine la corriente residual que atravesaría a una persona de 1,000 Ohm que toque la carcasa en ese instante antes de que dispare la protección.
              Solución:
              a) Corriente de falla franca a tierra:
              I_falla = V / R_pat = 120 V / 5.0 Ohm = 24.0 A.
              (Como 24 A > 30 mA, el interruptor diferencial RCD detecta el desbalance instantáneamente y abre el circuito en menos de 25 milisegundos).
              b) Tensión de contacto en la carcasa metálica durante los 25 ms de falla:
              V_toque = I_falla * R_pat... ¡pero la carcasa está al potencial del divisor de tierra!
              Considerando impedancia de la fuente despreciable frente a R_pat: la tensión es V_toque = 120 V si no hay retorno metálico, o si hay conductor de protección PE de R_PE = 0.5 Ohm: V_toque = 120 * (R_pat / (R_fase + R_pat)).
              En el peor caso sin conductor neutro de retorno: V_toque = 120 V.
              c) Corriente que derivaría por la persona:
              Como el cuerpo (1000 Ohm) está en paralelo con la puesta a tierra (5 Ohm):
              Por divisor de corriente:
              I_persona = I_falla * [ R_pat / (R_cuerpo + R_pat) ] = 24.0 A * [ 5 / (1000 + 5) ] = 24.0 * (5 / 1005) = 0.119 A.
              Sin embargo, el diferencial RCD corta en 20 ms.
              Según la curva de la IEC 60479, para t = 20 ms, el umbral de fibrilación ventricular exige más de 500 mA. Por lo tanto, 119 mA durante 20 ms se ubica en la Zona 2 segura (shock perceptible pero sin daño biológico permanente), salvando la vida del operador.
            bloque_sugerido: "Laboratorio 50 min • Curvas de disparo RCD y resistencia de puesta a tierra"
            slides:
              - numero: 1
                seccion: "RETIE"
                titulo: "Efectos Fisiológicos de la Corriente"
                puntos:
                  - "Curvas IEC 60479-1: umbral de no soltar (10-30 mA) y fibrilación (>50 mA)."
                  - "Resistencia del cuerpo humano normalizada en 1000 Ohmios bajo humedad."
              - numero: 2
                seccion: "PROTECCIÓN"
                titulo: "Puesta a Tierra y Disyuntor RCD"
                puntos:
                  - "Disyuntores diferenciales de 30 mA con tiempo de corte < 30 ms."
                  - "Resistencia de puesta a tierra R_pat <= 10 Ohm según reglamento RETIE."
      - codigo: "01021803"
        nombre: "General English II"
        creditos: 2
        obligatoria: true
        categoria: "FORMACION_GENERAL"
        color: "#8E8E93"
        temas:
          - numero_tema: 1
            corte: 1
            modalidad: "general"
            titulo: "Past Simple: Regular & Irregular Verbs in Historical Events"
            objetivo: "Narrar hitos históricos de la ciencia y eventos completados en el pasado usando verbos regulares e irregulares."
            concepto_clave_latex: ""
            ejemplo: "In 1954, Bell Labs demonstrated the first practical silicon solar cell."
            bloque_sugerido: "Timeline Reading 40 min • Milestones in electrical & thermal engineering"
            slides:
              - numero: 1
                seccion: "CEFR A2 • CORE CONCEPT"
                titulo: "Past Simple: Regular & Irregular Verbs in Historical Events: Communicative Purpose"
                puntos:
                  - "Use Past Simple for completed actions at a definite past time (in 1882, yesterday, last semester, two days ago)."
                  - "Regular verbs add -ed (invented, discovered, studied); irregular verbs change stem (built, wrote, went, found)."
                  - "Past of To Be uses 'was' (I/he/she/it) and 'were' (you/we/they) without 'did'."
                ejemplo: "In 1954, Bell Labs demonstrated the first practical silicon solar cell."
              - numero: 2
                seccion: "STRUCTURE & PATTERNS"
                titulo: "Core Grammatical Blueprint"
                puntos:
                  - "Affirmative: Subject + V2 (past form) — identical for all persons!"
                  - "-ed pronunciation: /t/ after voiceless (worked), /d/ after voiced (measured), /ɪd/ after t/d (tested, started)."
                  - "Past of Be: 'Tesla was an inventor; his patents were revolutionary.'"
                tabla:
                  - ["Verb Type", "Base -> Past", "-ed Sound / Note"]
                  - ["Regular (/t/, /d/)", "develop -> developed", "No extra syllable (/t/)"]
                  - ["Regular (/ɪd/)", "connect -> connected", "Extra syllable after t/d"]
                  - ["Irregular", "build -> built, rise -> rose", "Memorize stem change"]
              - numero: 3
                seccion: "QUESTIONS & NEGATION"
                titulo: "Interrogative, Negative & Short Answers"
                puntos:
                  - "Negative: Subject + did not (didn't) + BASE verb ('Edison didn't champion AC transmission')."
                  - "Questions: Did + subject + BASE verb? / Wh- + did + subject + BASE verb?"
                  - "With Was/Were: 'Were the measurements accurate? Yes, they were.'"
                ejemplo: "Last week, our team calibrated the pyranometer on the rooftop."
              - numero: 4
                seccion: "PRECISION & CONTRAST"
                titulo: "Key Distinctions & Common Pitfalls"
                puntos:
                  - "Never keep past form after 'did/didn't': say 'Did you finish?', NOT 'Did you finished?'."
                  - "Do not mix 'was/were' with 'did': say 'Were you in class?', NOT 'Did you were in class?'."
                tabla:
                  - ["Incorrect", "Correct", "Rule"]
                  - ["We didn't went", "We didn't go", "Base verb after didn't"]
                  - ["He was graduated in 2024", "He graduated in 2024", "Active Past Simple"]
              - numero: 5
                seccion: "CAMPUS & LAB CONTEXT"
                titulo: "Authentic Academic & Engineering Usage"
                puntos:
                  - "In 1954, Bell Labs demonstrated the first practical silicon solar cell."
                  - "Last week, our team calibrated the pyranometer on the rooftop."
                  - "Did Faraday discover electromagnetic induction in 1831? Yes, he did."
                ejemplo: "Academic Register (CEFR A2): Clear, concise communication in Unimagdalena seminars."
              - numero: 6
                seccion: "MASTERY CHECK"
                titulo: "Self-Assessment & Oral Drill"
                puntos:
                  - "Pronounce -ed: 'measured (/d/), calculated (/ɪd/), switched (/t/)'."
                  - "Rewrite in negative: 'The voltage dropped' -> 'The voltage didn't drop.'"
                  - "Write a 5-sentence timeline of an energy pioneer."
                ejemplo: "Practice reading each model sentence aloud with natural stress and intonation."
          - numero_tema: 2
            corte: 1
            modalidad: "general"
            titulo: "Past Continuous vs. Past Simple (While & When Clauses)"
            objetivo: "Combinar acciones pasadas en desarrollo con eventos puntuales que las interrumpieron."
            concepto_clave_latex: ""
            ejemplo: "While the technician was inspecting the transformer, it started to rain."
            bloque_sugerido: "Narrative Drill 40 min • Reporting past lab procedures & interruptions"
            slides:
              - numero: 1
                seccion: "CEFR A2 • CORE CONCEPT"
                titulo: "Past Continuous vs. Past Simple (While & When Clauses): Communicative Purpose"
                puntos:
                  - "Past Continuous (was / were + verb-ing) sets the background action in progress at a specific past moment."
                  - "Past Simple (V2) expresses the shorter interrupting event or sequential action."
                  - "Use 'while' / 'as' before Past Continuous, and 'when' typically before Past Simple."
                ejemplo: "While the technician was inspecting the transformer, it started to rain."
              - numero: 2
                seccion: "STRUCTURE & PATTERNS"
                titulo: "Core Grammatical Blueprint"
                puntos:
                  - "Interrupting pattern: 'While we were logging data, the breaker tripped.'"
                  - "Parallel background actions: 'While I was wiring the sensor, Ana was testing the code.'"
                  - "Comma rule: put a comma when the When/While clause comes first."
                tabla:
                  - ["Connector", "Typical Clause", "Example"]
                  - ["While + Past Cont.", "Long action in progress", "While the rotor was spinning..."]
                  - ["When + Past Simple", "Sudden interruption", "...when the alarm sounded."]
              - numero: 3
                seccion: "QUESTIONS & NEGATION"
                titulo: "Interrogative, Negative & Short Answers"
                puntos:
                  - "Negative: 'The generator wasn't running at midnight.'"
                  - "Questions: 'What were you doing when the power went out?'"
                  - "Sequential Past Simple (cause -> effect): 'When I pressed Start, the pump turned on' (one after another)."
                ejemplo: "What parameters were you monitoring when the voltage spike occurred?"
              - numero: 4
                seccion: "PRECISION & CONTRAST"
                titulo: "Key Distinctions & Common Pitfalls"
                puntos:
                  - "Avoid using Past Continuous for stative verbs: 'I knew the answer', NOT 'I was knowing'."
                  - "Match subject agreement: 'you/we/they WERE', 'I/he/she/it WAS'."
                tabla:
                  - ["Meaning", "Sentence", "Timeline"]
                  - ["Already in progress", "When I arrived, they were testing.", "Testing started BEFORE arrival"]
                  - ["Happened next", "When I arrived, they started testing.", "Testing started AFTER arrival"]
              - numero: 5
                seccion: "CAMPUS & LAB CONTEXT"
                titulo: "Authentic Academic & Engineering Usage"
                puntos:
                  - "While the technician was inspecting the transformer, it started to rain."
                  - "What parameters were you monitoring when the voltage spike occurred?"
                  - "At 10:30 a.m. yesterday, we were running a simulation in MATLAB."
                ejemplo: "Academic Register (CEFR A2): Clear, concise communication in Unimagdalena seminars."
              - numero: 6
                seccion: "MASTERY CHECK"
                titulo: "Self-Assessment & Oral Drill"
                puntos:
                  - "Combine with 'while': 'We / record temperature — the sensor / disconnect'."
                  - "Choose: 'When the bell rang, we (wrote / were writing) our conclusion.'"
                  - "Report a laboratory incident in 4 connected sentences."
                ejemplo: "Practice reading each model sentence aloud with natural stress and intonation."
          - numero_tema: 3
            corte: 1
            modalidad: "general"
            titulo: "Countable & Uncountable Nouns (Much, Many, A lot of, Few, Little)"
            objetivo: "Cuantificar recursos, materiales, energía, datos y equipos diferenciando sustantivos contables e incontables."
            concepto_clave_latex: ""
            ejemplo: "How much electricity does the university campus consume per month?"
            bloque_sugerido: "Quantifier Practice 35 min • Resource & energy consumption descriptions"
            slides:
              - numero: 1
                seccion: "CEFR A2 • CORE CONCEPT"
                titulo: "Countable & Uncountable Nouns (Much, Many, A lot of, Few, Little): Communicative Purpose"
                puntos:
                  - "Countable nouns have singular & plural forms (turbines, batteries, watts, hours)."
                  - "Uncountable nouns represent mass, abstract concepts, or liquids/gases (energy, electricity, equipment, information, research, water) -> ALWAYS singular verb!"
                  - "Quantifiers depend on countability: many / (a) few for countable; much / (a) little for uncountable."
                ejemplo: "How much electricity does the university campus consume per month?"
              - numero: 2
                seccion: "STRUCTURE & PATTERNS"
                titulo: "Core Grammatical Blueprint"
                puntos:
                  - "Large quantity: 'a lot of / plenty of' work with BOTH countable and uncountable nouns."
                  - "Questions & negatives: 'How many cells...?' vs. 'How much power...?'"
                  - "Nuance: 'a few / a little' = positive (some, enough); 'few / little' = negative (almost none)."
                tabla:
                  - ["Category", "Countable Plural", "Uncountable Singular"]
                  - ["Large amount", "many / a lot of panels", "much / a lot of heat"]
                  - ["Small (sufficient)", "a few samples", "a little coolant"]
                  - ["Almost zero", "very few errors", "very little friction"]
              - numero: 3
                seccion: "QUESTIONS & NEGATION"
                titulo: "Interrogative, Negative & Short Answers"
                puntos:
                  - "Count uncountable concepts using measure words: 'a piece of equipment', 'two liters of biodiesel', 'three megawatts of power'."
                  - "Watch out: 'data' and 'media' are treated as uncountable or plural in academic English, while 'information', 'advice', 'hardware', 'software' are strictly uncountable!"
                ejemplo: "We have a few spare fuses, so we can continue the experiment."
              - numero: 4
                seccion: "PRECISION & CONTRAST"
                titulo: "Key Distinctions & Common Pitfalls"
                puntos:
                  - "Never pluralize 'informations', 'equipments', or 'researches'!"
                  - "Say 'How much energy is lost?', NOT 'How many energy are lost?'."
                tabla:
                  - ["Spanish Plural", "Incorrect English", "Correct Academic English"]
                  - ["equipos", "three equipments", "three pieces of equipment"]
                  - ["investigaciones", "many researches", "extensive research / studies"]
              - numero: 5
                seccion: "CAMPUS & LAB CONTEXT"
                titulo: "Authentic Academic & Engineering Usage"
                puntos:
                  - "How much electricity does the university campus consume per month?"
                  - "We have a few spare fuses, so we can continue the experiment."
                  - "Modern LED systems waste very little energy as heat."
                ejemplo: "Academic Register (CEFR A2): Clear, concise communication in Unimagdalena seminars."
              - numero: 6
                seccion: "MASTERY CHECK"
                titulo: "Self-Assessment & Oral Drill"
                puntos:
                  - "Choose: 'How (much / many) current flows through R1?' -> 'much'."
                  - "Contrast: 'few students passed' vs. 'a few students passed'."
                  - "Classify 10 engineering nouns as countable or uncountable."
                ejemplo: "Practice reading each model sentence aloud with natural stress and intonation."
          - numero_tema: 4
            corte: 2
            modalidad: "general"
            titulo: "Comparative Adjectives: Comparing Performance & Qualities"
            objetivo: "Comparar el desempeño, costo y eficiencia de tecnologías utilizando adjetivos comparativos y modificadores."
            concepto_clave_latex: ""
            ejemplo: "Monocrystalline panels are slightly more efficient than polycrystalline ones."
            bloque_sugerido: "Benchmarking Drill 40 min • Comparing two renewable energy technologies"
            slides:
              - numero: 1
                seccion: "CEFR A2 • CORE CONCEPT"
                titulo: "Comparative Adjectives: Comparing Performance & Qualities: Communicative Purpose"
                puntos:
                  - "Short adjectives (1 syllable, or 2 ending in -y): add -er + than (cheaper, hotter, noisier)."
                  - "Long adjectives (2+ syllables): more / less + adjective + than (more efficient, less expensive)."
                  - "Irregular comparatives: good -> better, bad -> worse, far -> farther / further."
                ejemplo: "Monocrystalline panels are slightly more efficient than polycrystalline ones."
              - numero: 2
                seccion: "STRUCTURE & PATTERNS"
                titulo: "Core Grammatical Blueprint"
                puntos:
                  - "CVC doubling: big -> bigger, hot -> hotter, thin -> thinner."
                  - "-y -> -ier: heavy -> heavier, easy -> easier."
                  - "Degree modifiers before comparatives: 'much / far / significantly' (big gap) vs. 'slightly / a bit' (small gap)."
                tabla:
                  - ["Adjective Type", "Base", "Comparative Form"]
                  - ["1-syllable", "fast / hot", "faster than / hotter than"]
                  - ["2-syllable (-y)", "heavy / reliable", "heavier / more reliable"]
                  - ["Irregular", "good / bad / far", "better / worse / further"]
              - numero: 3
                seccion: "QUESTIONS & NEGATION"
                titulo: "Interrogative, Negative & Short Answers"
                puntos:
                  - "Double comparatives for trends: 'Solar modules are becoming cheaper and more efficient.'"
                  - "Proportional correlation ('The... the...'): 'The higher the temperature, the lower the open-circuit voltage.'"
                ejemplo: "Offshore winds are stronger and more consistent than onshore winds."
              - numero: 4
                seccion: "PRECISION & CONTRAST"
                titulo: "Key Distinctions & Common Pitfalls"
                puntos:
                  - "Never combine 'more' + '-er': say 'better' or 'faster', NOT 'more better' or 'more faster'."
                  - "Always use 'than' (with 'a'), NOT 'then' (time sequence) or 'that'."
                tabla:
                  - ["Modifier", "Gap Size", "Technical Comparison"]
                  - ["much / significantly", "Large difference", "Li-ion is significantly lighter than lead-acid."]
                  - ["slightly / marginally", "Small difference", "Prototype B is slightly quieter than A."]
              - numero: 5
                seccion: "CAMPUS & LAB CONTEXT"
                titulo: "Authentic Academic & Engineering Usage"
                puntos:
                  - "Monocrystalline panels are slightly more efficient than polycrystalline ones."
                  - "Offshore winds are stronger and more consistent than onshore winds."
                  - "The higher the wind speed, the greater the power output."
                ejemplo: "Academic Register (CEFR A2): Clear, concise communication in Unimagdalena seminars."
              - numero: 6
                seccion: "MASTERY CHECK"
                titulo: "Self-Assessment & Oral Drill"
                puntos:
                  - "Compare: 'LED bulbs / incandescent bulbs (efficient & durable)'."
                  - "Fix: 'Copper is more cheaper that silver' -> 'Copper is cheaper than silver.'"
                  - "Write 3 'The..., the...' engineering relationships."
                ejemplo: "Practice reading each model sentence aloud with natural stress and intonation."
          - numero_tema: 5
            corte: 2
            modalidad: "general"
            titulo: "Superlative Adjectives & Equatives (As... as)"
            objetivo: "Destacar valores extremos y expresar igualdad o proporción entre alternativas técnicas."
            concepto_clave_latex: ""
            ejemplo: "La Guajira has some of the highest wind speeds in South America."
            bloque_sugerido: "Comparison Matrix 35 min • Ranking 4 energy storage systems"
            slides:
              - numero: 1
                seccion: "CEFR A2 • CORE CONCEPT"
                titulo: "Superlative Adjectives & Equatives (As... as): Communicative Purpose"
                puntos:
                  - "Superlatives compare 3 or more items: 'the + -est' (the fastest) or 'the most / the least + adjective' (the most sustainable)."
                  - "Irregular superlatives: the best, the worst, the farthest/furthest."
                  - "Equatives ('as + adjective/adverb + as') express equality or ratio ('twice as fast as')."
                ejemplo: "La Guajira has some of the highest wind speeds in South America."
              - numero: 2
                seccion: "STRUCTURE & PATTERNS"
                titulo: "Core Grammatical Blueprint"
                puntos:
                  - "Preposition after superlatives: use 'IN' for places/groups ('the largest plant in Colombia') and 'OF' for time/sets ('the hottest day of the year')."
                  - "Negative equative: 'not as (so) expensive as' = cheaper than."
                  - "Multipliers: 'three times as powerful as', 'half as heavy as'."
                tabla:
                  - ["Structure", "Formula", "Example"]
                  - ["Superlative (short)", "the + adj-est", "the highest voltage in the grid"]
                  - ["Superlative (long)", "the most/least + adj", "the most reliable inverter"]
                  - ["Equative", "(not) as + adj + as", "not as noisy as a diesel genset"]
              - numero: 3
                seccion: "QUESTIONS & NEGATION"
                titulo: "Interrogative, Negative & Short Answers"
                puntos:
                  - "Pair superlatives with Present Perfect: 'This is the most accurate model we have ever built.'"
                  - "Use 'one of the + superlative + PLURAL noun': 'one of the sunniest regions in the country'."
                ejemplo: "Hydrogen has the highest gravimetric energy density of common fuels."
              - numero: 4
                seccion: "PRECISION & CONTRAST"
                titulo: "Key Distinctions & Common Pitfalls"
                puntos:
                  - "Never forget 'the' (or a possessive) before a superlative: 'the lowest cost'."
                  - "Use 'in' (NOT 'of') before singular places: 'in Latin America', NOT 'of Latin America'."
                tabla:
                  - ["Equative Multiplier", "Equivalent Meaning", "Example"]
                  - ["as efficient as", "Equal performance", "Unit A is as efficient as Unit B."]
                  - ["twice as large as", "2x capacity", "The new battery bank is twice as large as the old one."]
              - numero: 5
                seccion: "CAMPUS & LAB CONTEXT"
                titulo: "Authentic Academic & Engineering Usage"
                puntos:
                  - "La Guajira has some of the highest wind speeds in South America."
                  - "Hydrogen has the highest gravimetric energy density of common fuels."
                  - "Biomass gasification is not as widespread as solar PV on campus."
                ejemplo: "Academic Register (CEFR A2): Clear, concise communication in Unimagdalena seminars."
              - numero: 6
                seccion: "MASTERY CHECK"
                titulo: "Self-Assessment & Oral Drill"
                puntos:
                  - "Rewrite using 'not as... as': 'Lead-acid is heavier than lithium' -> 'Lithium isn't as heavy as lead-acid.'"
                  - "Complete: 'One of the most important ___ (factor -> factors) in design.'"
                  - "Write 3 superlatives about Colombian energy geography."
                ejemplo: "Practice reading each model sentence aloud with natural stress and intonation."
          - numero_tema: 6
            corte: 2
            modalidad: "general"
            titulo: "Future with Be Going To for Plans & Intentions"
            objetivo: "Expresar planes definidos de estudio, proyectos futuros y predicciones basadas en evidencia visible."
            concepto_clave_latex: ""
            ejemplo: "Next semester, we are going to take Thermodynamics and Linear Algebra."
            bloque_sugerido: "Project Planning 35 min • Outlining next-week experimental roadmap"
            slides:
              - numero: 1
                seccion: "CEFR A2 • CORE CONCEPT"
                titulo: "Future with Be Going To for Plans & Intentions: Communicative Purpose"
                puntos:
                  - "Form: am / is / are + going to + base verb."
                  - "Use 1 (Prior Intention/Plan): decisions already made before speaking ('We are going to build a solar tracker')."
                  - "Use 2 (Evidence-Based Prediction): present clues show what is imminent ('Look at the dark clouds — irradiance is going to drop')."
                ejemplo: "Next semester, we are going to take Thermodynamics and Linear Algebra."
              - numero: 2
                seccion: "STRUCTURE & PATTERNS"
                titulo: "Core Grammatical Blueprint"
                puntos:
                  - "Affirmative: 'I am going to specialize in smart grids.'"
                  - "Negative: 'They aren't going to replace the transformer this month.'"
                  - "Question: 'What are you going to present at the symposium?'"
                tabla:
                  - ["Use Case", "Context Clue", "Example"]
                  - ["Prior Plan", "Decided earlier", "We're going to test the circuit tomorrow."]
                  - ["Visible Evidence", "Current sensor/sky", "The motor is at 98°C; it's going to overheat!"]
              - numero: 3
                seccion: "QUESTIONS & NEGATION"
                titulo: "Interrogative, Negative & Short Answers"
                puntos:
                  - "Present Continuous can also express fixed arrangements with time/place: 'We are meeting our advisor at 3:00 p.m.'"
                  - "Avoid 'going to go': native speakers prefer 'We're going to the lab after lunch'."
                ejemplo: "Look at the battery monitor — it's at 4%, so it's going to shut down soon."
              - numero: 4
                seccion: "PRECISION & CONTRAST"
                titulo: "Key Distinctions & Common Pitfalls"
                puntos:
                  - "Never omit 'am/is/are': say 'She is going to present', NOT 'She going to present'."
                  - "Use formal 'going to' in academic writing (avoid casual spoken 'gonna' in essays)."
                tabla:
                  - ["Spoken Informal", "Academic Written", "Register Note"]
                  - ["We're gonna test", "We are going to test", "Never write 'gonna' in reports"]
                  - ["Are you gonna...?", "Are you going to...?", "Keep full spelling in slides"]
              - numero: 5
                seccion: "CAMPUS & LAB CONTEXT"
                titulo: "Authentic Academic & Engineering Usage"
                puntos:
                  - "Next semester, we are going to take Thermodynamics and Linear Algebra."
                  - "Look at the battery monitor — it's at 4%, so it's going to shut down soon."
                  - "Are you going to join the renewable energy seedbed (semillero) this term?"
                ejemplo: "Academic Register (CEFR A2): Clear, concise communication in Unimagdalena seminars."
              - numero: 6
                seccion: "MASTERY CHECK"
                titulo: "Self-Assessment & Oral Drill"
                puntos:
                  - "Write 3 academic plans for next cuatrimestre using 'be going to'."
                  - "Make 2 predictions from visible lab readings ('Voltage is rising fast...')."
                  - "Ask a partner 3 questions about their weekend study plan."
                ejemplo: "Practice reading each model sentence aloud with natural stress and intonation."
          - numero_tema: 7
            corte: 2
            modalidad: "general"
            titulo: "Future with Will / Won't for Predictions & Spontaneous Decisions"
            objetivo: "Formular predicciones tecnológicas, promesas, ofrecimientos y decisiones instantáneas con Will y Won't."
            concepto_clave_latex: ""
            ejemplo: "By 2035, renewable energy will supply a major share of regional electricity."
            bloque_sugerido: "Forecast Workshop 35 min • Energy transition predictions vs. instant lab actions"
            slides:
              - numero: 1
                seccion: "CEFR A2 • CORE CONCEPT"
                titulo: "Future with Will / Won't for Predictions & Spontaneous Decisions: Communicative Purpose"
                puntos:
                  - "Form: will ('ll) / will not (won't) + base verb (invariable for all subjects)."
                  - "Use 'will' for: (1) instant decisions made while speaking, (2) offers & promises, (3) general predictions/forecasts (often with think, expect, probably)."
                  - "Contrast: 'will' = spontaneous or opinion-based vs. 'be going to' = pre-planned or visible evidence."
                ejemplo: "By 2035, renewable energy will supply a major share of regional electricity."
              - numero: 2
                seccion: "STRUCTURE & PATTERNS"
                titulo: "Core Grammatical Blueprint"
                puntos:
                  - "Adverb placement: 'Solar storage will probably dominate microgrids' (before 'won't': 'probably won't')."
                  - "Spontaneous decision: 'The projector isn't on — I'll connect the HDMI cable.'"
                  - "Forecast verbs: 'Experts predict / expect / believe that demand will grow.'"
                tabla:
                  - ["Trigger", "Best Form", "Example"]
                  - ["Spontaneous offer", "Will ('ll)", "That box looks heavy. I'll help you."]
                  - ["Prior schedule/plan", "Be going to", "I'm going to study with Luis at 5:00."]
                  - ["Long-term forecast", "Will + adverb", "Green hydrogen will likely scale rapidly."]
              - numero: 3
                seccion: "QUESTIONS & NEGATION"
                titulo: "Interrogative, Negative & Short Answers"
                puntos:
                  - "Questions: 'Will electric vehicles stabilize grid demand?' -> 'Yes, they will / No, they won't.'"
                  - "Polite requests & offers: 'Will you pass me the probe?' / 'Shall we start the simulation?'"
                ejemplo: "Don't worry about the spreadsheet — I'll double-check the formulas right now."
              - numero: 4
                seccion: "PRECISION & CONTRAST"
                titulo: "Key Distinctions & Common Pitfalls"
                puntos:
                  - "Do not use 'will' after time conjunctions (when, as soon as, before, after, until): say 'I'll call you when the test finishes' (Present Simple!)."
                  - "Never add 'to' after will: 'will increase', NOT 'will to increase'."
                tabla:
                  - ["Time Clause Rule", "Incorrect", "Correct"]
                  - ["when / as soon as", "When it will reach 60 Hz...", "When it reaches 60 Hz, we will sync."]
                  - ["after / before", "Before I will submit...", "Before I submit, I'll check the PDF."]
              - numero: 5
                seccion: "CAMPUS & LAB CONTEXT"
                titulo: "Authentic Academic & Engineering Usage"
                puntos:
                  - "By 2035, renewable energy will supply a major share of regional electricity."
                  - "Don't worry about the spreadsheet — I'll double-check the formulas right now."
                  - "As soon as the sensor stabilizes, we will record the baseline."
                ejemplo: "Academic Register (CEFR A2): Clear, concise communication in Unimagdalena seminars."
              - numero: 6
                seccion: "MASTERY CHECK"
                titulo: "Self-Assessment & Oral Drill"
                puntos:
                  - "Choose: 'A: We're out of graph paper. B: Oh! I (will / am going to) get some.' -> 'will'."
                  - "Fix: 'When the class will end, we'll eat' -> 'When the class ends, we'll eat.'"
                  - "Write 3 forecasts for Colombia's energy sector."
                ejemplo: "Practice reading each model sentence aloud with natural stress and intonation."
          - numero_tema: 8
            corte: 3
            modalidad: "general"
            titulo: "Modal Verbs of Obligation & Advice (Must, Have to, Should, Ought to)"
            objetivo: "Distinguir entre obligación interna/externa, prohibición, ausencia de necesidad y recomendaciones técnicas."
            concepto_clave_latex: ""
            ejemplo: "Engineers must comply with RETIE electrical safety standards in Colombia."
            bloque_sugerido: "Compliance Briefing 35 min • Safety regulations vs. optional best practices"
            slides:
              - numero: 1
                seccion: "CEFR A2 • CORE CONCEPT"
                titulo: "Modal Verbs of Obligation & Advice (Must, Have to, Should, Ought to): Communicative Purpose"
                puntos:
                  - "Strong obligation: 'must' (rules, safety notices, speaker's authority) & 'have to / has to' (external regulations, institutional requirements)."
                  - "CRITICAL NEGATIVE CONTRAST: 'mustn't' = PROHIBITED! vs. 'don't/doesn't have to' = NOT NECESSARY (optional)."
                  - "Advice & best practices: 'should / shouldn't' and 'ought to' + base verb."
                ejemplo: "Engineers must comply with RETIE electrical safety standards in Colombia."
              - numero: 2
                seccion: "STRUCTURE & PATTERNS"
                titulo: "Core Grammatical Blueprint"
                puntos:
                  - "Affirmative: 'All visitors must wear insulated boots.' / 'Students have to pass 162 credits.'"
                  - "Prohibition: 'You must not bypass the circuit breaker.'"
                  - "No obligation: 'You don't have to print the report; digital PDF is fine.'"
                tabla:
                  - ["Modal", "Meaning", "Lab / Campus Example"]
                  - ["must / have to", "100% Mandatory", "You must ground the chassis."]
                  - ["mustn't", "Strictly Forbidden", "You mustn't open live panels."]
                  - ["don't have to", "Optional", "You don't have to memorize constants."]
                  - ["should / shouldn't", "Recommendation", "You should save backups hourly."]
              - numero: 3
                seccion: "QUESTIONS & NEGATION"
                titulo: "Interrogative, Negative & Short Answers"
                puntos:
                  - "Questions of obligation usually prefer 'Do we have to...?' ('Do we have to wear lab coats today?')."
                  - "Past obligation uses 'had to' (since 'must' has no past form for obligation: 'Yesterday we had to recalibrate twice')."
                ejemplo: "You don't have to bring your own oscilloscope; the lab provides them."
              - numero: 4
                seccion: "PRECISION & CONTRAST"
                titulo: "Key Distinctions & Common Pitfalls"
                puntos:
                  - "Spanish speakers often confuse 'don't have to' with prohibition -> remember 'mustn't' = forbidden!"
                  - "'Have to' takes do/does in negatives and questions; 'must' and 'should' never use do/does."
                tabla:
                  - ["Situation", "Wrong Choice", "Accurate Modal"]
                  - ["Prohibido tocar", "You don't have to touch", "You mustn't touch"]
                  - ["Opcional asistir", "You mustn't attend", "You don't have to attend"]
              - numero: 5
                seccion: "CAMPUS & LAB CONTEXT"
                titulo: "Authentic Academic & Engineering Usage"
                puntos:
                  - "Engineers must comply with RETIE electrical safety standards in Colombia."
                  - "You don't have to bring your own oscilloscope; the lab provides them."
                  - "We should insulate the steam pipe to reduce thermal losses."
                ejemplo: "Academic Register (CEFR A2): Clear, concise communication in Unimagdalena seminars."
              - numero: 6
                seccion: "MASTERY CHECK"
                titulo: "Self-Assessment & Oral Drill"
                puntos:
                  - "Choose: 'Entry is free; you (mustn't / don't have to) pay' -> 'don't have to'."
                  - "Past form: 'We must repeat the test yesterday' -> 'We had to repeat the test yesterday.'"
                  - "Write 4 technical recommendations using should/must/mustn't."
                ejemplo: "Practice reading each model sentence aloud with natural stress and intonation."
          - numero_tema: 9
            corte: 3
            modalidad: "general"
            titulo: "Present Perfect Simple: Life Experiences (Ever, Never, Already, Yet)"
            objetivo: "Conectar experiencias académicas pasadas con el presente mediante el Presente Perfecto y marcadores clave."
            concepto_clave_latex: ""
            ejemplo: "Have you ever designed a circuit on a breadboard? Yes, several times."
            bloque_sugerido: "Experience Log 40 min • Academic portfolio milestones with Present Perfect"
            slides:
              - numero: 1
                seccion: "CEFR A2 • CORE CONCEPT"
                titulo: "Present Perfect Simple: Life Experiences (Ever, Never, Already, Yet): Communicative Purpose"
                puntos:
                  - "Form: have / has + Past Participle (V3: worked, measured / built, written, been, gone)."
                  - "Use Present Perfect for: (1) life experiences at an unspecified time (ever / never), (2) recent achievements with present relevance (just, already, yet)."
                  - "Never pair Present Perfect with finished past dates (*yesterday, in 2022*)!"
                ejemplo: "Have you ever designed a circuit on a breadboard? Yes, several times."
              - numero: 2
                seccion: "STRUCTURE & PATTERNS"
                titulo: "Core Grammatical Blueprint"
                puntos:
                  - "'Already' (sooner than expected): mid-position in affirmative ('We have already submitted the lab')."
                  - "'Yet' (up to now): end of negatives & questions ('Have you checked the results yet? No, not yet')."
                  - "'Just' (moments ago): 'The simulation has just converged.'"
                tabla:
                  - ["Adverb", "Clause Type", "Position & Example"]
                  - ["ever / never", "Question / Affirmative", "Have you ever visited a wind farm?"]
                  - ["just / already", "Affirmative", "She has already finished Topic 9."]
                  - ["yet", "Negative & Question", "We haven't tested the inverter yet."]
              - numero: 3
                seccion: "QUESTIONS & NEGATION"
                titulo: "Interrogative, Negative & Short Answers"
                puntos:
                  - "'Have been to' vs. 'Have gone to': 'Ana has been to Ituango' (visited and returned) vs. 'Ana has gone to the lab' (she is still there now!)."
                  - "Follow up an 'ever' experience with Past Simple details: 'Have you ever used PVsyst? Yes, I have. I used it last month.'"
                ejemplo: "Our team has already collected 500 irradiance samples, but we haven't plotted them yet."
              - numero: 4
                seccion: "PRECISION & CONTRAST"
                titulo: "Key Distinctions & Common Pitfalls"
                puntos:
                  - "Do not use Present Simple for 'yet/already': 'I have already eaten', NOT 'I already eat' in formal British/academic English."
                  - "Memorize key V3 forms: write -> written, see -> seen, do -> done, run -> run, choose -> chosen."
                tabla:
                  - ["Verb", "Past Simple (V2)", "Past Participle (V3)"]
                  - ["write / take", "wrote / took", "written / taken"]
                  - ["go / be", "went / was-were", "gone / been"]
                  - ["rise / fall", "rose / fell", "risen / fallen"]
              - numero: 5
                seccion: "CAMPUS & LAB CONTEXT"
                titulo: "Authentic Academic & Engineering Usage"
                puntos:
                  - "Have you ever designed a circuit on a breadboard? Yes, several times."
                  - "Our team has already collected 500 irradiance samples, but we haven't plotted them yet."
                  - "Solar installations on the Caribbean coast have grown rapidly."
                ejemplo: "Academic Register (CEFR A2): Clear, concise communication in Unimagdalena seminars."
              - numero: 6
                seccion: "MASTERY CHECK"
                titulo: "Self-Assessment & Oral Drill"
                puntos:
                  - "Insert 'yet' or 'already': 'Has the lecture started ___?' -> 'yet'."
                  - "Contrast: 'He has been to Bogotá' vs. 'He has gone to Bogotá'."
                  - "Write 3 academic achievements you have completed so far."
                ejemplo: "Practice reading each model sentence aloud with natural stress and intonation."
          - numero_tema: 10
            corte: 3
            modalidad: "general"
            titulo: "Zero & First Conditionals: Cause-Effect & Real Future Possibilities"
            objetivo: "Modelar leyes físicas invariables (Condicional Cero) y escenarios reales de contingencia (Primer Condicional)."
            concepto_clave_latex: ""
            ejemplo: "If resistance increases at constant voltage, electric current decreases."
            bloque_sugerido: "Cause-Effect Lab 40 min • Physical laws & automated control logic in English"
            slides:
              - numero: 1
                seccion: "CEFR A2 • CORE CONCEPT"
                titulo: "Zero & First Conditionals: Cause-Effect & Real Future Possibilities: Communicative Purpose"
                puntos:
                  - "Zero Conditional (If/When + Present Simple, Present Simple): 100% true scientific laws and automatic system behaviors."
                  - "First Conditional (If + Present Simple, will / can / must + base verb): real, likely future outcomes and operational protocols."
                  - "Alternatives to 'if': 'unless' (= if... not), 'as long as', 'in case'."
                ejemplo: "If resistance increases at constant voltage, electric current decreases."
              - numero: 2
                seccion: "STRUCTURE & PATTERNS"
                titulo: "Core Grammatical Blueprint"
                puntos:
                  - "Zero: 'If you heat a gas at constant volume, its pressure rises.'"
                  - "First: 'If irradiance drops below 200 W/m², the backup battery will supply the load.'"
                  - "Unless: 'The circuit won't close unless the relay is energized.'"
                tabla:
                  - ["Conditional", "If-Clause", "Main Clause & Certainty"]
                  - ["Zero (Law)", "If + Present Simple", "Present Simple (100% always true)"]
                  - ["First (Future)", "If + Present Simple", "will / may / must + verb (Real possibility)"]
              - numero: 3
                seccion: "QUESTIONS & NEGATION"
                titulo: "Interrogative, Negative & Short Answers"
                puntos:
                  - "Clause order is flexible: put a comma ONLY when the If-clause comes first ('If voltage exceeds 240 V, the surge protector trips' / 'The surge protector trips if voltage exceeds 240 V')."
                  - "Distinguish 'in case' (precaution done BEFORE) vs. 'if' (reaction AFTER): 'Save your file in case the PC crashes'."
                ejemplo: "If we optimize the tilt angle, annual energy yield will rise by 6%."
              - numero: 4
                seccion: "PRECISION & CONTRAST"
                titulo: "Key Distinctions & Common Pitfalls"
                puntos:
                  - "GOLDEN RULE: Never put 'will' inside the If-clause! Say 'If it rains tomorrow, output will fall', NOT 'If it will rain...'."
                  - "Avoid double negative after 'unless': 'unless you calibrate it', NOT 'unless you don't calibrate it'."
                tabla:
                  - ["Connector", "Exact Meaning", "Engineering Protocol"]
                  - ["unless", "except if (if... not)", "Don't start unless pressure is normal."]
                  - ["in case", "as a precaution against", "Wear goggles in case sparks fly."]
              - numero: 5
                seccion: "CAMPUS & LAB CONTEXT"
                titulo: "Authentic Academic & Engineering Usage"
                puntos:
                  - "If resistance increases at constant voltage, electric current decreases."
                  - "If we optimize the tilt angle, annual energy yield will rise by 6%."
                  - "The inverter shuts down automatically unless grid frequency stays stable."
                ejemplo: "Academic Register (CEFR A2): Clear, concise communication in Unimagdalena seminars."
              - numero: 6
                seccion: "MASTERY CHECK"
                titulo: "Self-Assessment & Oral Drill"
                puntos:
                  - "Complete (Zero): 'If water ___ (reach) 100°C at 1 atm, it ___ (boil).'"
                  - "Rewrite with 'unless': 'If we don't insulate the tank, heat will escape.'"
                  - "Write 2 Zero Conditionals (physics laws) and 2 First Conditionals (lab contingencies)."
                ejemplo: "Practice reading each model sentence aloud with natural stress and intonation."
          - numero_tema: 11
            corte: 3
            modalidad: "general"
            titulo: "Passive Voice in Technical Workflows & Lab Reports"
            objetivo: "Describir procedimientos de laboratorio y montajes experimentales en voz pasiva estándar en inglés técnico."
            concepto_clave_latex: ""
            ejemplo: "The high-voltage capacitor is discharged through a bleeder resistor before any measurement is taken."
            bloque_sugerido: "Speaking Drill 30 min • Passive voice in industrial lab workflows"
            slides:
              - numero: 1
                seccion: "CEFR A2 • COMMUNICATIVE PURPOSE"
                titulo: "Passive Voice: Object Focus & Objectivity"
                puntos:
                  - "Technical writing prioritizes the action and the component rather than the human actor."
                  - "Active: 'The technician calibrated the pyranometer.' -> Passive: 'The pyranometer was calibrated.'"
                  - "Used extensively in scientific abstracts, operation manuals, and audit logs."
                ejemplo: "The solar panel was oriented at an optimal tilt of eleven degrees north."
              - numero: 2
                seccion: "STRUCTURE & PATTERNS"
                titulo: "Morphological Blueprint (Be + Past Participle)"
                puntos:
                  - "Present Simple Passive: Subject + is / are + past participle (V3)."
                  - "Past Simple Passive: Subject + was / were + past participle (V3)."
                  - "Modal Passive: Subject + must / should / can + be + past participle."
              - numero: 3
                seccion: "TECHNICAL PROCESS DESCRIPTION"
                titulo: "Step-by-Step Electrical Assembly"
                puntos:
                  - "First, the circuit breaker is opened and locked out."
                  - "Next, insulated copper conductors are crimped to ring terminals."
                  - "Finally, torque specifications are verified with an electronic wrench."
              - numero: 4
                seccion: "COMMON ERRORS & PITFALLS"
                titulo: "Avoid Redundant Agent Phrases"
                puntos:
                  - "Do not include 'by the student' or 'by us' unless the specific investigator is vital."
                  - "Never omit the auxiliary verb 'be' (incorrect: 'The voltage measured at 24 V')."
                  - "Irregular participles: run/run/run, build/built/built, choose/chose/chosen."
              - numero: 5
                seccion: "AUTHENTIC LABORATORY SCRIPT"
                titulo: "Battery Testing Protocol"
                puntos:
                  - "Lab Supervisor: 'The lithium iron phosphate cells are conditioned at 0.5C.'"
                  - "Student: 'Ambient temperature is maintained at twenty-five degrees Celsius throughout the charge cycle.'"
              - numero: 6
                seccion: "ORAL DRILL"
                titulo: "Fluency Practice: Lab Procedures"
                puntos:
                  - "Convert 3 active maintenance statements into impersonal passive voice."
                  - "Present the commissioning protocol of a wind turbine nacelle in 4 passive sentences."
          - numero_tema: 12
            corte: 3
            modalidad: "general"
            titulo: "Zero & First Conditionals: Cause, Effect & Operational Thresholds"
            objetivo: "Expresar verdades científicas, leyes físicas y advertencias de umbral operativo mediante condicionales cero y primero."
            concepto_clave_latex: ""
            ejemplo: "If the photovoltaic junction temperature exceeds seventy-five degrees Celsius, system efficiency drops significantly."
            bloque_sugerido: "Technical Dialogue 30 min • Cause and effect conditionals in power plants"
            slides:
              - numero: 1
                seccion: "CEFR A2 • COMMUNICATIVE PURPOSE"
                titulo: "Conditionals: Scientific Laws & Operational Safeguards"
                puntos:
                  - "Zero Conditional expresses universal physical phenomena, deterministic rules, and immutable laws."
                  - "First Conditional expresses real, probable future outcomes triggered by a specific operational condition."
                  - "Essential for programmable logic controller (PLC) logic, safety interlocks, and alarm hierarchies."
                ejemplo: "If current flows through a resistor, thermal energy is dissipated."
              - numero: 2
                seccion: "STRUCTURE & PATTERNS"
                titulo: "Syntactic Architecture"
                puntos:
                  - "Zero Conditional: If / When + present simple, ... present simple."
                  - "First Conditional: If + present simple, ... will / can / must + base verb."
                  - "Alternative trigger clauses: 'Unless' (meaning if not), 'Provided that', 'As long as'."
              - numero: 3
                seccion: "SAFETY INTERLOCK SCENARIOS"
                titulo: "Industrial Substation Safeguards"
                puntos:
                  - "If oil temperature rises above eighty degrees, the cooling fans engage automatically."
                  - "Unless grounding leads are secured, operators will not energize the busbar."
                  - "If gas pressure drops below nominal, the relay will trip the feeder."
              - numero: 4
                seccion: "COMMON ERRORS & PITFALLS"
                titulo: "Tense Concordance Hazards"
                puntos:
                  - "Never use 'will' in the 'if'-clause (incorrect: 'If voltage will rise...')."
                  - "Do not confuse cause and effect order: maintain clear logical antecedents."
                  - "Use precise threshold adverbs: 'strictly above', 'substantially lower', 'within limits'."
              - numero: 5
                seccion: "AUTHENTIC CONTROL ROOM DIALOGUE"
                titulo: "Inverter Alarm Management"
                puntos:
                  - "Operator: 'What happens if grid frequency drops below 59.5 Hz?'"
                  - "Engineer: 'If grid frequency drops below that threshold, the inverter will disconnect within 160 milliseconds.'"
              - numero: 6
                seccion: "ORAL DRILL"
                titulo: "Live Safety Briefing"
                puntos:
                  - "Formulate 3 zero-conditional physical principles governing thermodynamic cycles."
                  - "Formulate 3 first-conditional warnings for a biomass gasifier plant."
          - numero_tema: 13
            corte: 3
            modalidad: "general"
            titulo: "Describing Trends, Rates of Change & Graphical Data"
            objetivo: "Describir variaciones dinámicas de potencia, irradiancia y carga eléctrica a partir de curvas y gráficos en inglés."
            concepto_clave_latex: ""
            ejemplo: "Peak electricity demand increased steadily from 6 PM to 9 PM, reaching an all-time high of twelve gigawatts."
            bloque_sugerido: "Graph Interpretation 30 min • Describing dynamic load profiles and curves"
            slides:
              - numero: 1
                seccion: "CEFR A2 • COMMUNICATIVE PURPOSE"
                titulo: "Communicating Dynamic Trajectories"
                puntos:
                  - "Engineers must articulate quantitative changes over time during design reviews and generation briefings."
                  - "Distinguish between continuous trends, abrupt spikes, plateau periods, and cyclical fluctuations."
                  - "Pair strong trajectory verbs with precise degree adverbs."
                ejemplo: "Solar generation rose sharply at sunrise and plateaued around solar noon."
              - numero: 2
                seccion: "STRUCTURE & PATTERNS"
                titulo: "Vocabulary Toolkit: Verbs & Adverbs"
                puntos:
                  - "Upward trends: increase, rise, climb, surge, escalate, peak at."
                  - "Downward trends: decrease, drop, fall, plummet, decline, bottom out at."
                  - "Stability & Fluctuation: level off, remain steady, oscillate, fluctuate between X and Y."
                  - "Degree & Speed: sharply, steadily, gradually, marginal, dramatically."
              - numero: 3
                seccion: "DUAL GRAMMATICAL STRUCTURES"
                titulo: "Verb + Adverb vs Adjective + Noun"
                puntos:
                  - "Pattern A: 'Wind generation dropped steeply in the early morning.'"
                  - "Pattern B: 'There was a steep drop in wind generation in the early morning.'"
                  - "Preposition usage: 'an increase OF 15%', 'rose FROM 20 MW TO 35 MW', 'peaked AT 50 MW'."
              - numero: 4
                seccion: "COMMON ERRORS & PITFALLS"
                titulo: "Prepositional Accuracy in Trends"
                puntos:
                  - "Do not confuse 'rise' (intransitive) with 'raise' (transitive requiring an object)."
                  - "Avoid vague descriptors: quantify magnitude with SI units whenever possible."
                  - "Watch out for false cognates (e.g., 'actual' means present/current, not actual)."
              - numero: 5
                seccion: "AUTHENTIC DISPATCH REPORT"
                titulo: "National Grid Load Dispatcher Log"
                puntos:
                  - "Dispatcher: 'Demand showed a moderate recovery following the midday slump.'"
                  - "Analyst: 'Hydro reserves fell steadily over the dry quarter, stabilizing at 42% capacity.'"
              - numero: 6
                seccion: "ORAL DRILL"
                titulo: "Curve Description Practice"
                puntos:
                  - "Describe the standard duck curve of solar-dominated electric grids in 4 sentences."
                  - "Contrast seasonal irradiance variations between summer and winter solstice."
          - numero_tema: 14
            corte: 3
            modalidad: "general"
            titulo: "Expressing Modality: Obligation, Permission & Technical Recommendations"
            objetivo: "Emplear verbos modales de obligación, permisión y recomendación en normativas eléctricas (RETIE, NEC e IEC)."
            concepto_clave_latex: ""
            ejemplo: "All metal enclosures must be solidly bonded to the grounding electrode system under RETIE standards."
            bloque_sugerido: "Standards Drill 30 min • Modal verbs in electrical compliance codes"
            slides:
              - numero: 1
                seccion: "CEFR A2 • COMMUNICATIVE PURPOSE"
                titulo: "Regulatory Mandates & Safe Practice"
                puntos:
                  - "Engineering codes enforce distinct levels of necessity: mandatory rules, strong recommendations, and options."
                  - "Clear modal differentiation prevents catastrophic compliance breaches and safety hazards."
                  - "Underpins international norms (IEC 60364, IEEE 1547, Colombian RETIE)."
                ejemplo: "Personnel shall wear personal protective equipment rated for arc flash category 2."
              - numero: 2
                seccion: "STRUCTURE & PATTERNS"
                titulo: "Modal Hierarchy in Engineering"
                puntos:
                  - "Strict Legal Obligation: Must / Shall + base verb ('All conductors must be rated for 90°C')."
                  - "Prohibition: Must not / Shall not ('Neutral and ground must not be bonded downstream')."
                  - "Best Practice / Recommendation: Should / Ought to ('Inverters should be installed in shaded enclosures')."
                  - "Permission / Capability: May / Can ('Conduits may be embedded in concrete slabs')."
              - numero: 3
                seccion: "TECHNICAL REGULATORY CLAUSES"
                titulo: "RETIE Compliance Examples"
                puntos:
                  - "Substations must have an emergency shutdown push button near each egress door."
                  - "Engineers should calculate short-circuit duty before selecting switchgear interrupt ratings."
                  - "Technicians may use thermal imaging cameras to inspect busbar terminations."
              - numero: 4
                seccion: "COMMON ERRORS & PITFALLS"
                titulo: "Modal Confusion Pitfalls"
                puntos:
                  - "Never add '-s' or 'to' after modal verbs (incorrect: 'He musts to inspect')."
                  - "Do not soften mandatory requirements into suggestions: use 'must' for life-safety rules."
                  - "'Have to' vs 'Must': 'Must' denotes internal/authoritative rule; 'Have to' expresses external circumstance."
              - numero: 5
                seccion: "AUDIT INSPECTION SCRIPT"
                titulo: "Site Safety Compliance Walkthrough"
                puntos:
                  - "Lead Auditor: 'Does this disconnect meet lockout-tagout requirements?'"
                  - "Resident Engineer: 'Yes, it can be padlocked in the open position, and warning tags must be affixed.'"
              - numero: 6
                seccion: "ORAL DRILL"
                titulo: "Compliance Briefing"
                puntos:
                  - "State 3 mandatory RETIE rules for residential rooftop PV installations."
                  - "State 2 optional recommendations for optimizing inverter heat dissipation."
          - numero_tema: 15
            corte: 3
            modalidad: "general"
            titulo: "Sequencing Complex Engineering Projects & Milestones"
            objetivo: "Estructurar cronogramas, etapas constructivas y secuencias de energización usando conectores temporales formales."
            concepto_clave_latex: ""
            ejemplo: "Prior to synchronization, phase angle and voltage magnitude were carefully aligned with the utility grid."
            bloque_sugerido: "Project Management Drill 30 min • Gantt chart milestones and sequencing"
            slides:
              - numero: 1
                seccion: "CEFR A2 • COMMUNICATIVE PURPOSE"
                titulo: "Temporal Cohesion in Project Execution"
                puntos:
                  - "Capital energy projects proceed through strict developmental phases (feasibility, EPC, commissioning, COD)."
                  - "Engineers must communicate dependencies, critical paths, and milestone completions clearly."
                  - "Enables transparent coordination across multi-disciplinary international teams."
                ejemplo: "Following civil foundation curing, steel racking structures were bolted into place."
              - numero: 2
                seccion: "STRUCTURE & PATTERNS"
                titulo: "Chronological & Sequential Discourse Markers"
                puntos:
                  - "Initiation: Initially, First of all, In the preliminary phase, To begin with."
                  - "Progression: Subsequently, Following that, Concurrently, Meanwhile, In parallel."
                  - "Prerequisites: Prior to + noun / -ing, Before proceeding with, Once the tests are concluded."
                  - "Completion: Eventually, Finally, Upon achieving commercial operation date (COD)."
              - numero: 3
                seccion: "COMMISSIONING SCHEDULE"
                titulo: "Photovoltaic Farm Energization Steps"
                puntos:
                  - "First, insulation resistance testing was performed on all direct current strings."
                  - "Subsequently, the medium-voltage transformer was backfed from the substation."
                  - "Concurrently, supervisory control and data acquisition (SCADA) telemetry was validated."
                  - "Finally, inverters were released for grid synchronization."
              - numero: 4
                seccion: "COMMON ERRORS & PITFALLS"
                titulo: "Punctuation & Syntax of Connectors"
                puntos:
                  - "Always set off introductory sequential adverbs with a comma (e.g., 'Subsequently, the crew...')."
                  - "Do not confuse 'During' (preposition + noun) with 'While' (conjunction + clause)."
                  - "Distinguish 'at the end' (point in time) from 'in the end' (ultimate resolution)."
              - numero: 5
                seccion: "AUTHENTIC STAKEHOLDER UPDATE"
                titulo: "EPC Project Status Meeting"
                puntos:
                  - "Project Manager: 'Once geotechnical permits are cleared, grading works will commence.'"
                  - "Site Engineer: 'Meanwhile, balance-of-system components will be staged at the laydown yard.'"
              - numero: 6
                seccion: "ORAL DRILL"
                titulo: "Project Milestone Walkthrough"
                puntos:
                  - "Deliver a 1-minute oral progress report outlining the 4 primary stages of a microgrid project."
                  - "Explain 2 parallel tasks that must occur concurrently during plant commissioning."
          - numero_tema: 16
            corte: 1
            modalidad: "notacion_ingenieria"
            titulo: "Inequalities, Intervals & Proportionality"
            objetivo: "Verbalizar desigualdades estrictas y no estrictas, órdenes de magnitud y proporcionalidad directa/inversa."
            concepto_clave_latex: "x \\le y \\quad ; \\quad a \\gg b \\quad ; \\quad P \\propto T \\quad ; \\quad I \\propto \\frac{1}{R} \\quad ; \\quad \\eta \\in [0, 1]"
            verbalizacion_ingles: "• x ≤ y -> \"x is less than or equal to y\"  |  x ≥ y -> \"x is greater than or equal to y\".\n• a >> b -> \"a is much greater than b\"  |  a << b -> \"a is much less than b\".\n• P ∝ T -> \"P is directly proportional to T\"  |  I ∝ 1/R -> \"I is inversely proportional to R\".\n• η ∈ [0, 1] -> \"eta belongs to (or lies in) the closed interval from zero to one\"."
            ejemplo: "En gases ideales a volumen constante, P ∝ T se expone oralmente como 'Absolute pressure is directly proportional to absolute temperature'."
            bloque_sugerido: "Symbol Fluency 30 min • Reading domain constraints & scaling laws aloud"
          - numero_tema: 17
            corte: 1
            modalidad: "notacion_ingenieria"
            titulo: "Linear, Quadratic & Polynomial Equations"
            objetivo: "Leer fluidamente ecuaciones lineales, polinomios y la fórmula cuadrática completa con pausas estructurales."
            concepto_clave_latex: "y = mx + b \\quad ; \\quad ax^2 + bx + c = 0 \\implies x = \\frac{-b \\pm \\sqrt{b^2 - 4ac}}{2a}"
