                  - ["If it would fail, we stop", "If it failed, we would stop", "No 'would' in If-clause"]
                  - ["If I was in charge (informal)", "If I were in charge (formal)", "Subjunctive 'were'"]
              - numero: 5
                seccion: "CAMPUS & LAB CONTEXT"
                titulo: "Authentic Academic & Engineering Usage"
                puntos:
                  - "If superconducting cables operated at room temperature, transmission losses would vanish."
                  - "How much CO2 would Santa Marta avoid if all public buses were electric?"
                  - "If I were the project lead, I would select lithium iron phosphate batteries."
                ejemplo: "Academic Register (CEFR B1.1): Clear, concise communication in Unimagdalena seminars."
              - numero: 6
                seccion: "MASTERY CHECK"
                titulo: "Self-Assessment & Oral Drill"
                puntos:
                  - "Complete: 'If wind speed ___ (be) constant, forecasting ___ (be) trivial.'"
                  - "Contrast 1st vs. 2nd Conditional for a real vs. ideal lab budget."
                  - "Answer: 'What would happen if Earth's atmosphere had no greenhouse gases?'"
                ejemplo: "Practice reading each model sentence aloud with natural stress and intonation."
          - numero_tema: 4
            corte: 2
            modalidad: "general"
            titulo: "Passive Voice I (Present & Past Simple): Focusing on Processes & Results"
            objetivo: "Redactar descripciones objetivas de procesos técnicos y reportes de laboratorio utilizando la Voz Pasiva."
            concepto_clave_latex: ""
            ejemplo: "In a Rankine cycle, high-pressure steam is expanded through a turbine."
            bloque_sugerido: "Lab Methods Writing 45 min • Objective process description in Passive Voice"
            slides:
              - numero: 1
                seccion: "CEFR B1.1 • CORE CONCEPT"
                titulo: "Passive Voice I (Present & Past Simple): Focusing on Processes & Results: Communicative Purpose"
                puntos:
                  - "Form: Subject (receiver) + am/is/are (Present) or was/were (Past) + Past Participle (V3)."
                  - "Academic & technical English favors Passive Voice when the PROCESS, ACTION, or RESULT matters more than the human actor ('The samples were heated to 450 K')."
                  - "Add 'by + agent' ONLY when the actor provides essential information ('The law was formulated by Fourier')."
                ejemplo: "In a Rankine cycle, high-pressure steam is expanded through a turbine."
              - numero: 2
                seccion: "STRUCTURE & PATTERNS"
                titulo: "Core Grammatical Blueprint"
                puntos:
                  - "Present Simple Passive (processes): 'Biogas is produced through anaerobic digestion.'"
                  - "Past Simple Passive (methods/history): 'Three sensors were mounted along the pipe.'"
                  - "Sequence connectors in process writing: First, Next, Subsequently, Finally."
                tabla:
                  - ["Tense", "Active Voice", "Passive Voice (Objective)"]
                  - ["Present Simple", "Inverters convert DC to AC.", "DC is converted to AC by inverters."]
                  - ["Past Simple", "We calibrated the probe.", "The probe was calibrated prior to testing."]
              - numero: 3
                seccion: "QUESTIONS & NEGATION"
                titulo: "Interrogative, Negative & Short Answers"
                puntos:
                  - "Questions in Passive: 'Where is geothermal energy harvested?' / 'When was the turbine commissioned?'"
                  - "Distinguish 'by' (agent/person/system) vs. 'with' (instrument/tool/material): 'Voltage was measured WITH a digital oscilloscope'."
                ejemplo: "All experimental measurements were recorded at five-second intervals."
              - numero: 4
                seccion: "PRECISION & CONTRAST"
                titulo: "Key Distinctions & Common Pitfalls"
                puntos:
                  - "Intransitive verbs (happen, occur, arrive, rise, consist) CANNOT be passive! Say 'A voltage drop occurred', NEVER 'was occurred'!"
                  - "Always check V3 accuracy: 'is transmitted', 'was chosen', 'were driven'."
                tabla:
                  - ["Intransitive Trap", "Incorrect Passive", "Correct Active"]
                  - ["occur / happen", "An error was occurred", "An error occurred"]
                  - ["rise (no object)", "Temperature was risen", "Temperature rose (or was raised)"]
              - numero: 5
                seccion: "CAMPUS & LAB CONTEXT"
                titulo: "Authentic Academic & Engineering Usage"
                puntos:
                  - "In a Rankine cycle, high-pressure steam is expanded through a turbine."
                  - "All experimental measurements were recorded at five-second intervals."
                  - "Voltage was stepped up from 13.8 kV to 220 kV at the substation."
                ejemplo: "Academic Register (CEFR B1.1): Clear, concise communication in Unimagdalena seminars."
              - numero: 6
                seccion: "MASTERY CHECK"
                titulo: "Self-Assessment & Oral Drill"
                puntos:
                  - "Convert to Passive: 'Technicians inspect the blades every six months.'"
                  - "Fix: 'A short circuit was happened in Node 3' -> 'A short circuit occurred in Node 3.'"
                  - "Describe a 4-step energy conversion process in Present Passive."
                ejemplo: "Practice reading each model sentence aloud with natural stress and intonation."
          - numero_tema: 5
            corte: 2
            modalidad: "general"
            titulo: "Defining & Non-Defining Relative Clauses (Who, Which, That, Whose, Where)"
            objetivo: "Construir definiciones técnicas precisas e insertar información explicativa mediante cláusulas relativas."
            concepto_clave_latex: ""
            ejemplo: "An inverter is a power electronic device that converts DC into AC."
            bloque_sugerido: "Technical Definitions 40 min • Writing encyclopedic engineering definitions"
            slides:
              - numero: 1
                seccion: "CEFR B1.1 • CORE CONCEPT"
                titulo: "Defining & Non-Defining Relative Clauses (Who, Which, That, Whose, Where): Communicative Purpose"
                puntos:
                  - "Defining Relative Clauses identify WHICH person/thing we mean -> NO commas; 'that' can replace 'who' or 'which'."
                  - "Non-Defining Relative Clauses add extra info to an already identified noun -> MUST use commas; NEVER use 'that'!"
                  - "Relative words: who (people), which (things/whole clause), that (defining only), whose (possession), where (place = in which)."
                ejemplo: "An inverter is a power electronic device that converts DC into AC."
              - numero: 2
                seccion: "STRUCTURE & PATTERNS"
                titulo: "Core Grammatical Blueprint"
                puntos:
                  - "Defining: 'A pyranometer is an instrument that/which measures solar irradiance.'"
                  - "Non-defining: 'Copper, which has low resistivity, is widely used in windings.'"
                  - "Omitting pronoun: you can drop who/which/that in defining clauses ONLY when it is the OBJECT ('The data [that] we collected is clean')."
                tabla:
                  - ["Clause Type", "Commas?", "Allowed Pronouns & Example"]
                  - ["Defining (essential)", "No commas", "Cells that/which use silicon dominate."]
                  - ["Non-defining (extra)", "Commas required", "Silicon, which is abundant, is reliable."]
              - numero: 3
                seccion: "QUESTIONS & NEGATION"
                titulo: "Interrogative, Negative & Short Answers"
                puntos:
                  - "'Whose' works for BOTH people and inanimate systems: 'A turbine whose blades are pitched optimally captures more power.'"
                  - "Sentential 'which' comments on an entire fact: 'Efficiency rose by 4%, which exceeded our target.'"
                ejemplo: "La Guajira, where trade winds blow steadily all year, hosts wind projects."
              - numero: 4
                seccion: "PRECISION & CONTRAST"
                titulo: "Key Distinctions & Common Pitfalls"
                puntos:
                  - "NEVER use 'what' as a relative pronoun after a noun (*the formula what we used* -> 'the formula that we used')!"
                  - "Do not repeat the object pronoun: 'The circuit that we built' (NOT 'that we built it')."
                tabla:
                  - ["Relative Word", "Replaces", "Technical Definition"]
                  - ["where (= in which)", "Place / System zone", "The chamber where combustion occurs..."]
                  - ["whose", "his / her / its", "Materials whose conductivity is high..."]
              - numero: 5
                seccion: "CAMPUS & LAB CONTEXT"
                titulo: "Authentic Academic & Engineering Usage"
                puntos:
                  - "An inverter is a power electronic device that converts DC into AC."
                  - "La Guajira, where trade winds blow steadily all year, hosts wind projects."
                  - "Engineers select materials whose thermal resistance minimizes heat leakage."
                ejemplo: "Academic Register (CEFR B1.1): Clear, concise communication in Unimagdalena seminars."
              - numero: 6
                seccion: "MASTERY CHECK"
                titulo: "Self-Assessment & Oral Drill"
                puntos:
                  - "Join (non-defining): 'Law 1715 promotes renewables. It was enacted in 2014.'"
                  - "Can 'that' be omitted? 'The sensor that measures pressure' (No, subject!) vs. 'The sensor that we bought' (Yes, object!)."
                  - "Write 3 formal definitions of energy devices using defining relative clauses."
                ejemplo: "Practice reading each model sentence aloud with natural stress and intonation."
          - numero_tema: 6
            corte: 2
            modalidad: "general"
            titulo: "Used to & Would: Describing Past Habits & Technological Evolution"
            objetivo: "Contrastar tecnologías antiguas y hábitos pasados frente a estándares actuales usando used to, would y be/get used to."
            concepto_clave_latex: ""
            ejemplo: "Households used to use 60 W incandescent bulbs, whereas LEDs now use 8 W."
            bloque_sugerido: "Tech Evolution 35 min • Comparing legacy vs. smart energy systems"
            slides:
              - numero: 1
                seccion: "CEFR B1.1 • CORE CONCEPT"
                titulo: "Used to & Would: Describing Past Habits & Technological Evolution: Communicative Purpose"
                puntos:
                  - "'Used to + base verb' describes BOTH past habits AND past states that are no longer true ('Power grids used to be strictly unidirectional')."
                  - "'Would + base verb' describes repeated past ACTIONS/routines (NOT states like be, have, own, live) once past context is set."
                  - "Contrast: 'be used to + noun/-ing' (be accustomed to) & 'get used to + noun/-ing' (adapt to)."
                ejemplo: "Households used to use 60 W incandescent bulbs, whereas LEDs now use 8 W."
              - numero: 2
                seccion: "STRUCTURE & PATTERNS"
                titulo: "Core Grammatical Blueprint"
                puntos:
                  - "Affirmative: 'Factories used to burn coal directly on site.'"
                  - "Negative & Question drop the -d: 'didn't use to' / 'Did grids use to store solar energy?'"
                  - "'No longer' / 'not... anymore' express the present contrast: 'We no longer rely on analog meters.'"
                tabla:
                  - ["Structure", "Followed By", "Meaning & Example"]
                  - ["used to", "Base verb", "Past habit/state: Grids used to be analog."]
                  - ["be used to", "Noun / Verb-ing", "Accustomed now: I'm used to coding in Python."]
                  - ["get used to", "Noun / Verb-ing", "Adapting: You'll get used to LaTeX fast."]
              - numero: 3
                seccion: "QUESTIONS & NEGATION"
                titulo: "Interrogative, Negative & Short Answers"
                puntos:
                  - "Check state verbs: say 'There used to be a diesel generator here', NEVER 'There would be a diesel generator here'!"
                  - "For a single one-time past event, use Past Simple ('In 2019, we installed LEDs'), NOT 'used to'."
                ejemplo: "Grid operators didn't use to deal with bidirectional prosumer power flows."
              - numero: 4
                seccion: "PRECISION & CONTRAST"
                titulo: "Key Distinctions & Common Pitfalls"
                puntos:
                  - "Watch the -ing trap after 'be used to': 'She is used to waking up at 5:30 a.m.', NOT 'used to wake up' when 'is' precedes it!"
                  - "Don't use 'use to' for present habits -> use 'usually' ('I usually study at night', NOT 'I use to study')."
                tabla:
                  - ["False Friend Trap", "Incorrect", "Natural English"]
                  - ["Present habit ('suelo')", "I use to study daily", "I usually study daily"]
                  - ["After 'am/is/are'", "I am used to work late", "I am used to working late"]
              - numero: 5
                seccion: "CAMPUS & LAB CONTEXT"
                titulo: "Authentic Academic & Engineering Usage"
                puntos:
                  - "Households used to use 60 W incandescent bulbs, whereas LEDs now use 8 W."
                  - "Grid operators didn't use to deal with bidirectional prosumer power flows."
                  - "First-year students quickly get used to solving equations with SI units."
                ejemplo: "Academic Register (CEFR B1.1): Clear, concise communication in Unimagdalena seminars."
              - numero: 6
                seccion: "MASTERY CHECK"
                titulo: "Self-Assessment & Oral Drill"
                puntos:
                  - "Choose: 'Ten years ago, EVs (used to / would) be rare' (state!) -> 'used to'."
                  - "Fix: 'I use to drink coffee every morning' -> 'I usually drink coffee every morning.'"
                  - "Contrast 3 legacy energy technologies with modern equivalents."
                ejemplo: "Practice reading each model sentence aloud with natural stress and intonation."
          - numero_tema: 7
            corte: 2
            modalidad: "general"
            titulo: "Modals of Deduction & Probability (Must, Might, Could, Can't)"
            objetivo: "Formular hipótesis diagnósticas y niveles de certeza ante evidencias técnicas en el presente."
            concepto_clave_latex: ""
            ejemplo: "The thermocouple reads -200°C in Santa Marta — the wire must be disconnected."
            bloque_sugerido: "Fault Diagnosis Lab 40 min • Troubleshooting engineering anomalies in English"
            slides:
              - numero: 1
                seccion: "CEFR B1.1 • CORE CONCEPT"
                titulo: "Modals of Deduction & Probability (Must, Might, Could, Can't): Communicative Purpose"
                puntos:
                  - "Logical certainty (~95% sure it IS true): 'must + base verb' ('The LED is on, so the supply must be active')."
                  - "Possibility (~30–50% sure): 'may / might / could + base verb' ('The noise might come from a worn bearing')."
                  - "Logical impossibility (~95% sure it is NOT true): 'can't / couldn't + base verb' ('Efficiency can't exceed 100%!')."
                ejemplo: "The thermocouple reads -200°C in Santa Marta — the wire must be disconnected."
              - numero: 2
                seccion: "STRUCTURE & PATTERNS"
                titulo: "Core Grammatical Blueprint"
                puntos:
                  - "Continuous deduction (happening right now): modal + be + verb-ing ('The inverter might be clipping peak power')."
                  - "Negative possibility: use 'might not / may not' ('The sensor may not be calibrated')."
                  - "CRITICAL: 'could not' means 0% impossible, whereas 'might not' means 'maybe not'!"
                tabla:
                  - ["Certainty Level", "Modal Form", "Diagnostic Deduction"]
                  - ["~95% Certain (Yes)", "must + V / be V-ing", "Current is zero; the fuse must be blown."]
                  - ["~40% Possible", "may / might / could", "A loose cable could cause this drop."]
                  - ["~95% Impossible (No)", "can't / couldn't", "That reading can't be right (η > 1)!"]
              - numero: 3
                seccion: "QUESTIONS & NEGATION"
                titulo: "Interrogative, Negative & Short Answers"
                puntos:
                  - "Opposite of deductive 'must' is 'CAN'T', NOT 'mustn't' ('mustn't' is only for prohibition!)."
                  - "Avoid 'can' for specific present possibility: say 'There may/could be a leak', NOT 'There can be a leak right now' (use 'can' for general theoretical possibility: 'Overheating can damage cells')."
                ejemplo: "Harmonic distortion could be causing the transformer vibration."
              - numero: 4
                seccion: "PRECISION & CONTRAST"
                titulo: "Key Distinctions & Common Pitfalls"
                puntos:
                  - "Incorrect: 'The battery mustn't be full; voltage is 10.5 V' -> Correct: 'The battery can't be full; voltage is 10.5 V.'"
                  - "Keep base verb 'be' after modals: 'It might be faulty', NOT 'It might faulty'."
                tabla:
                  - ["Modal Pair", "Meaning Difference", "Example"]
                  - ["might not", "Uncertain (maybe not)", "The report might not arrive today."]
                  - ["couldn't / can't", "Logically impossible", "Perpetual motion can't work."]
              - numero: 5
                seccion: "CAMPUS & LAB CONTEXT"
                titulo: "Authentic Academic & Engineering Usage"
                puntos:
                  - "The thermocouple reads -200°C in Santa Marta — the wire must be disconnected."
                  - "Harmonic distortion could be causing the transformer vibration."
                  - "That Carnot efficiency calculation can't be correct for these temperatures."
                ejemplo: "Academic Register (CEFR B1.1): Clear, concise communication in Unimagdalena seminars."
              - numero: 6
                seccion: "MASTERY CHECK"
                titulo: "Self-Assessment & Oral Drill"
                puntos:
                  - "Diagnose 3 anomalies using must, might/could, and can't."
                  - "Fix: 'It mustn't be copper; it's magnetic!' -> 'It can't be copper; it's magnetic!'"
                  - "Explain the difference between 'might not work' and 'can't work'."
                ejemplo: "Practice reading each model sentence aloud with natural stress and intonation."
          - numero_tema: 8
            corte: 3
            modalidad: "general"
            titulo: "Gerunds (-ing) vs. Infinitives (to + verb) after Specific Verbs"
            objetivo: "Emplear correctamente gerundios e infinitivos como sujetos, complementos de preposición y patrones verbales académicos."
            concepto_clave_latex: ""
            ejemplo: "Installing rooftop PV reduces peak air-conditioning demand on campus."
            bloque_sugerido: "Academic Syntax 40 min • Verb complementation in technical writing"
            slides:
              - numero: 1
                seccion: "CEFR B1.1 • CORE CONCEPT"
                titulo: "Gerunds (-ing) vs. Infinitives (to + verb) after Specific Verbs: Communicative Purpose"
                puntos:
                  - "Gerund (verb-ing) acts as a noun: (1) sentence subject ('Reducing heat loss saves fuel'), (2) after ALL prepositions ('by optimizing, without losing, interested in modeling'), (3) after verbs like avoid, consider, suggest, recommend, finish, keep, involve."
                  - "To-Infinitive (to + verb): (1) purpose ('in order to cool the core'), (2) after adjectives ('easy to install'), (3) after verbs like decide, expect, manage, fail, afford, plan, tend."
                ejemplo: "Installing rooftop PV reduces peak air-conditioning demand on campus."
              - numero: 2
                seccion: "STRUCTURE & PATTERNS"
                titulo: "Core Grammatical Blueprint"
                puntos:
                  - "Preposition + -ing ALWAYS (even when 'to' is a preposition: 'look forward to presenting', 'lead to overheating')."
                  - "Make / Let + object + BARE infinitive (no 'to'): 'Heat makes gases expand' (Passive adds 'to': 'is made to expand')."
                  - "Meaning-shift verbs: stop, remember, try + -ing vs. + to-infinitive!"
                tabla:
                  - ["Pattern", "Key Academic Verbs", "Example"]
                  - ["Verb + -ing", "avoid, consider, suggest, involve", "We suggest insulating the valve."]
                  - ["Verb + to + V", "aim, tend, fail, manage, enable (+obj)", "Sensors enable us to track loads."]
                  - ["Prep + -ing", "by, for, without, lead to", "Cool the cell by increasing airflow."]
              - numero: 3
                seccion: "QUESTIONS & NEGATION"
                titulo: "Interrogative, Negative & Short Answers"
                puntos:
                  - "Meaning shift: 'stop to check' (pause an activity in order to check) vs. 'stop checking' (quit checking)."
                  - "'Try to solve' (attempt something difficult) vs. 'try restarting' (test an experiment/method to see if it helps)."
                ejemplo: "Our algorithm managed to reduce forecasting error by 14%."
              - numero: 4
                seccion: "PRECISION & CONTRAST"
                titulo: "Key Distinctions & Common Pitfalls"
                puntos:
                  - "Watch 'suggest / recommend': NEVER say *suggest us to use*! Say 'suggest using' OR 'suggest that we use'."
                  - "Use -ing (not infinitive) as concise technical subjects: 'Storing hydrogen requires compression'."
                tabla:
                  - ["Verb", "+ Gerund (-ing)", "+ Infinitive (to + V)"]
                  - ["remember", "Recall past memory: remember testing it", "Don't forget task: remember to ground it"]
                  - ["try", "Experiment option: try lowering the step", "Make effort: try to converge the solver"]
              - numero: 5
                seccion: "CAMPUS & LAB CONTEXT"
                titulo: "Authentic Academic & Engineering Usage"
                puntos:
                  - "Installing rooftop PV reduces peak air-conditioning demand on campus."
                  - "Our algorithm managed to reduce forecasting error by 14%."
                  - "We improved thermal efficiency by preheating the combustion air."
                ejemplo: "Academic Register (CEFR B1.1): Clear, concise communication in Unimagdalena seminars."
              - numero: 6
                seccion: "MASTERY CHECK"
                titulo: "Self-Assessment & Oral Drill"
                puntos:
                  - "Fix: 'The advisor suggested us to recalibrate' -> 'suggested recalibrating / that we recalibrate'."
                  - "Complete: 'High resistance leads to ___ (lose) energy as heat' -> 'losing'."
                  - "Write 4 sentences using 'by + -ing', 'in order to', 'enable + obj + to', and 'involve + -ing'."
                ejemplo: "Practice reading each model sentence aloud with natural stress and intonation."
          - numero_tema: 9
            corte: 3
            modalidad: "general"
            titulo: "Question Tags & Echo Questions in Academic Discussions"
            objetivo: "Confirmar datos, mantener discusiones fluidas y verificar supuestos técnicos mediante Question Tags."
            concepto_clave_latex: ""
            ejemplo: "Grid frequency in Colombia is 60 Hz, isn't it?"
            bloque_sugerido: "Seminar Dialogue 35 min • Confirming data & active listening in Q&A"
            slides:
              - numero: 1
                seccion: "CEFR B1.1 • CORE CONCEPT"
                titulo: "Question Tags & Echo Questions in Academic Discussions: Communicative Purpose"
                puntos:
                  - "Polarity Flip Rule: Affirmative statement -> Negative tag ('is it? -> isn't it?'); Negative statement -> Affirmative tag ('isn't it? -> is it?')."
                  - "Match the auxiliary or modal of the main clause (is -> isn't, can -> can't, have -> haven't; Present/Past Simple -> don't/doesn't/didn't) + pronoun."
                  - "Intonation: FALLING = confirming what you already think is true; RISING = genuine question."
                ejemplo: "Grid frequency in Colombia is 60 Hz, isn't it?"
              - numero: 2
                seccion: "STRUCTURE & PATTERNS"
                titulo: "Core Grammatical Blueprint"
                puntos:
                  - "With To Be / Modals: 'Copper is a great conductor, isn't it?' / 'We can export to PDF, can't we?'"
                  - "With Action Verbs: 'The turbine reached 1500 rpm, didn't it?'"
                  - "Special tags: 'I am on Slide 4, aren't I?' | 'Let's start the timer, shall we?' | 'Nothing failed, did it?'"
                tabla:
                  - ["Main Clause", "Question Tag", "Special Note"]
                  - ["I'm next,", "aren't I?", "Never *amn't I*"]
                  - ["Let's test Node 2,", "shall we?", "Collaborative proposal"]
                  - ["There's no current,", "is there?", "Negative word -> positive tag"]
              - numero: 3
                seccion: "QUESTIONS & NEGATION"
                titulo: "Interrogative, Negative & Short Answers"
                puntos:
                  - "Words like never, rarely, hardly, nobody, nothing make the clause NEGATIVE -> use a POSITIVE tag ('The system rarely overheats, does it?')."
                  - "Echo questions show active listening in seminars: 'A: Efficiency hit 46%. B: Did it? That's impressive!'"
                ejemplo: "We haven't exceeded the 1.2 MB PDF limit, have we? No, we haven't."
              - numero: 4
                seccion: "PRECISION & CONTRAST"
                titulo: "Key Distinctions & Common Pitfalls"
                puntos:
                  - "Spanish uses invariable '¿verdad?' / '¿no?'; English MUST mirror the exact auxiliary and pronoun every time!"
                  - "Answer tags according to the FACT: 'The valve isn't open, is it?' -> If closed: 'No, it isn't' (NOT 'Yes, it isn't'!)."
                tabla:
                  - ["Statement", "Wrong Tag", "Correct Tag"]
                  - ["You calibrated it,", "no? / isn't it?", "didn't you?"]
                  - ["She rarely misses lab,", "doesn't she?", "does she?"]
              - numero: 5
                seccion: "CAMPUS & LAB CONTEXT"
                titulo: "Authentic Academic & Engineering Usage"
                puntos:
                  - "Grid frequency in Colombia is 60 Hz, isn't it?"
                  - "We haven't exceeded the 1.2 MB PDF limit, have we? No, we haven't."
                  - "Let's compare the two thermodynamic cycles, shall we?"
                ejemplo: "Academic Register (CEFR B1.1): Clear, concise communication in Unimagdalena seminars."
              - numero: 6
                seccion: "MASTERY CHECK"
                titulo: "Self-Assessment & Oral Drill"
                puntos:
                  - "Add tags: 'They built a prototype, ___?' / 'It hardly ever snows here, ___?'"
                  - "Add tags: 'I'm responsible for Slide 2, ___?' / 'Let's verify the units, ___?'"
                  - "Practice rising vs. falling intonation on 4 technical confirmation questions."
                ejemplo: "Practice reading each model sentence aloud with natural stress and intonation."
          - numero_tema: 10
            corte: 3
            modalidad: "general"
            titulo: "Connectors of Contrast, Addition & Cause (Although, Despite, Due to, Therefore)"
            objetivo: "Articular párrafos argumentativos y reportes técnicos con conectores lógicos de contraste, adición, causa y consecuencia."
            concepto_clave_latex: ""
            ejemplo: "Although initial capital costs are high, solar microgrids offer low operating expenses."
            bloque_sugerido: "Cohesion Workshop 40 min • Linking clauses cleanly in engineering reports"
            slides:
              - numero: 1
                seccion: "CEFR B1.1 • CORE CONCEPT"
                titulo: "Connectors of Contrast, Addition & Cause (Although, Despite, Due to, Therefore): Communicative Purpose"
                puntos:
                  - "CONTRAST + Clause (S+V): 'although / even though / whereas / while'. CONTRAST + Noun/-ing: 'despite / in spite of'. Sentence linker: 'However, / Nevertheless,'."
                  - "CAUSE + Clause: 'because / since / as'. CAUSE + Noun/-ing: 'due to / owing to / because of'."
                  - "RESULT (new sentence or after semicolon): 'Therefore, / Consequently, / As a result, / Thus,'."
                ejemplo: "Although initial capital costs are high, solar microgrids offer low operating expenses."
              - numero: 2
                seccion: "STRUCTURE & PATTERNS"
                titulo: "Core Grammatical Blueprint"
                puntos:
                  - "Clause vs. Noun Phrase rule: 'Although wind was low, output remained stable' vs. 'Despite low wind, output remained stable'."
                  - "Bridge trick: 'despite the fact that + S + V' converts a noun preposition into a clause connector!"
                  - "Addition: 'Furthermore, / Moreover, / In addition to + noun/-ing'."
                tabla:
                  - ["Relation", "+ Full Clause (S + V)", "+ Noun Phrase / -ing"]
                  - ["Contrast", "although / even though / whereas", "despite / in spite of"]
                  - ["Cause", "because / since / as", "due to / owing to / because of"]
                  - ["Addition", "Moreover, / Furthermore, (sentence)", "in addition to / besides"]
              - numero: 3
                seccion: "QUESTIONS & NEGATION"
                titulo: "Interrogative, Negative & Short Answers"
                puntos:
                  - "Punctuation mastery: 'Efficiency dropped; therefore, we cleaned the panels.' (semicolon BEFORE 'therefore', comma AFTER!)."
                  - "Use 'whereas / while' to contrast two symmetrical facts: 'PV generates DC, whereas wind turbines typically feed AC systems.'"
                ejemplo: "Voltage fluctuated due to sudden cloud cover over the campus array."
              - numero: 4
                seccion: "PRECISION & CONTRAST"
                titulo: "Key Distinctions & Common Pitfalls"
                puntos:
                  - "NEVER write 'despite of' (*in spite of* has 'of', *despite* NEVER takes 'of'!)."
                  - "Never put both 'Although' and 'but' in the same sentence: pick one!"
                tabla:
                  - ["Common Error", "Correction", "Why"]
                  - ["Despite of the heat,", "Despite the heat, / In spite of the heat,", "'Despite' takes no 'of'"]
                  - ["Although it rained, but...", "Although it rained, we tested.", "No 'but' with 'although'"]
              - numero: 5
                seccion: "CAMPUS & LAB CONTEXT"
                titulo: "Authentic Academic & Engineering Usage"
                puntos:
                  - "Although initial capital costs are high, solar microgrids offer low operating expenses."
                  - "Voltage fluctuated due to sudden cloud cover over the campus array."
                  - "Thermal losses exceeded 12%; therefore, additional rock-wool insulation was installed."
                ejemplo: "Academic Register (CEFR B1.1): Clear, concise communication in Unimagdalena seminars."
              - numero: 6
                seccion: "MASTERY CHECK"
                titulo: "Self-Assessment & Oral Drill"
                puntos:
                  - "Transform 'Although the battery was cold, it delivered full current' -> use 'Despite...'."
                  - "Transform 'Because resistance rose, current fell' -> use 'Due to...' and 'Consequently,'."
                  - "Write a 5-sentence technical paragraph using 4 different logical connectors."
                ejemplo: "Practice reading each model sentence aloud with natural stress and intonation."
          - numero_tema: 11
            corte: 3
            modalidad: "general"
            titulo: "Third Conditional: Counterfactual Analysis & Post-Incident Engineering Reviews"
            objetivo: "Formular hipótesis sobre eventos pasados que no ocurrieron y analizar fallos técnicos en inglés profesional (If + Past Perfect, would have + past participle)."
            concepto_clave_latex: ""
            ejemplo: "If the thermal protection relay had tripped immediately, the power transformer would not have suffered catastrophic insulation breakdown."
            bloque_sugerido: "Speaking Drill 30 min • Third conditional in electrical failure analysis"
            slides:
              - numero: 1
                seccion: "CEFR B1 • COMMUNICATIVE PURPOSE"
                titulo: "Third Conditional: Past Hypotheticals & Lessons Learned"
                puntos:
                  - "Used to talk about conditions in the past that did not happen, and their hypothetical past outcomes."
                  - "Crucial for industrial incident investigation reports, safety debriefs, and reliability root-cause analysis."
                  - "Expresses regret, critique, or technical counterfactual logic."
                ejemplo: "If the backup diesel generator had started automatically, the university hospital would not have lost critical power."
              - numero: 2
                seccion: "STRUCTURE & PATTERNS"
                titulo: "Morphological Blueprint"
                puntos:
                  - "Condition Clause: If + subject + had (or hadn't) + past participle (V3)."
                  - "Result Clause: Subject + would (or could / might) + have + past participle (V3)."
                  - "Contraction Note: 'If we'd known' / 'it would've failed'."
              - numero: 3
                seccion: "TECHNICAL FAILURE AUDIT"
                titulo: "Turbine Overspeed Investigation"
                puntos:
                  - "Condition: If the centrifugal governor had responded within fifty milliseconds..."
                  - "Consequence: ...the Pelton runner would have avoided severe blade deformation."
                  - "Alternative Modal: The operator might have vented the penstock if the SCADA telemetry had displayed the pressure surge."
              - numero: 4
                seccion: "COMMON ERRORS & PITFALLS"
                titulo: "Modal Placement & Auxiliary Consistency"
                puntos:
                  - "Never place 'would have' inside the 'if' clause (incorrect: 'If the team would have replaced the fuse...')."
                  - "Correct: 'If the team had replaced the fuse, the circuit would have operated safely.'"
                  - "Watch out for double 'had had' when the main verb is 'have': 'If we had had the spare capacitor...'"
              - numero: 5
                seccion: "AUTHENTIC DEBRIEF DIALOGUE"
                titulo: "Substation Maintenance Review"
                puntos:
                  - "Lead Auditor: 'What would have happened if the SF6 circuit breaker had leaked during the storm?'"
                  - "Senior Engineer: 'The busbar protection system would have isolated the entire feeder line immediately.'"
              - numero: 6
                seccion: "ORAL DRILL"
                titulo: "Rapid-Fire Past Scenarios"
                puntos:
                  - "Prompt: 'Pump cavitation / install booster stage' -> 'If we had installed a booster pump, cavitation would not have eroded the impeller.'"
                  - "Prompt: 'Solar inverter overheating / clean heat sink' -> 'If the technicians had cleaned the aluminum heat sink, the inverter would not have derated its output power.'"
          - numero_tema: 12
            corte: 3
            modalidad: "general"
            titulo: "Mixed Conditionals in Technical Contexts & Long-Term System Design"
            objetivo: "Combinar condiciones hipotéticas pasadas con impactos en el presente, o condiciones presentes permanentes con resultados pasados."
            concepto_clave_latex: ""
            ejemplo: "If the design team had integrated maximum power point tracking five years ago, this solar facility would be generating 15% more revenue today."
            bloque_sugerido: "Speaking Drill 30 min • Mixed conditionals in infrastructure planning"
            slides:
              - numero: 1
                seccion: "CEFR B1 • COMMUNICATIVE PURPOSE"
                titulo: "Mixed Conditionals: Bridging Past Actions & Present States"
                puntos:
                  - "Past Action -> Present Result: Evaluating how an earlier engineering decision directly impacts current system performance."
                  - "Present Condition -> Past Result: Showing how an enduring trait or permanent design rule shaped a past event."
                  - "Essential for techno-economic feasibility discussions and retrofitting debates."
                ejemplo: "If Unimagdalena had installed lithium-ion battery storage during the initial campus build, our microgrid would operate off-grid right now."
              - numero: 2
                seccion: "STRUCTURE & PATTERNS"
                titulo: "Type A: Past Cause -> Present Outcome"
                puntos:
                  - "If + Past Perfect (had + V3) -> Subject + would / could + base verb."
                  - "Example: 'If we had calibrated the flowmeter yesterday, our current thermodynamic readings would be accurate.'"
              - numero: 3
                seccion: "STRUCTURE & PATTERNS"
                titulo: "Type B: Present Trait -> Past Outcome"
                puntos:
                  - "If + Past Simple (were / had) -> Subject + would have + past participle (V3)."
                  - "Example: 'If our campus grid were not interconnected with the national transmission network, the blackout last night would have shut down our servers.'"
              - numero: 4
                seccion: "COMMON ERRORS & PITFALLS"
                titulo: "Time Marker Confusion"
                puntos:
                  - "Ensure the time indicators ('now', 'today', 'last semester') match the respective halves of the sentence."
                  - "Use subjunctive 'were' rather than 'was' in formal engineering reports ('If the line were energized...')."
                  - "Do not confuse Third Conditional (pure past) with Mixed (past affecting present)."
              - numero: 5
                seccion: "AUTHENTIC DESIGN DIALOGUE"
                titulo: "Microgrid Feasibility Meeting"
                puntos:
                  - "Project Lead: 'If we were more familiar with hydrogen fuel cells, we would have submitted the grant proposal last Friday.'"
                  - "Consultant: 'And if the university had allocated budget in January, the prototype electrolyzer would be operational today.'"
              - numero: 6
                seccion: "ORAL DRILL"
                titulo: "Transition Practice"
                puntos:
                  - "Convert: 'We did not insulate the pipe. It is cold.' -> 'If we had insulated the steam pipe, it would not be losing thermal energy now.'"
                  - "Convert: 'The sensor is waterproof. It did not short-circuit.' -> 'If the pressure sensor were not waterproof, moisture would have destroyed its circuitry.'"
          - numero_tema: 13
            corte: 3
            modalidad: "general"
            titulo: "Reported Speech in Audits, Safety Inspections & Incident Investigations"
            objetivo: "Transmitir declaraciones técnicas, advertencias de seguridad y hallazgos periciales aplicando las reglas de retrogradación temporal (backshift)."
            concepto_clave_latex: ""
            ejemplo: "The lead safety inspector reported that the main gas turbine had exceeded its permissible vibration threshold during the test run."
            bloque_sugerido: "Speaking Drill 30 min • Technical reporting and witness debriefs"
            slides:
              - numero: 1
                seccion: "CEFR B1 • COMMUNICATIVE PURPOSE"
                titulo: "Reported Speech: Formal Dissemination of Field Findings"
                puntos:
                  - "In engineering practice, oral instructions and witness statements must be formally documented in written logs."
                  - "Shifting from Direct Quote ('The pressure is climbing dangerously') to Indirect Speech ('The technician stated that the pressure was climbing dangerously')."
                  - "Key reporting verbs: stated, reported, confirmed, claimed, warned, emphasized."
                ejemplo: "The environmental officer confirmed that the cooling pond discharged zero hazardous chemicals into the bay."
              - numero: 2
                seccion: "STRUCTURE & PATTERNS"
                titulo: "Tense Backshift Rules"
                puntos:
                  - "Present Simple -> Past Simple: 'The pump operates' -> 'He said the pump operated.'"
                  - "Present Continuous -> Past Continuous: 'The battery is charging' -> 'She reported the battery was charging.'"
                  - "Past Simple / Present Perfect -> Past Perfect: 'We replaced the seal' -> 'They affirmed they had replaced the seal.'"
                  - "Will -> Would, Can -> Could, Must -> Had to."
              - numero: 3
                seccion: "TECHNICAL REPORTING VERBS"
                titulo: "Precision Reporting Beyond 'Said'"
                puntos:
                  - "Warn: The superintendent warned the crew that high-voltage busbars were still energized."
                  - "Recommend: The consultant recommended that the plant upgrade its programmable logic controllers."
                  - "Notice: The field team noticed that the oil level had dropped below the minimum sightline."
              - numero: 4
                seccion: "COMMON ERRORS & PITFALLS"
                titulo: "Pronoun and Time/Place Shifts"
                puntos:
                  - "Shift deictic markers: 'here' -> 'there', 'today' -> 'that day', 'tomorrow' -> 'the following day'."
                  - "No backshift when reporting a universal physical law: 'The professor explained that water boils at 100 degrees Celsius at sea level.'"
                  - "Avoid awkward double negatives in accident reports."
              - numero: 5
                seccion: "AUTHENTIC AUDIT RECORD"
                titulo: "Field Safety Log Excerpt"
                puntos:
                  - "Direct: 'We cannot re-energize the feeder until the lockout tag is officially removed.'"
                  - "Reported: 'The maintenance supervisor emphasized that the crew could not re-energize the feeder until the lockout tag was officially removed.'"
              - numero: 6
                seccion: "ORAL DRILL"
                titulo: "Transforming Field Statements"
                puntos:
                  - "Prompt: 'The harmonic distortion is exceeding IEEE standards.' -> 'The grid analyst reported that harmonic distortion was exceeding IEEE standards.'"
                  - "Prompt: 'We will dispatch an emergency crew at sunrise.' -> 'The dispatcher assured the team that they would dispatch an emergency crew at sunrise.'"
          - numero_tema: 14
            corte: 3
            modalidad: "general"
            titulo: "Passive Voice II: Modal Passives & Causative Structures (Have / Get Done)"
            objetivo: "Describir servicios de mantenimiento externalizados, certificaciones de calibración y mandatos regulatorios utilizando modales pasivos y estructuras causativas."
            concepto_clave_latex: ""
            ejemplo: "The campus substation must be inspected annually by a certified high-voltage contractor, and all protective relays are had calibrated before commissioning."
            bloque_sugerido: "Speaking Drill 30 min • Modal passives & third-party service contracts"
            slides:
              - numero: 1
                seccion: "CEFR B1 • COMMUNICATIVE PURPOSE"
                titulo: "Modal Passives & Causative Constructions in Engineering Management"
                puntos:
                  - "Engineering facilities rarely perform all specialized calibrations in-house; they outsource to certified test laboratories."
                  - "Modal Passive expresses obligation, recommendation, or possibility without naming the contractor: 'The system must be serviced.'"
                  - "Causative (Have / Get + object + past participle) expresses arranging for third-party execution: 'We had the boiler inspected.'"
                ejemplo: "Every three years, Unimagdalena has the solar pyranometers recalibrated by an accredited metrology institute."
              - numero: 2
                seccion: "STRUCTURE & PATTERNS"
                titulo: "Modal Passive Morphological Blueprint"
                puntos:
                  - "Formula: Subject + modal verb (must / should / can / may) + be + past participle (V3)."
                  - "Example 1: 'All confined spaces must be ventilated prior to personnel entry.'"
                  - "Example 2: 'High-frequency noise can be mitigated through passive LC filtering.'"
              - numero: 3
                seccion: "STRUCTURE & PATTERNS"
                titulo: "Causative Blueprint: Have / Get Something Done"
                puntos:
                  - "Formula: Subject + have / get + object + past participle (V3)."
                  - "Professional Formal: 'The plant manager had the vibration sensors checked.'"
                  - "Action-Oriented / Informal: 'We got the backup diesel fuel filters replaced yesterday.'"
              - numero: 4
                seccion: "COMMON ERRORS & PITFALLS"
                titulo: "Active vs. Causative Confusion"
                puntos:
                  - "Incorrect: 'We repaired the ultrasonic transducer' (implies our students did the internal crystal repair)."
                  - "Correct: 'We had the ultrasonic transducer repaired by the manufacturer.'"
                  - "Do not forget 'be' in modal passives: 'The tank must checked' is wrong; write 'must be checked'."
              - numero: 5
                seccion: "AUTHENTIC CONTRACT DIALOGUE"
                titulo: "Substation Commissioning Call"
                puntos:
                  - "Operations Manager: 'Has the utility approved our grid tie-in?'"
                  - "Electrical Engineer: 'Yes, we had the interconnection study certified last week, and all grounding rods should be tested by Monday.'"
              - numero: 6
                seccion: "ORAL DRILL"
                titulo: "Prompt & Transformation"
                puntos:
                  - "Prompt: 'Third party tested the insulation oil.' -> 'We had the transformer insulation oil tested by a laboratory.'"
                  - "Prompt: 'Safety code requires earthing all steel structural members.' -> 'All steel structural members must be earthed according to safety codes.'"
          - numero_tema: 15
            corte: 3
            modalidad: "general"
            titulo: "Academic Abstracts & Executive Summaries for Technical Energy Papers"
            objetivo: "Redactar y sintetizar resúmenes académicos (abstracts) siguiendo la estructura internacional IMRaD (Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion)."
            concepto_clave_latex: ""
            ejemplo: "This study evaluates the performance of a hybrid photovoltaic-thermal collector under Caribbean tropical conditions, demonstrating a 14.2% increase in total energy conversion efficiency."
            bloque_sugerido: "Writing & Presentation 35 min • Crafting an IEEE-style conference abstract"
            slides:
              - numero: 1
                seccion: "CEFR B1 • COMMUNICATIVE PURPOSE"
                titulo: "The Structure of an Engineering Abstract (IMRaD)"
                puntos:
                  - "An abstract is a self-contained, 200-to-250-word synthesis of an entire technical investigation."
                  - "Motivates the reader: Background & Problem Statement (1–2 sentences)."
                  - "Specifies the approach: Methodology & Experimental Setup (2–3 sentences)."
                  - "Highlights the breakthrough: Key Quantitative Results & Conclusions (2–3 sentences)."
                ejemplo: "Energy Engineering undergraduates present their research projects at international conferences using standardized English abstracts."
              - numero: 2
                seccion: "STRUCTURE & PATTERNS"
                titulo: "Verbal Tenses across Abstract Sections"
                puntos:
                  - "Background: Present Simple ('Global energy demand continues to accelerate...')."
                  - "Methodology: Past Simple Passive ('A numerical CFD model was constructed and meshed...')."
                  - "Results: Past Simple / Present Simple ('The prototype achieved a coefficient of performance of 3.8...')."
                  - "Conclusion / Implications: Present Simple / Modals ('These findings demonstrate that solar absorption cooling is economically viable in coastal climates.')."
              - numero: 3
                seccion: "KEY SIGNPOSTING PHRASES"
                titulo: "Formulaic Academic Expressions"
                puntos:
                  - "'This paper proposes a novel dispatch algorithm for...'"
                  - "'Experimental validation was conducted using an instrumented test bench...'"
                  - "'Results indicate a statistically significant reduction in fuel consumption...'"
                  - "'The authors conclude that integrating phase change materials enhances round-trip efficiency.'"
              - numero: 4
                seccion: "COMMON ERRORS & PITFALLS"
                titulo: "Conciseness & Objectivity"
                puntos:
                  - "Never cite bibliographic references or equation numbers directly in an abstract."
                  - "Avoid vague claims: replace 'efficiency was very good' with 'isentropic efficiency improved from 72.1% to 81.4%'."
                  - "Do not use colloquialisms or unsupported future promises."
              - numero: 5
                seccion: "AUTHENTIC ABSTRACT BREAKDOWN"
                titulo: "Unimagdalena Clean Energy Case Study"
                puntos:
                  - "Title: 'Thermo-hydraulic characterization of microchannel heat exchangers for waste heat recovery.'"
                  - "Key Result: 'An overall heat transfer coefficient of 1,850 W/(m²·K) was obtained with an allowable pressure drop below 12 kPa.'"
              - numero: 6
                seccion: "ORAL DRILL"
                titulo: "Elevator Pitch from Abstract"
                puntos:
                  - "Summarize your senior capstone project in 60 seconds using the 4-part formula: 'My research addresses [Problem] by [Method], which achieved [Result], proving that [Impact].'"
          - numero_tema: 16
            corte: 1
            modalidad: "notacion_ingenieria"
            titulo: "Limits & Continuity Verbalization"
            objetivo: "Leer rigurosamente límites laterales, límites al infinito y condiciones de continuidad en inglés académico."
            concepto_clave_latex: "\\lim_{x \\to a^+} f(x) = L \\quad ; \\quad \\lim_{t \\to \\infty} e^{-t/\\tau} = 0 \\quad ; \\quad \\lim_{x \\to c} f(x) = f(c)"
            verbalizacion_ingles: "• lim_{x -> a⁺} f(x) = L -> \"the limit of f of x as x approaches a from the right (or from above) equals L\" (for a⁻: \"from the left / from below\").\n• lim_{t -> ∞} e^(-t/τ) = 0 -> \"the limit as t approaches infinity (or tends to infinity) of e to the minus t over tau equals zero\".\n• Continuity: \"f is continuous at c if the limit of f of x as x approaches c equals f of c\"."
            ejemplo: "Exposición del estado estacionario térmico cuando t -> ∞: 'As time tends to infinity, the transient exponential term vanishes'."
            bloque_sugerido: "Calculus Speech 30 min • Verbalizing limits & asymptotic steady states"
          - numero_tema: 17
            corte: 1
            modalidad: "notacion_ingenieria"
            titulo: "Ordinary & Partial Derivatives (Leibniz & Lagrange Notation)"
            objetivo: "Verbalizar derivadas ordinarias, segundas derivadas, notación prima/punto y derivadas parciales."
            concepto_clave_latex: "\\frac{dy}{dx} = f'(x) \\quad ; \\quad a = \\frac{d^2x}{dt^2} = \\ddot{x} \\quad ; \\quad \\left(\\frac{\\partial P}{\\partial T}\\right)_V = \\frac{nR}{V}"
            verbalizacion_ingles: "• dy/dx -> \"d y by d x\" or \"d y over d x\" or formally \"the first derivative of y with respect to x\".\n• f'(x), f''(x) -> \"f prime of x\", \"f double prime of x\"  |  ẋ, ẍ -> \"x dot\", \"x double dot\" (time derivatives).\n• d²x/dt² -> \"d squared x by d t squared\" (\"the second derivative of x with respect to t\").\n• (∂P/∂T)_V -> \"the partial derivative of P with respect to T at constant volume V\" (or \"partial P over partial T, holding V constant\")."
            ejemplo: "Lectura de relaciones termodinámicas de Maxwell y tasas de transferencia de calor dQ/dt ('Q dot')."
            bloque_sugerido: "Derivative Fluency 35 min • Leibniz, Lagrange, Newton-dot & partials aloud"
          - numero_tema: 18
            corte: 2
            modalidad: "notacion_ingenieria"
            titulo: "Indefinite & Definite Integrals"
            objetivo: "Pronunciar integrales indefinidas, integrales definidas con límites e integrales de línea o superficie cerradas."
            concepto_clave_latex: "\\int f(x)\\,dx = F(x) + C \\quad ; \\quad E = \\int_{t_1}^{t_2} P(t)\\,dt \\quad ; \\quad \\oint \\vec{E}\\cdot d\\vec{l} = -\\frac{d\\Phi_B}{dt}"
            verbalizacion_ingles: "• ∫ f(x) dx = F(x) + C -> \"the indefinite integral of f of x d x equals capital F of x plus a constant of integration C\".\n• ∫_{t₁}^{t₂} P(t) dt -> \"the definite integral from t sub one to t sub two of P of t d t\".\n• ∮ E · dl = -dΦ_B/dt -> \"the closed line integral (or contour integral) of vector E dot d l equals minus d Phi sub B by d t\"."
            ejemplo: "Explicación oral en inglés de cómo la energía eléctrica facturada es la integral definida de la potencia activa en el tiempo."
            bloque_sugerido: "Integral Reading 30 min • Definite bounds & Faraday's closed-loop integral"
          - numero_tema: 19
            corte: 2
            modalidad: "notacion_ingenieria"
            titulo: "Electric Circuits & Phasor Notation"
            objetivo: "Leer impedancias complejas, valores eficaces RMS y fasores de tensión/corriente en régimen AC."
            concepto_clave_latex: "Z = R + jX_L \\quad ; \\quad V_{\\text{rms}} = \\frac{V_m}{\\sqrt{2}} \\quad ; \\quad \\tilde{V} = V_0 \\angle \\phi = V_0 e^{j\\phi}"
            verbalizacion_ingles: "• Z = R + j X_L -> \"complex impedance Z equals resistance R plus j times inductive reactance X sub L\" (in Electrical Engineering, j is used instead of i to avoid confusion with current!).\n• V_rms = V_m / √2 -> \"V r-m-s (root-mean-square voltage) equals peak voltage V sub m over the square root of two\".\n• Ṽ = V₀ ∠ φ -> \"phasor V tilde equals V naught at an angle of phi\"."
            ejemplo: "Defensa oral de un análisis fasorial de circuito monofásico a 60 Hz indicando desfase inductivo ('lagging power factor')."
            bloque_sugerido: "AC Phasor Speech 35 min • Complex impedance, RMS & polar phasor reading"
          - numero_tema: 20
            corte: 3
            modalidad: "notacion_ingenieria"
            titulo: "Summations, Products & Series"
            objetivo: "Verbalizar notación sigma de sumatorias, productorias pi y expansiones en series de potencias o Fourier."
            concepto_clave_latex: "\\bar{x} = \\frac{1}{n}\\sum_{i=1}^{n} x_i \\quad ; \\quad \\eta_{\\text{sys}} = \\prod_{k=1}^{m} \\eta_k \\quad ; \\quad e^x = \\sum_{n=0}^{\\infty} \\frac{x^n}{n!}"
            verbalizacion_ingles: "• Σ_{i=1}^n x_i -> \"the sum from i equals one to n of x sub i\".\n• Π_{k=1}^m η_k -> \"the product from k equals one to m of eta sub k\".\n• Σ_{n=0}^∞ x^n / n! -> \"the infinite sum from n equals zero to infinity of x to the n over n factorial\"."
            ejemplo: "Eficiencia global de una cadena energética (caldera × turbina × generador × transformador) leída como productoria Π η_k."
            bloque_sugerido: "Series & Sigma Drill 30 min • Discrete sums, factorials & cascaded efficiencies"
          - numero_tema: 21
            corte: 3
            modalidad: "notacion_ingenieria"
            titulo: "Complex Numbers, Euler's Identity & Harmonic Waveforms"
            objetivo: "Expresar señales sinusoidales en el dominio del tiempo, frecuencia angular, conjugados complejos y fórmula de Euler."
            concepto_clave_latex: "e^{j\\omega t} = \\cos(\\omega t) + j\\sin(\\omega t) \\quad ; \\quad v(t) = V_m\\cos(\\omega t + \\theta_v) \\quad ; \\quad S = \\tilde{V}\\tilde{I}^*"
            verbalizacion_ingles: "• e^(jωt) = cos(ωt) + j sin(ωt) -> \"e to the j omega t equals cosine of omega t plus j sine of omega t\".\n• v(t) = V_m cos(ωt + θ_v) -> \"instantaneous voltage v of t equals V sub m cosine of quantity omega t plus theta sub v\".\n• S = Ṽ Ĩ* -> \"complex power S equals phasor V times the complex conjugate of phasor I (I star)\"."
            ejemplo: "Presentación de potencia compleja trifásica usando el conjugado fasorial de corriente ('I conjugate' o 'I star')."
            bloque_sugerido: "Harmonic Notation 30 min • Euler's identity & complex conjugate power"
          - numero_tema: 22
            corte: 3
            modalidad: "notacion_ingenieria"
            verbalizacion_ingles: "• V_dot = A * v -> \"volumetric flow rate V dot equals cross-sectional area A times average fluid velocity v, in cubic meters per second\".
• m_dot = rho * A * v -> \"mass flow rate m dot equals fluid density rho times area times velocity, in kilograms per second\".
• A_1 * v_1 = A_2 * v_2 -> \"area one times velocity one equals area two times velocity two for steady incompressible flow\"."
            titulo: "Fluid Dynamics, Continuity Equation & Volumetric Flow Rate"
            objetivo: "Articular la ecuación de continuidad para flujo incompresible, caudal volumétrico y conservación de masa en fluidos."
            concepto_clave_latex: "\\dot{V} = A v \\quad [\\text{m}^3/\\text{s}] \\quad ; \\quad \\dot{m} = \\rho A v = \\rho \\dot{V} \\quad [\\text{kg/s}] \\quad ; \\quad A_1 v_1 = A_2 v_2"
            ejemplo: "En tuberías de carga hidroeléctrica: 'The volumetric flow rate into the penstock is thirty-two point five cubic meters per second, accelerating the water velocity as pipe diameter narrows'."
            bloque_sugerido: "Speaking Drill 30 min • Continuity equation and mass flow rate verbalization"
          - numero_tema: 23
            corte: 3
            modalidad: "notacion_ingenieria"
            verbalizacion_ingles: "• P_1 + 1/2 rho v_1^2 + rho g z_1 -> \"static pressure P sub one plus one-half rho v one squared plus rho g z one equals constant along a streamline, in pascals\".
• P/gamma + v^2/(2g) + z = H -> \"pressure head P over gamma plus velocity head v squared over two g plus elevation head z equals total hydraulic head H, in meters\"."
            titulo: "Bernoulli's Equation, Pressure Head & Piezometric Head"
            objetivo: "Verbalizar la conservación de energía mecánica en fluidos ideales a lo largo de una línea de corriente en unidades de presión y altura de columna."
            concepto_clave_latex: "P_1 + \\frac{1}{2}\\rho v_1^2 + \\rho g z_1 = P_2 + \\frac{1}{2}\\rho v_2^2 + \\rho g z_2 \\quad ; \\quad \\frac{P_1}{\\gamma} + \\frac{v_1^2}{2g} + z_1 = \\frac{P_2}{\\gamma} + \\frac{v_2^2}{2g} + z_2 = H"
            ejemplo: "En el análisis de un tubo de Venturi: 'The drop in piezometric head between the inlet and the throat yields the differential pressure required to compute flow velocity'."
            bloque_sugerido: "Technical Discussion 30 min • Bernoulli's equation, pressure head and kinetic head"
          - numero_tema: 24
            corte: 3
            modalidad: "notacion_ingenieria"
            verbalizacion_ingles: "• Re = (rho * v * D) / mu -> \"Reynolds number equals fluid density rho times velocity v times internal diameter D divided by dynamic viscosity mu, dimensionless\".
• h_f = f * (L / D) * (v^2 / (2g)) -> \"frictional head loss h sub f equals Darcy friction factor f times pipe length over diameter times velocity squared over two g, in meters\".
• f_lam = 64 / Re -> \"for laminar flow with Reynolds number below two thousand three hundred, the friction factor equals sixty-four divided by Re\"."
            titulo: "Reynolds Number, Viscous Regimes & Darcy-Weisbach Friction Factor"
            objetivo: "Expresar regímenes de flujo (laminar vs. turbulento), viscosidad cinemática y pérdidas por fricción en tuberías en inglés técnico."
            concepto_clave_latex: "Re = \\frac{\\rho v D}{\\mu} = \\frac{v D}{\\nu} \\quad [-] \\quad ; \\quad h_f = f \\frac{L}{D} \\frac{v^2}{2g} \\quad [\\text{m}] \\quad ; \\quad f_{lam} = \\frac{64}{Re}"
            ejemplo: "En circuitos de bombeo geotérmico: 'Because the Reynolds number exceeds forty thousand, the flow regime is fully turbulent, requiring the Colebrook-White correlation'."
            bloque_sugerido: "Speaking Drill 30 min • Reynolds number, turbulent regimes and head loss"
          - numero_tema: 25
            corte: 3
            modalidad: "notacion_ingenieria"
            verbalizacion_ingles: "• P(z) = P_0 + rho g h -> \"hydrostatic pressure at depth h equals ambient pressure P nought plus density rho times gravitational acceleration g times depth h, in pascals\".
• Delta P = rho_m g Delta h -> \"differential pressure equals manometric fluid density times g times deflection height Delta h\".
• F_1 / A_1 = F_2 / A_2 -> \"input force over input area equals output force over output area in a hydraulic actuator\"."
            titulo: "Hydrostatic Pressure, Pascal's Law & Manometry Calculations"
            objetivo: "Articular presión estática en profundidades sumergidas, principio de transmisión de presión en fluidos confinados y lectura manométrica diferencial."
            concepto_clave_latex: "P(z) = P_0 + \\rho g h \\quad [\\text{Pa}] \\quad ; \\quad \\Delta P = \\rho_m g \\Delta h \\quad ; \\quad \\frac{F_1}{A_1} = \\frac{F_2}{A_2} \\implies F_2 = F_1 \\left(\\frac{A_2}{A_1}\\right)"
            ejemplo: "En compuertas de presas hidroeléctricas: 'The total hydrostatic force acting on the vertical sluice gate equals fluid specific weight times gate centroid depth times submerged gate area'."
            bloque_sugerido: "Technical Dialogue 30 min • Hydrostatic pressure, Pascal's law and hydraulic actuators"
          - numero_tema: 26
            corte: 3
            modalidad: "notacion_ingenieria"
            verbalizacion_ingles: "• Q_dot - W_dot_cv = sum(m_dot_out * (h_out + v_out^2/2 + g z_out)) - sum(m_dot_in * (h_in + v_in^2/2 + g z_in)) -> \"rate of net heat input Q dot minus shaft power W dot sub control volume equals total enthalpy, kinetic, and potential energy exiting minus entering the boundary, in kilowatts\"."
            titulo: "First Law of Thermodynamics for Open Control Volumes (SFEE)"
            objetivo: "Verbalizar la ecuación de conservación de energía para volúmenes de control en régimen estacionario (turbinas, compresores y toberas)."
            concepto_clave_latex: "\\dot{Q} - \\dot{W}_{cv} = \\sum_{out} \\dot{m}_e \\left(h_e + \\frac{v_e^2}{2} + g z_e\\right) - \\sum_{in} \\dot{m}_i \\left(h_i + \\frac{v_i^2}{2} + g z_i\\right) \\quad [\\text{kW}]"
            ejemplo: "En una turbina de vapor adiabática: 'Assuming zero heat loss and negligible kinetic changes, the turbine shaft work equals mass flow rate times specific enthalpy drop: W dot equals m dot times quantity h inlet minus h exit'."
            bloque_sugerido: "Speaking Drill 30 min • Steady-flow energy equation and enthalpy verbalization"
          - numero_tema: 27
            corte: 3
            modalidad: "notacion_ingenieria"
            verbalizacion_ingles: "• P * V = n * R_u * T -> \"pressure times volume equals number of moles n times universal gas constant R sub u times absolute temperature T in kelvins\".
• P * v = R * T -> \"pressure times specific volume v equals specific gas constant R times temperature\".
• Z = (P * v) / (R * T) -> \"compressibility factor Z equals P v over R T, deviating from unity as gas pressure approaches critical state\".
• P * v^n = const -> \"polytropic process equation P times specific volume to the power n equals constant\"."
            titulo: "Ideal Gas Law, Compressibility Factor Z & Polytropic Processes"
            objetivo: "Expresar ecuaciones de estado de gases ideales y reales, factor de compresibilidad y transformaciones politrópicas de compresión/expansión."
            concepto_clave_latex: "P V = n R_u T \\quad ; \\quad P v = R T \\quad ; \\quad Z = \\frac{P v}{R T} \\quad [-] \\quad ; \\quad P v^n = \\text{const}"
            ejemplo: "En compresión de biogás: 'At twelve megapascals, methane deviates from ideal gas behavior, exhibiting a compressibility factor Z of approximately zero point eight-eight'."
            bloque_sugerido: "Technical Discussion 30 min • Ideal gas law, Z factor and polytropic compression"
          - numero_tema: 28
            corte: 3
            modalidad: "notacion_ingenieria"
            verbalizacion_ingles: "• eta_Carnot = 1 - T_L / T_H -> \"Carnot thermal efficiency equals one minus absolute temperature of the cold sink T sub L divided by hot source T sub H\".
• dS = delta Q_rev / T -> \"differential entropy dS equals reversible heat transfer delta Q divided by thermodynamic temperature T, in kilojoules per kelvin\".
• S_dot_gen >= 0 -> \"rate of entropy generation S dot gen is strictly greater than or equal to zero for all spontaneous real processes according to the Second Law\"."
            titulo: "Second Law of Thermodynamics, Entropy Generation & Carnot Limit"
            objetivo: "Verbalizar entropía, generación de entropía por irreversibilidades y eficiencia térmica máxima de ciclos termodinámicos."
            concepto_clave_latex: "\\eta_{th, Carnot} = 1 - \\frac{T_L}{T_H} \\quad ; \\quad dS = \\frac{\\delta Q_{rev}}{T} \\quad ; \\quad \\dot{S}_{gen} = \\frac{dS_{sys}}{dt} - \\sum \\frac{\\dot{Q}_k}{T_k} - \\sum \\dot{m}_i s_i + \\sum \\dot{m}_e s_e \\ge 0"
            ejemplo: "En ciclos combinados de gas y vapor: 'The maximum theoretical efficiency is capped by the Carnot limit between the combustion temperature and the ambient cooling water temperature'."
            bloque_sugerido: "Speaking Drill 30 min • Second law of thermodynamics, entropy generation and Carnot limit"
          - numero_tema: 29
            corte: 3
            modalidad: "notacion_ingenieria"
            verbalizacion_ingles: "• Q_dot_cond = -k * A * (dT / dx) -> \"conductive heat transfer rate Q dot equals minus thermal conductivity k times surface area A times temperature gradient dT over dx, in watts\".
• R_th_cond = L / (k * A) -> \"conductive thermal resistance equals wall thickness L divided by thermal conductivity k times area A, in kelvins per watt\".
• Q_dot = Delta T / R_th_total -> \"heat flow equals overall temperature difference Delta T divided by total equivalent thermal resistance\"."
            titulo: "Fourier's Law of Thermal Conduction & 1D Thermal Resistance Networks"
            objetivo: "Expresar la ley de conducción térmica de Fourier, gradiente de temperatura unidimensional y analogía de circuitos de resistencia térmica."
            concepto_clave_latex: "\\dot{Q}_{cond} = -k A \\frac{dT}{dx} \\quad [\\text{W}] \\quad ; \\quad R_{th, cond} = \\frac{L}{k A} \\quad [\\text{K/W}] \\quad ; \\quad \\dot{Q} = \\frac{\\Delta T}{R_{th, total}}"
            ejemplo: "En aislamiento de colectores solares térmicos: 'The heat loss through the mineral wool insulation is calculated as the temperature drop divided by the sum of conductive and convective resistances'."
            bloque_sugerido: "Technical Dialogue 30 min • Fourier's law and thermal resistance networks"
          - numero_tema: 30
            corte: 3
            modalidad: "notacion_ingenieria"
            verbalizacion_ingles: "• Q_dot_conv = h * A * (T_s - T_infinity) -> \"convective heat transfer rate equals convection heat transfer coefficient h times area A times surface temperature T sub s minus fluid ambient temperature T infinity, in watts\".
• Q_dot_rad = epsilon * sigma * A * (T_s^4 - T_surr^4) -> \"radiative heat transfer rate equals surface emissivity epsilon times Stefan-Boltzmann constant sigma times area times the difference of fourth powers of surface and surrounding absolute temperatures\"."
            titulo: "Newton's Law of Cooling & Stefan-Boltzmann Surface Radiation"
            objetivo: "Articular transferencia de calor por convección y radiación térmica superficial de cuerpos negros y grises."
            concepto_clave_latex: "\\dot{Q}_{conv} = h A (T_s - T_\\infty) \\quad [\\text{W}] \\quad ; \\quad \\dot{Q}_{rad} = \\varepsilon \\sigma A (T_s^4 - T_{surr}^4) \\quad [\\text{W}] \\quad ; \\quad \\sigma = 5.670 \\times 10^{-8} \\ \\frac{\\text{W}}{\\text{m}^2 \\text{K}^4}"
            ejemplo: "En disipadores de inversores fotovoltaicos: 'Natural convection accounts for seventy percent of heat dissipation, while thirty percent is radiated to the ambient enclosure'."
            bloque_sugerido: "Speaking Drill 30 min • Convection coefficient, Stefan-Boltzmann law and emissivity"

  - cuatrimestre: 4
    creditos_totales: 15
    asignaturas:
      - codigo: "02011809"
        nombre: "Álgebra Lineal"
        creditos: 3
        obligatoria: true
        categoria: "MATEMATICAS"
        color: "#5E5CE6"
        temas:
          - numero_tema: 1
            corte: 1
            modalidad: "tecnica"
            titulo: "Sistemas de Ecuaciones Lineales y Eliminación Gaussiana"
            objetivo: "Resolver sistemas lineales de gran escala mediante reducción por filas Gauss-Jordan."
            concepto_clave_latex: "A\\vec{x} = \\vec{b} \\quad ; \\quad [A \\mid \\vec{b}] \\xrightarrow{\\text{RREF}} [I \\mid \\vec{x}]"
            ejemplo: "Solución de corrientes de malla en una red eléctrica de distribución."
            bloque_sugerido: "Pomodoro 50/10 • Gauss-Jordan"
          - numero_tema: 2
            corte: 1
            modalidad: "tecnica"
            titulo: "Álgebra Matricial, Inversas y Factorización LU"
            objetivo: "Operar matrices particionadas, calcular inversas y descomponer A = LU."
            concepto_clave_latex: "A = L U \\quad ; \\quad L\\vec{y} = \\vec{b},\\;\\; U\\vec{x} = \\vec{y} \\quad ; \\quad (AB)^{-1} = B^{-1}A^{-1}"
            ejemplo: "Reutilización de factorización LU en simulaciones horarias de flujo DC."
            bloque_sugerido: "Práctica 45 min • Descomposición LU"
          - numero_tema: 3
            corte: 1
            modalidad: "tecnica"
            titulo: "Determinantes, Propiedades y Regla de Cramer"
            objetivo: "Evaluar invertibilidad matricial y sensibilidad mediante determinantes y cofactores."
            concepto_clave_latex: "\\det(A) = \\sum_{j=1}^{n}(-1)^{i+j}a_{ij}M_{ij} \\quad ; \\quad \\det(A) \\neq 0 \\iff A\\text{ es invertible}"
            ejemplo: "Verificación de no singularidad del Jacobiano en Newton-Raphson."
            bloque_sugerido: "Pomodoro 45/10 • Cofactores y Jacobiano"
          - numero_tema: 4
            corte: 2
            modalidad: "tecnica"
            titulo: "Espacios Vectoriales, Subespacios, Base y Dimensión"
            objetivo: "Determinar independencia lineal, espacio columna, espacio nulo y rango."
            concepto_clave_latex: "\\dim(\\text{Col } A) + \\dim(\\text{Nul } A) = n \\quad ; \\quad \\text{rango}(A) = \\dim(\\text{Col } A)"
            ejemplo: "Identificación de grados de libertad independientes en balances estequiométricos."
            bloque_sugerido: "Pomodoro 50/10 • Teorema rango-nulidad"
          - numero_tema: 5
            corte: 2
            modalidad: "tecnica"
            titulo: "Transformaciones Lineales y Cambio de Base"
            objetivo: "Representar operadores lineales matricialmente y transformar coordenadas."
            concepto_clave_latex: "T(\\alpha\\vec{u} + \\beta\\vec{v}) = \\alpha T(\\vec{u}) + \\beta T(\\vec{v}) \\quad ; \\quad [\\vec{x}]_{\\mathcal{B}} = P_{\\mathcal{B}}^{-1}\\vec{x}"
            ejemplo: "Transformación de Clarke y Park (abc -> dq0) en control de inversores trifásicos."
            bloque_sugerido: "Práctica 50 min • Transformada dq0"
          - numero_tema: 6
            corte: 2
            modalidad: "tecnica"
            titulo: "Ortogonalidad, Proceso de Gram-Schmidt y Factorización QR"
            objetivo: "Construir bases ortonormales y proyecciones ortogonales estables."
            concepto_clave_latex: "\\text{proy}_W\\vec{y} = \\sum_{i=1}^{k}(\\vec{y}\\cdot\\vec{u}_i)\\vec{u}_i \\quad ; \\quad A = Q R\\;\\;(Q^T Q = I)"
            ejemplo: "Descomposición ortogonal de armónicos de corriente en calidad de potencia."
            bloque_sugerido: "Pomodoro 50/10 • Gram-Schmidt y QR"
          - numero_tema: 7
            corte: 3
            modalidad: "tecnica"
            titulo: "Mínimos Cuadrados Lineales y Estimación de Estado"
            objetivo: "Ajustar sistemas sobredeterminados minimizando la norma euclidiana del residual."
            concepto_clave_latex: "\\hat{x} = (A^T A)^{-1}A^T\\vec{b} \\quad ; \\quad \\|\\vec{b} - A\\hat{x}\\|_2 = \\min"
            ejemplo: "Estimación de estado nodal en redes eléctricas con mediciones redundantes SCADA."
            bloque_sugerido: "Práctica 45 min • Ecuaciones normales"
          - numero_tema: 8
            corte: 3
            modalidad: "tecnica"
            titulo: "Valores y Vectores Propios y Diagonalización"
            objetivo: "Calcular el espectro de matrices para desacoplar sistemas dinámicos lineales."
            concepto_clave_latex: "A\\vec{v} = \\lambda\\vec{v} \\quad ; \\quad \\det(A - \\lambda I) = 0 \\quad ; \\quad A = P D P^{-1}"
            ejemplo: "Modos naturales de oscilación electromecánica entre generadores síncronos."
            bloque_sugerido: "Pomodoro 50/10 • Autovalores y estabilidad"
          - numero_tema: 9
            corte: 3
            modalidad: "tecnica"
            titulo: "Matrices Simétricas, Formas Cuadráticas y SVD"
            objetivo: "Aplicar diagonalización ortogonal y descomposición en valores singulares."
            concepto_clave_latex: "A = U \\Sigma V^T \\quad ; \\quad Q(\\vec{x}) = \\vec{x}^T A \\vec{x} > 0\\;\\;(\\text{definida positiva})"
            ejemplo: "Reducción de dimensionalidad SVD en mapas espacio-temporales de viento."
            bloque_sugerido: "Taller 45 min • Formas cuadráticas y SVD"
          - numero_tema: 10
            corte: 2
            modalidad: "teorico"
            titulo: "Descomposición en Valores Singulares (SVD) y Pseudoinversa de Moore-Penrose"
            objetivo: "Dominar la descomposición SVD $A = U \\Sigma V^T$ y el cálculo de la pseudoinversa de Moore-Penrose $A^+$ para la resolución óptima de sistemas lineales sobredeterminados e indeterminados."
            concepto_clave_latex: "A = U \\Sigma V^T = \\sum_{i=1}^r \\sigma_i \\mathbf{u}_i \\mathbf{v}_i^T \\quad ; \\quad A^+ = V \\Sigma^+ U^T \\quad [\\sigma_1 \\ge \\sigma_2 \\ge \\dots \\ge \\sigma_r > 0]"
            ejemplo: "Problema 1: Dada la matriz $A = \\begin{pmatrix} 3 & 0 \\\\ 0 & -2 \\end{pmatrix}$, hallar sus valores singulares y pseudoinversa. Calculamos $A^T A = \\begin{pmatrix} 9 & 0 \\\\ 0 & 4 \\end{pmatrix}$, con autovalores $\\lambda_1 = 9, \\lambda_2 = 4$, por lo que $\\sigma_1 = 3, \\sigma_2 = 2$. Así $U = \\begin{pmatrix} 1 & 0 \\\\ 0 & -1 \\end{pmatrix}, V = I$, y $A^+ = \\begin{pmatrix} 1/3 & 0 \\\\ 0 & -1/2 \\end{pmatrix}$. Problema 2: En un sistema de estimación de estado $A\\mathbf{x} = \\mathbf{b}$ con rango deficiente, la solución de norma euclidiana mínima única es $\\hat{\\mathbf{x}} = A^+ \\mathbf{b}$."
            bloque_sugerido: "Taller SVD 45 min • Factorización singular y pseudoinversa en MATLAB/Python"
            slides:
              - numero: 1
                seccion: "FUNDAMENTOS MATRICIALES"
                titulo: "Estructura Geométrica de la SVD"
                puntos:
                  - "Toda matriz real $A \\in \\mathbb{R}^{m \\times n}$ mapea esferas unitarias de $\\mathbb{R}^n$ en hiperelipsoides en $\\mathbb{R}^m$."
                  - "Las columnas de $V$ son autovectores ortonormales de $A^T A$, mientras que las columnas de $U$ lo son de $A A^T$."
                  - "Los valores singulares $\\sigma_i = \\sqrt{\\lambda_i(A^T A)}$ representan las longitudes de los semiejes del elipsoide resultante."
              - numero: 2
                seccion: "OPTIMIZACIÓN Y PSEUDOINVERSA"
                titulo: "Propiedades de Moore-Penrose"
                puntos:
                  - "La matriz pseudoinversa satisface las 4 condiciones de Penrose: $A A^+ A = A$, $A^+ A A^+ = A^+$, $(AA^+)^T = AA^+$, $(A^+ A)^T = A^+ A$."
                  - "Permite comprimir datos y matrices de impedancia reteniendo los $k$ valores singulares dominantes (Teorema de Eckart-Young-Mirsky)."
                  - "Garantiza soluciones estables incluso cuando $\\det(A^T A) \\approx 0$ mediante truncamiento de valores singulares (TSVD)."
          - numero_tema: 11
            corte: 2
            modalidad: "teorico"
            titulo: "Teorema de Cayley-Hamilton y Cálculo de Funciones Matriciales"
            objetivo: "Aplicar el Teorema de Cayley-Hamilton para expresar polinomios y potencias de matrices $A^k$ en función de potencias de orden menor que $n$, simplificando la evaluación de operadores dinámicos."
            concepto_clave_latex: "p(\\lambda) = \\det(\\lambda I - A) = 0 \\implies p(A) = A^n + c_{n-1}A^{n-1} + \\dots + c_1 A + c_0 I = \\mathbf{0}"
            ejemplo: "Problema 1: Sea $A = \\begin{pmatrix} 1 & 2 \\\\ 3 & 4 \\end{pmatrix}$. El polinomio característico es $p(\\lambda) = \\lambda^2 - 5\\lambda - 2$. Por Cayley-Hamilton: $A^2 - 5A - 2I = 0 \\implies A^2 = 5A + 2I$. Hallar $A^3$: $A^3 = 5A^2 + 2A = 5(5A + 2I) + 2A = 27A + 10I = \\begin{pmatrix} 37 & 54 \\\\ 81 & 118 \\end{pmatrix}$. Problema 2: Inversa mediante Cayley-Hamilton: $A(A - 5I) = 2I \\implies A^{-1} = \\frac{1}{2}(A - 5I) = \\frac{1}{2}\\begin{pmatrix} -4 & 2 \\\\ 3 & -1 \\end{pmatrix} = \\begin{pmatrix} -2 & 1 \\\\ 1.5 & -0.5 \\end{pmatrix}$."
            bloque_sugerido: "Cálculo Simbólico 40 min • Potencias matriciales y verificación con Cayley-Hamilton"
            slides:
              - numero: 1
