Calcular la frecuencia de resonancia del modo fundamental $TE_{101}$ ($m=1, n=0, p=1$): $f_0 = \\frac{3 \\times 10^8}{2} \\sqrt{\\frac{1^2}{0.05^2} + 0 + \\frac{1^2}{0.05^2}} = 1.5 \\times 10^8 \\times \\frac{\\sqrt{2}}{0.05} = 1.5 \\times 10^8 \\times 28.284 = 4.243 \\times 10^9\\text{ Hz} = 4.243\\text{ GHz}$. Problema 2: En cavidades de cobre bien pulidas, el factor de calidad alcanza $Q \\approx 10000 - 30000$, proporcionando un ancho de banda extremadamente estrecho $\\Delta f = f_0 / Q \\approx 140\\text{ kHz}$, ideal como filtro pasabanda o cámara de magnetrón de microondas."
            bloque_sugerido: "Resonancia EM 40 min • Modos de cavidad y factor de calidad Q cargado vs descargado"
            slides:
              - numero: 1
                seccion: "CIRCUITO RESONANTE 3D"
                titulo: "Almacenamiento Confinado"
                puntos:
                  - "Equivalente electromagnético tridimensional distribuido de un circuito tanque LC."
                  - "En la frecuencia de resonancia exacta $\\omega_0$, la energía eléctrica media almacenada en el volumen es idéntica a la magnética: $\\langle U_e \\rangle = \\langle U_m \\rangle$."
                  - "Las corrientes inducidas de radiofrecuencia circulan por una capa superficial de espesor $\\delta_s$ en las paredes metálicas internas."
              - numero: 2
                seccion: "SUPERCONDUCTIVIDAD RF"
                titulo: "Cavidades de Niobio Superconductor"
                puntos:
                  - "Enfriadas a 2 K con helio líquido, la resistencia superficial cae a nano-ohmios, logrando factores de calidad $Q > 10^9 - 10^{10}$."
                  - "Permiten generar gradientes de aceleración de más de 35 MV/m en aceleradores de partículas de radiación sincrotrón."
                  - "Sustentan fuentes de radiación utilizadas en la caracterización cuántica de nuevos materiales energéticos."
          - numero_tema: 22
            corte: 3
            modalidad: "teorico"
            titulo: "Circuitos Magnéticos, Histéresis y Pérdidas de Foucault en Núcleos"
            objetivo: "Modelar circuitos magnéticos aplicando analogías de Ohm con reluctancia $\\mathcal{R}$, calculando pérdidas por histéresis de Steinmetz y pérdidas por corrientes de Foucault."
            concepto_clave_latex: "\\mathcal{F} = N I = \\Phi \\mathcal{R} \\quad ; \\quad \\mathcal{R} = \\frac{l}{\\mu A} \\quad ; \\quad P_{fe} = P_h + P_e = k_h f B_{\\max}^n + k_e f^2 t_{lam}^2 B_{\\max}^2"
            ejemplo: "Problema 1: Un núcleo de acero al silicio laminado tiene una longitud media de $l_c = 0.5\\text{ m}$, sección $A = 20\\text{ cm}^2 = 2 \\times 10^{-3}\\text{ m}^2$, permeabilidad relativa $\\mu_r = 2500$ y un entrehierro de aire de $l_g = 1.0\\text{ mm}$. Devanado de $N = 400$ espiras. Reluctancia del núcleo de acero: $\\mathcal{R}_c = \\frac{0.5}{2500 \\times 4\\pi \\times 10^{-7} \\times 2 \\times 10^{-3}} = \\frac{0.5}{6.283 \\times 10^{-6}} = 79577\\text{ A-v/Wb}$. Reluctancia del entrehierro de aire: $\\mathcal{R}_g = \\frac{1.0 \\times 10^{-3}}{4\\pi \\times 10^{-7} \\times 2 \\times 10^{-3}} = \\frac{1.0 \\times 10^{-3}}{2.513 \\times 10^{-9}} = 397887\\text{ A-v/Wb}$. Reluctancia total: $\\mathcal{R}_T = 79577 + 397887 = 477464\\text{ A-v/Wb}$. El entrehierro de 1 mm aporta el $83.3\\%$ de la resistencia al flujo. Para un flujo de $\\Phi = 2.4\\text{ mWb}$, la corriente requerida es $I = \\frac{\\Phi \\mathcal{R}_T}{N} = \\frac{0.0024 \\times 477464}{400} = 2.86\\text{ A}$. Problema 2: Laminar el núcleo en láminas de espesor $t_{lam} = 0.35\\text{ mm}$ aisladas con barniz carlite reduce las corrientes de Foucault proporcionalmente a $t_{lam}^2$, disminuyendo las pérdidas en más del $90\\%$."
            bloque_sugerido: "Máquinas Eléctricas 45 min • Ciclos B-H de histéresis y separación de pérdidas en el hierro"
            slides:
              - numero: 1
                seccion: "ANALOGÍA MAGNÉTICA DE HOPKINSON"
                titulo: "Fuerza Magnetomotriz y Reluctancia"
                puntos:
                  - "Fuerza Magnetomotriz $\\mathcal{F} = N I$ análoga al voltaje $V$."
                  - "Flujo magnético $\\Phi = \\iint \\mathbf{B} \\cdot d\\mathbf{A}$ análogo a la corriente eléctrica $I$."
                  - "Reluctancia $\\mathcal{R} = \\frac{l}{\\mu A}$ análoga a la resistencia eléctrica $R$."
                  - "Permeancia $\\mathcal{P} = 1/\\mathcal{R}$ análoga a la conductancia $G$."
              - numero: 2
                seccion: "PÉRDIDAS EN EL HIERRO"
                titulo: "Histéresis y Corrientes Parásitas"
                puntos:
                  - "Pérdidas por Histéresis: Área encerrada por el lazo $B-H$ en cada ciclo de magnetización alternada ($W_h = \\oint H dB$)."
                  - "Pérdidas de Foucault (Eddy Currents): Corrientes microscópicas en bucle inducidas por $\\frac{\\partial B}{\\partial t}$ dentro del material conductor del núcleo."
                  - "Uso de aceros eléctricos de grano orientado (GOES) para optimizar transformadores de distribución."
          - numero_tema: 23
            corte: 3
            modalidad: "teorico"
            titulo: "Efecto Proximidad y Distribución de Corriente en Conductores Multifilares"
            objetivo: "Analizar la distorsión asimétrica de la densidad de corriente en conductores adyacentes debida a los campos magnéticos mutuos, evaluando la resistencia AC en cables y devanados."
            concepto_clave_latex: "R_{AC} = R_{DC} \\cdot k_{skin} \\cdot k_{prox} \\quad ; \\quad k_{prox} \\propto \\left(\\frac{d_{cond}}{s_{separacion}}\\right)^2 f^2"
            ejemplo: "Problema 1: Dos conductores cilíndricos paralelos transportan corrientes alternas en la misma dirección a $10\\text{ kHz}$. El campo magnético generado por el conductor 1 ejerce una fuerza de Lorentz sobre las cargas móviles del conductor 2, empujando la densidad de corriente hacia los bordes externos opuestos (efecto proximidad repulsivo). Si las corrientes circulan en direcciones opuestas, la densidad de corriente se concentra en las superficies interiores enfrentadas. En ambos casos, el área efectiva de conducción se contrae drásticamente, incrementando la resistencia AC hasta 4 veces la resistencia DC. Problema 2: El hilo de Litz (Litz wire), compuesto por decenas de hilos finamente aislados entre sí y trenzados en patrones transpuestos geométricos, asegura que cada hilo ocupe uniformemente todas las posiciones espaciales, cancelando el efecto proximidad en inversores solares."
            bloque_sugerido: "Electrónica de Potencia 40 min • Modelado de Dowell para resistencia AC en transformadores HF"
            slides:
              - numero: 1
                seccion: "CAMPOS MAGNÉTICOS CRUZADOS"
                titulo: "Mecanismo del Efecto Proximidad"
                puntos:
                  - "A diferencia del efecto pelicular que es simétrico y puramente autoinducido, el efecto proximidad surge de la interacción con conductores vecinos."
                  - "Provoca puntos calientes ('hot spots') localizados en las capas internas de devanados de transformadores e inductores."
                  - "Aumenta exponencialmente con el número de capas enrolladas superpuestas."
              - numero: 2
                seccion: "MITIGACIÓN TÉCNICA"
                titulo: "Hilo de Litz y Láminas de Cobre"
                puntos:
                  - "Elegir el diámetro de cada hilo individual menor que la profundidad de piel ($d_{hilo} < 2\\delta_s$)."
                  - "Uso de conductores en lámina plana (foil windings) para inductores de alta corriente en cargadores de vehículos eléctricos."
                  - "Intercalado de capas de primario y secundario (interleaving) para cancelar fuerzas magnetomotrices locales."
          - numero_tema: 24
            corte: 3
            modalidad: "teorico"
            titulo: "Inductancia Mutua, Coeficiente de Acoplamiento y Polaridad en Transformadores"
            objetivo: "Calcular la inductancia mutua $M$ entre circuitos magnéticamente acoplados a partir del flujo concatenado, deduciendo la convención de puntos de polaridad y el coeficiente de acoplamiento $k$."
            concepto_clave_latex: "M = k \\sqrt{L_1 L_2} \\quad [0 \\le k \\le 1] \\quad ; \\quad v_1 = L_1 \\frac{di_1}{dt} \\pm M \\frac{di_2}{dt} \\quad ; \\quad v_2 = \\pm M \\frac{di_1}{dt} + L_2 \\frac{di_2}{dt}"
            ejemplo: "Problema 1: Dos bobinas acopladas sobre un núcleo toroidal tienen inductancias propias $L_1 = 400\\text{ mH}$, $L_2 = 100\\text{ mH}$ y un coeficiente de acoplamiento de $k = 0.95$. Calcular la inductancia mutua $M$: $M = 0.95 \\sqrt{0.400 \\times 0.100} = 0.95 \\times \\sqrt{0.040} = 0.95 \\times 0.200 = 0.190\\text{ H} = 190\\text{ mH}$. Si se conectan en serie con polaridad aditiva: $L_{eq,aditiva} = L_1 + L_2 + 2M = 400 + 100 + 2(190) = 880\\text{ mH}$. Con polaridad sustractiva: $L_{eq,sustractiva} = L_1 + L_2 - 2M = 500 - 380 = 120\\text{ mH}$. Problema 2: En sistemas de transferencia inalámbrica de potencia inductiva (WPT) para vehículos eléctricos, el núcleo de aire reduce el acoplamiento a $k \\approx 0.15 - 0.30$, requiriendo redes de compensación resonante serie-paralelo para maximizar la potencia transmitida."
            bloque_sugerido: "Laboratorio de Circuitos 40 min • Ensayo de acoplamiento mutuo y regla de los puntos"
            slides:
              - numero: 1
                seccion: "ACOPLAMIENTO MAGNÉTICO"
                titulo: "La Regla de los Puntos de Polaridad"
                puntos:
                  - "Si una corriente entra por el terminal con punto de una bobina, la tensión inducida en la otra bobina es positiva en su correspondiente terminal con punto."
                  - "Físicamente representa el sentido relativo del devanado de las espiras en torno al núcleo magnético."
                  - "En transformadores de potencia de núcleo ferromagnético cerrado, $k > 0.998$, acercándose al transformador ideal."
              - numero: 2
                seccion: "TRANSFERENCIA INALÁMBRICA"
                titulo: "Carga Inductiva Resonante"
                puntos:
                  - "Permite cargar vehículos eléctricos sin contacto físico eliminando riesgos de choque eléctrico en lluvia."
                  - "Bobinas emisora y receptora sintonizadas a idéntica frecuencia resonante (típicamente $85\\text{ kHz}$ según norma SAE J2954)."
                  - "Flujo magnético de dispersión controlado mediante blindajes de ferrita y aluminio para cumplir normas ICNIRP de exposición humana."
          - numero_tema: 25
            corte: 3
            modalidad: "teorico"
            titulo: "Tensor de Esfuerzos de Maxwell y Fuerzas Electromecánicas en Máquinas"
            objetivo: "Calcular fuerzas y torques mecánicos a partir de la distribución espacial de campos electromagnéticos integrando el Tensor de Esfuerzos de Maxwell sobre superficies de control cerradas."
            concepto_clave_latex: "T_{ij} = \\varepsilon_0 \\left( E_i E_j - \\frac{1}{2}\\delta_{ij} |\\mathbf{E}|^2 \\right) + \\frac{1}{\\mu_0} \\left( B_i B_j - \\frac{1}{2}\\delta_{ij} |\\mathbf{B}|^2 \\right) \\quad ; \\quad \\mathbf{F} = \\oint_S \\mathbf{T} \\cdot d\\mathbf{A}"
            ejemplo: "Problema 1: En el entrehierro cilíndrico de un generador síncrono eólico de imanes permanentes de radio medio $r = 1.2\\text{ m}$, longitud axial $L = 0.8\\text{ m}$ y espesor de entrehierro $g = 3\\text{ mm}$, el campo radial es $B_r = 0.9\\text{ T}$ y el campo azimutal de reacción de armadura es $B_\\theta = 0.25\\text{ T}$. El esfuerzo de corte tangencial de Maxwell es: $\\sigma_{r\\theta} = \\frac{1}{\\mu_0} B_r B_\\theta = \\frac{0.9 \\times 0.25}{4\\pi \\times 10^{-7}} = \\frac{0.225}{1.2566 \\times 10^{-6}} = 1.79 \\times 10^5\\text{ N/m}^2 = 179\\text{ kPa}$. Superficie del entrehierro: $A = 2\\pi r L = 2\\pi(1.2)(0.8) = 6.032\\text{ m}^2$. Fuerza tangencial total: $F_\\theta = 1.79 \\times 10^5 \\times 6.032 = 1.08 \\times 10^6\\text{ N}$. Torque electromagnético generado: $\\tau = F_\\theta \\cdot r = 1.08 \\times 10^6 \\times 1.2 = 1.296\\text{ MN}\\cdot\\text{m}$. Problema 2: La atracción magnética radial normal $\\sigma_{rr} = \\frac{B_r^2 - B_\\theta^2}{2\\mu_0} \\approx \\frac{0.9^2}{2\\mu_0} \\approx 322\\text{ kPa}$ ejerce un esfuerzo de compresión masivo sobre los rodamientos mecánicos si existe excentricidad en el rotor."
            bloque_sugerido: "Electromecánica 45 min • Cálculo de par por tensor de Maxwell vs método de coenergía"
            slides:
              - numero: 1
                seccion: "DENSIDAD DE FUERZA DE LORENTZ"
                titulo: "Esfuerzos Mecánicos del Campo"
                puntos:
                  - "Transforma la fuerza volumétrica de Lorentz $\\mathbf{f} = \\rho \\mathbf{E} + \\mathbf{J} \\times \\mathbf{B}$ en la divergencia de un tensor de tensiones mecánicas superficiales: $\\mathbf{f} = \\nabla \\cdot \\mathbf{T}$."
                  - "Tensión a lo largo de las líneas de campo magnético: Las líneas de campo actúan como cuerdas elásticas tensas ($B^2/(2\\mu)$)."
                  - "Presión hidrostática perpendicular a las líneas de campo: Tienden a separarse y repelerse lateralmente."
              - numero: 2
                seccion: "SIMULACIÓN POR ELEMENTOS FINITOS"
                titulo: "Cálculo de Torque en Motores Eléctricos"
                puntos:
                  - "En software FEM (ANSYS Maxwell, FEMM), el torque se obtiene integrando numéricamente el tensor a lo largo de una banda de elementos en el aire del entrehierro."
                  - "No requiere conocer las fuerzas de Lorentz individuales espira por espira en los conductores ranurados."
                  - "Permite diseñar rotores con mínimo par de rizado ('cogging torque') para generadores eólicos direct-drive."
          - numero_tema: 26
            corte: 3
            modalidad: "teorico"
            titulo: "Ruptura Dieléctrica, Descargas Parciales y Efecto Corona en Alta Tensión"
            objetivo: "Modelar el campo eléctrico crítico de ionización del aire según la ley de Peek, calculando pérdidas de potencia por efecto corona y criterios de diseño de conductores en líneas de transmisión."
            concepto_clave_latex: "E_0 = 30 m \\delta \\left( 1 + \\frac{0.3}{\\sqrt{\\delta r}} \\right) \\quad [\\text{kV/cm}] \\quad ; \\quad P_{corona} \\propto \\frac{242.2}{\\delta}(f + 25)\\sqrt{\\frac{r}{D}}(V - V_d)^2"
            ejemplo: "Problema 1: Calcular el gradiente crítico disruptivo de ruptura $E_0$ en aire seco a nivel del mar ($\\delta = 1.0$) para un conductor de fase cilíndrico de radio $r = 1.5\\text{ cm}$ con factor de rugosidad superficial $m = 0.85$ (conductor trenzado envejecido). Aplicando la fórmula de Peek: $E_0 = 30(0.85)(1.0) \\left( 1 + \\frac{0.3}{\\sqrt{1.0 \\times 1.5}} \\right) = 25.5 \\left( 1 + \\frac{0.3}{1.2247} \\right) = 25.5(1 + 0.245) = 25.5(1.245) = 31.75\\text{ kV/cm}$. Si el campo eléctrico superficial nominal en la línea supera los $31.75\\text{ kV/cm}$, el aire circundante se ioniza, desatando una descarga luminiscente continua (efecto corona). Problema 2: En días lluviosos en la Sierra Nevada de Santa Marta, la humedad reduce el factor $m$ a $0.6$, disparando las pérdidas por corona hasta $15\\text{ kW/km}$ por circuito trifásico y generando interferencia de radiofrecuencia (RIV) y zumbido acústico audible."
            bloque_sugerido: "Alta Tensión 45 min • Ley de Peek, diseño de haces de conductores y anillos anticorona"
            slides:
              - numero: 1
                seccion: "FÍSICA DE LA DESCARGA EN GASES"
                titulo: "Mecanismo de Avalancha de Townsend"
                puntos:
                  - "Campos eléctricos elevados aceleran electrones libres iniciales provocando ionización por impacto en moléculas de $N_2$ y $O_2$."
                  - "Se forma una vaina de plasma luminosa azulada alrededor del conductor acompañada de síntesis de ozono ($O_3$) y ácido nítrico corrosivo."
                  - "Las pérdidas aumentan con el cuadrado del voltaje por encima del umbral de extinción ($V - V_d$)."
              - numero: 2
                seccion: "INGENIERÍA DE LÍNEAS"
                titulo: "Mitigación con Haces de Subconductores"
                puntos:
                  - "Subdividir cada fase en un haz ('bundle') de 2, 3 o 4 conductores separados por espaciadores incrementa el radio geométrico equivalente ($r_{eq} = \\sqrt[n]{n r R^{n-1}}$)."
                  - "Reduce drásticamente el gradiente de potencial superficial por debajo del límite crítico de Peek."
                  - "Uso de anillos anticorona toroidales en cadenas de aisladores para uniformizar la distribución de campo eléctrico en terminales."
          - numero_tema: 27
            corte: 3
            modalidad: "teorico"
            titulo: "Blindaje Electromagnético, Efecto Jaula de Faraday y Compatibilidad (EMC)"
            objetivo: "Calcular la efectividad de apantallamiento $SE$ de recintos metálicos frente a ondas electromagnéticas radiadas e interferencias conducidas según normas IEC/IEEE."
            concepto_clave_latex: "SE = R + A + B \\quad [\\text{dB}] \\quad ; \\quad A = 20 \\log_{10}(e^{t/\\delta_s}) \\approx 8.686 \\frac{t}{\\delta_s} \\quad ; \\quad R = 20 \\log_{10}\\left( \\frac{|\\eta_0|}{4|\\eta_s|} \\right)"
            ejemplo: "Problema 1: Una lámina de cobre de espesor $t = 0.5\\text{ mm}$ ($\\sigma = 5.8 \\times 10^7\\text{ S/m}$) se utiliza para blindar un centro de control de subestación frente a pulsos electromagnéticos de alta frecuencia de $f = 10\\text{ MHz}$. Profundidad de penetración a 10 MHz: $\\delta_s = \\frac{1}{\\sqrt{\\pi \\times 10^7 \\times 4\\pi \\times 10^{-7} \\times 5.8 \\times 10^7}} \\approx 0.0209\\text{ mm}$. Calcular la atenuación por absorción pura $A$: $A = 8.686 \\times \\frac{0.5\\text{ mm}}{0.0209\\text{ mm}} = 8.686 \\times 23.92 = 207.8\\text{ dB}$. Una atenuación de más de 200 dB reduce la potencia residual de la onda a una fracción menor a $10^{-20}$, garantizando un blindaje prácticamente hermético. Problema 2: A bajas frecuencias ($60\\text{ Hz}$), la impedancia intrínseca de campos magnéticos de alta corriente es muy baja, requiriendo materiales de alta permeabilidad magnética ($\\mu$-metal o permalloy) para desviar las líneas de inducción magnética."
            bloque_sugerido: "Compatibilidad Electromagnética 40 min • Normas CISPR/IEC 61000 y efectividad de blindaje"
            slides:
              - numero: 1
                seccion: "MECANISMOS DE APANTALLAMIENTO"
                titulo: "Reflexión, Absorción y Múltiples Reflexiones"
                puntos:
                  - "Pérdida por Reflexión ($R$): Desajuste entre la impedancia de la onda incidente y la impedancia característica del metal de blindaje."
                  - "Pérdida por Absorción ($A$): Disipación térmica Joule de corrientes parásitas al atravesar el espesor del material."
                  - "Factor de corrección de reflexiones internas múltiples ($B$): Relevante solo en láminas extremadamente delgadas ($t < \\delta_s$)."
              - numero: 2
                seccion: "INTEGRIDAD DE SUBESTACIONES"
                titulo: "Jaulas de Faraday y Puesta a Tierra"
                puntos:
                  - "Cualquier ranura o apertura de ventilación en el gabinete actúa como una antena de ranura si su dimensión mayor se acerca a $\\lambda/2$."
                  - "Mallas de puesta a tierra equipotenciales de baja impedancia en subestaciones encapsuladas en $SF_6$ (GIS)."
                  - "Protección contra pulsos electromagnéticos de origen nuclear (HEMP) y descargas atmosféricas directas."
          - numero_tema: 28
            corte: 3
            modalidad: "teorico"
            titulo: "Superconductividad, Fenómeno de Meissner y Cables HTS de Potencia"
            objetivo: "Comprender la transición a resistencia eléctrica nula y expulsión de flujo magnético en superconductores de alta temperatura crítica (HTS), evaluando su aplicación en cables de transmisión de gran densidad energética."
            concepto_clave_latex: "\\mathbf{B} = 0 \\quad [T < T_c, \\ H < H_c \\implies \\text{Diamagnetismo Perfecto}] \\quad ; \\quad \\mathbf{J}_c = J_c(T, B) \\quad ; \\quad \\lambda_L = \\sqrt{\\frac{m}{\\mu_0 n_s e^2}}"
            ejemplo: "Problema 1: Un cable superconductor HTS de segunda generación basado en cintas de $YBCO$ ($YBa_2Cu_3O_{7-\\delta}$, $T_c = 93\\text{ K}$) opera refrigerado con nitrógeno líquido a $77\\text{ K}$. Una sola cinta de 4 mm de ancho y $1\\ \\mu\\text{m}$ de espesor superconductor transporta una corriente crítica de $I_c = 150\\text{ A}$ sin disipación Joule ($R = 0$). Calcular la densidad de corriente crítica en la capa activa: $A = 4 \\times 10^{-3}\\text{ m} \\times 10^{-6}\\text{ m} = 4 \\times 10^{-9}\\text{ m}^2$. Densidad de corriente: $J_c = \\frac{150\\text{ A}}{4 \\times 10^{-9}\\text{ m}^2} = 3.75 \\times 10^{10}\\text{ A/m}^2 = 37500\\text{ A/mm}^2$. Esto es más de 7000 veces superior a la densidad admisible en cables convencionales de cobre ($~5\\text{ A/mm}^2$). Problema 2: Un cable subterráneo HTS trifásico concéntrico de 15 cm de diámetro puede transportar 3.2 GW de potencia eléctrica a media tensión (50 kV), eliminando la necesidad de subestaciones transformadoras gigantes en centros urbanos densos."
            bloque_sugerido: "Superconductividad Aplicada 45 min • Ecuaciones de London y limitadores de corriente de falla (SFCL)"
            slides:
              - numero: 1
                seccion: "ELECTRODINÁMICA DE LONDON"
                titulo: "Resistencia Cero y Efecto Meissner"
                puntos:
                  - "Primera Ecuación de London: $\\frac{\\partial \\mathbf{J}_s}{\\partial t} = \\frac{n_s e^2}{m} \\mathbf{E}$ (aceleración continua de pares de Cooper sin fricción)."
                  - "Segunda Ecuación de London: $\\nabla \\times \\mathbf{J}_s = -\\frac{n_s e^2}{m} \\mathbf{B}$, que combinada con Ampère implica $\\nabla^2 \\mathbf{B} = \\frac{1}{\\lambda_L^2} \\mathbf{B}$."
                  - "El campo magnético se extingue exponencialmente en la superficie con una longitud de penetración de London $\\lambda_L \\approx 50 - 200\\text{ nm}$."
              - numero: 2
                seccion: "REDES DE TRANSMISIÓN DEL FUTURO"
                titulo: "Limitadores de Falla (SFCL) y Almacenamiento SMES"
                puntos:
                  - "Limitadores de Corriente de Falla Superconductores (SFCL): Durante un cortocircuito, la corriente supera $I_c$, el material transita instantáneamente a estado resistivo normal (quench) frenando la falla en menos de 2 milisegundos sin piezas móviles."
                  - "Sistemas SMES: Almacenamiento magnético toroidal sin pérdidas de ciclado con tiempos de inyección de potencia de microsegundos."
                  - "Sistemas de refrigeración criogénica con circuito cerrado Stirling o Gifford-McMahon."
          - numero_tema: 29
            corte: 3
            modalidad: "teorico"
            titulo: "Métodos Numéricos Electromagnéticos: Diferencias Finitas (FDTD) y Elementos Finitos (FEM)"
            objetivo: "Formular la discretización espaciotemporal de las ecuaciones rotacionales de Maxwell mediante el algoritmo de Yee (FDTD) y la formulación variacional de elementos finitos (FEM)."
            concepto_clave_latex: "E_x^{n+1/2}(i+1/2,j,k) = E_x^{n-1/2} + \\frac{\\Delta t}{\\varepsilon \\Delta y}(H_z - H_z) - \\frac{\\Delta t}{\\varepsilon \\Delta z}(H_y - H_y) \\quad ; \\quad \\Delta t \\le \\frac{1}{c\\sqrt{\\frac{1}{\\Delta x^2} + \\frac{1}{\\Delta y^2} + \\frac{1}{\\Delta z^2}}}"
            ejemplo: "Problema 1: En una simulación FDTD tridimensional con celdas espaciales cúbicas de resolución $\\Delta x = \\Delta y = \\Delta z = 1.0\\text{ mm}$, calcular el paso de tiempo máximo permitido por la condición de estabilidad de Courant-Friedrichs-Lewy (CFL): $\\Delta t_{max} = \\frac{1.0 \\times 10^{-3}\\text{ m}}{3.0 \\times 10^8\\text{ m/s} \\times \\sqrt{3}} = \\frac{10^{-3}}{5.196 \\times 10^8} \\approx 1.924 \\times 10^{-12}\\text{ s} = 1.924\\text{ ps}$. Un paso temporal mayor genera inestabilidad numérica no física y divergencia exponencial instantánea del campo. Problema 2: En formulaciones FEM 2D para diseño de aisladores de subestación, se minimiza el funcional de energía electrostática $W[V] = \\frac{1}{2}\\iint \\varepsilon |\\nabla V|^2 dx dy$ sobre una malla de triángulos adaptativos."
            bloque_sugerido: "Computación Electromagnética 45 min • Algoritmo de celda intercalada de Kane Yee en Python"
            slides:
              - numero: 1
                seccion: "DISCRETIZACIÓN TEMPORAL FDTD"
                titulo: "La Malla Intercalada de Kane Yee"
                puntos:
                  - "Las componentes de $\\mathbf{E}$ y $\\mathbf{H}$ se posicionan desplazadas espacialmente en medio paso de rejilla ($\\Delta x/2$) y temporalmente en medio paso de tiempo ($\\Delta t/2$)."
                  - "Evalúa directamente los rotacionales de Maxwell sin inversión de matrices mediante actualización explícita ('leapfrog')."
                  - "Condiciones de frontera absorbentes de capas perfectamente adaptadas (PML) para simular espacio abierto infinito sin reflexiones numéricas."
              - numero: 2
                seccion: "MÉTODO DE ELEMENTOS FINITOS (FEM)"
                titulo: "Geometrías Complejas y Materiales No Lineales"
                puntos:
                  - "Ideal para geometrías curvas de rotores ranurados y materiales con permeabilidad no lineal $\\mu(B)$ saturable."
                  - "Resuelve la formulación débil mediante funciones de base nodales o de borde (elementos de Whitney)."
                  - "Núcleo de software de diseño industrial de alta fidelidad (COMSOL Multiphysics, ANSYS Maxwell)."
          - numero_tema: 30
            corte: 3
            modalidad: "teorico"
            titulo: "Campos Electromagnéticos Ambientales y Normatividad de Exposición en Subestaciones"
            objetivo: "Evaluar los niveles de exposición ocupacional y poblacional a campos electromagnéticos de frecuencia industrial (60 Hz) generados por líneas de transmisión y subestaciones eléctricas, aplicando las directrices internacionales ICNIRP y el RETIE colombiano."
            concepto_clave_latex: "B_{max, poblacional} \\le 200\\ \\mu\\text{T} \\quad ; \\quad B_{max, ocupacional} \\le 1000\\ \\mu\\text{T} \\quad ; \\quad E_{max, poblacional} \\le 4.16\\text{ kV/m} \\quad [60\\text{ Hz}]"
            ejemplo: "Problema 1: A una distancia horizontal de $x = 15\\text{ m}$ del eje de una línea aérea trifásica de 500 kV suspendida a una altura mínima de $h = 12\\text{ m}$ sobre el suelo, las mediciones arrojan un campo magnético de $B = 14.5\\ \\mu\\text{T}$ y un campo eléctrico de $E = 2.1\\text{ kV/m}$ a 1 metro sobre el nivel del terreno. Comparar con los límites del Reglamento Técnico de Instalaciones Eléctricas de Colombia (RETIE / Resolución 90708): El límite poblacional continuo es $200\\ \\mu\\text{T}$ y $4.16\\text{ kV/m}$. Como $14.5\\ \\mu\\text{T} \\ll 200\\ \\mu\\text{T}$ y $2.1\\text{ kV/m} < 4.16\\text{ kV/m}$, la servidumbre cumple satisfactoriamente la normatividad de seguridad de salud pública. Problema 2: En el patio de una subestación de 230 kV, el campo eléctrico bajo pórticos puede alcanzar $8.5\\text{ kV/m}$, requiriendo trajes de protección conductivos (traje de Faraday) y protocolos de permanencia de tiempo restringido para los ingenieros de mantenimiento."
            bloque_sugerido: "Seguridad Electromagnética 40 min • Simulación de perfiles de campo bajo líneas de alta tensión"
            slides:
              - numero: 1
                seccion: "BIOELECTROMAGNETISMO"
                titulo: "Efectos Biológicos a Frecuencia Industrial (60 Hz)"
                puntos:
                  - "A bajas frecuencias (60 Hz), los campos eléctricos y magnéticos no ionizantes no rompen enlaces moleculares ni causan calentamiento térmico."
                  - "El mecanismo primario es la inducción de densidades de corriente microscópicas ($J_{ind} = \\sigma_{tejido} E_{int}$) en tejidos nerviosos y musculares."
                  - "Las directrices ICNIRP imponen factores de seguridad de hasta 50 veces por debajo de los umbrales de estimulación sináptica detectable."
              - numero: 2
                seccion: "ZONAS DE SERVIDUMBRE Y RETIE"
                titulo: "Franjas de Seguridad de Líneas de Transmisión"
                puntos:
                  - "El ancho de la franja de servidumbre (retiradas mínimas de 15 a 60 metros según el nivel de tensión) garantiza que en el borde del corredor los campos no superen los límites poblacionales."
                  - "Cálculo de tensiones inducidas por acoplamiento capacitivo en vallas metálicas y tuberías paralelas."
                  - "Uso de medidores de campo triaxiales calibrados según norma IEEE Std 644 para certificación y licenciamiento ambiental."
      - codigo: "01021805"
        nombre: "General English IV"
        creditos: 2
        obligatoria: true
        categoria: "FORMACION_GENERAL"
        color: "#8E8E93"
        temas:
          - numero_tema: 1
            corte: 1
            modalidad: "general"
            titulo: "Past Perfect Simple & Continuous: Sequencing Past Events"
            objetivo: "Ordenar cronológicamente antecedentes y causas previas a un evento pasado en reportes de ingeniería."
            concepto_clave_latex: ""
            ejemplo: "By the time we checked the logger, it had already recorded 10,000 data points."
            bloque_sugerido: "Chronology Lab 40 min • Root-cause sequencing in technical incident reports"
            slides:
              - numero: 1
                seccion: "CEFR B1.2 • CORE CONCEPT"
                titulo: "Past Perfect Simple & Continuous: Sequencing Past Events: Communicative Purpose"
                puntos:
                  - "Past Perfect Simple (had + V3) marks 'the past before the past' — an action completed BEFORE another past reference point."
                  - "Past Perfect Continuous (had been + V-ing) emphasizes how long an activity had been running before a past event occurred."
                  - "Key triggers: by the time, before, after, already, just, because."
                ejemplo: "By the time we checked the logger, it had already recorded 10,000 data points."
              - numero: 2
                seccion: "STRUCTURE & PATTERNS"
                titulo: "Core Grammatical Blueprint"
                puntos:
                  - "Past Perfect Simple: 'By the time the technician arrived, the breaker had tripped.'"
                  - "Past Perfect Continuous: 'The bearing failed because it had been vibrating for weeks.'"
                  - "Clear chronological chain with 'before/after' can use Past Simple, while 'by the time' strongly prefers Past Perfect."
                tabla:
                  - ["Aspect", "Form", "Diagnostic Meaning"]
                  - ["Past Perfect Simple", "had + V3", "Completed prior event (had overheated)"]
                  - ["Past Perfect Cont.", "had been + V-ing", "Prior duration/cause (had been leaking)"]
              - numero: 3
                seccion: "QUESTIONS & NEGATION"
                titulo: "Interrogative, Negative & Short Answers"
                puntos:
                  - "Negative: 'We hadn't calibrated the zero offset before the first trial.'"
                  - "Question: 'How long had the turbine been operating before the shutdown?'"
                ejemplo: "The battery voltage dropped because the load had been drawing 15 A for three hours."
              - numero: 4
                seccion: "PRECISION & CONTRAST"
                titulo: "Key Distinctions & Common Pitfalls"
                puntos:
                  - "Don't overuse Past Perfect when events are told in chronological order (A, then B, then C -> Past Simple)."
                  - "Use Past Perfect when looking BACKWARD from event B to earlier cause A!"
                tabla:
                  - ["Sequence", "Tense Choice", "Example"]
                  - ["A -> then B (forward)", "Past Simple + Past Simple", "Pressure rose and the valve opened."]
                  - ["At B, looking back at A", "Past Simple + Past Perfect", "The valve opened because pressure had risen."]
              - numero: 5
                seccion: "CAMPUS & LAB CONTEXT"
                titulo: "Authentic Academic & Engineering Usage"
                puntos:
                  - "By the time we checked the logger, it had already recorded 10,000 data points."
                  - "The battery voltage dropped because the load had been drawing 15 A for three hours."
                  - "Had you studied Python before you enrolled in Energy Engineering?"
                ejemplo: "Academic Register (CEFR B1.2): Clear, concise communication in Unimagdalena seminars."
              - numero: 6
                seccion: "MASTERY CHECK"
                titulo: "Self-Assessment & Oral Drill"
                puntos:
                  - "Combine: 'The grid stabilized. Earlier, operators isolated the fault' (use 'after' or 'because')."
                  - "Choose: 'It was hot because the furnace (ran / had been running) all day' -> 'had been running'."
                  - "Write a 4-sentence root-cause timeline of a past system event."
                ejemplo: "Practice reading each model sentence aloud with natural stress and intonation."
          - numero_tema: 2
            corte: 1
            modalidad: "general"
            titulo: "Third Conditional: Regrets, Past Hypotheses & Post-Mortem Analysis"
            objetivo: "Evaluar escenarios pasados contrafactuales y lecciones aprendidas mediante el Tercer Condicional."
            concepto_clave_latex: ""
            ejemplo: "If the operator had noticed the pressure alarm, she would have closed the bypass valve."
            bloque_sugerido: "Post-Mortem Review 40 min • Counterfactual analysis of engineering case studies"
            slides:
              - numero: 1
                seccion: "CEFR B1.2 • CORE CONCEPT"
                titulo: "Third Conditional: Regrets, Past Hypotheses & Post-Mortem Analysis: Communicative Purpose"
                puntos:
                  - "Form: If + Past Perfect (had + V3), would / could / might + have + V3."
                  - "Refers 100% to the PAST — imagining how a past outcome would have differed if an earlier condition had changed."
                  - "Essential in engineering post-mortem reviews without assigning personal blame."
                ejemplo: "If the operator had noticed the pressure alarm, she would have closed the bypass valve."
              - numero: 2
                seccion: "STRUCTURE & PATTERNS"
                titulo: "Core Grammatical Blueprint"
                puntos:
                  - "Affirmative counterfactual: 'If we had insulated the tank, we would have saved 18% of the heat.'"
                  - "Negative -> Positive flip: 'If the relay hadn't tripped, the motor could have burned out.'"
                  - "Modal nuance: 'would have' (certain result), 'could have' (ability/chance), 'might have' (possibility)."
                tabla:
                  - ["Clause", "Structure", "Example"]
                  - ["Condition (Unreal Past)", "If + had (not) + V3", "If we had checked the polarity,"]
                  - ["Outcome (Unreal Past)", "would/could/might + have + V3", "the fuse wouldn't have blown."]
              - numero: 3
                seccion: "QUESTIONS & NEGATION"
                titulo: "Interrogative, Negative & Short Answers"
                puntos:
                  - "Spoken contraction alert: 'I'd' = 'I had' (before V3) OR 'I would' (before 'have') -> 'If I'd known, I'd have fixed it'."
                  - "Formal inversion (B2 preview): 'Had we used thicker wire, voltage drop would have been negligible.'"
                ejemplo: "The project wouldn't have finished on schedule if the team hadn't automated data cleaning."
              - numero: 4
                seccion: "PRECISION & CONTRAST"
                titulo: "Key Distinctions & Common Pitfalls"
                puntos:
                  - "NEVER put 'would have' in the If-clause (*If we would have tested...* -> 'If we had tested...')."
                  - "Never write 'would of' (phonetic spelling error of spoken 'would've' -> ALWAYS write 'would have')!"
                tabla:
                  - ["Spoken Sound", "Wrong Spelling", "Correct Academic Writing"]
                  - ["/ˈwʊdəv/", "would of failed", "would have failed"]
                  - ["If + would have", "If it would have rained", "If it had rained"]
              - numero: 5
                seccion: "CAMPUS & LAB CONTEXT"
                titulo: "Authentic Academic & Engineering Usage"
                puntos:
                  - "If the operator had noticed the pressure alarm, she would have closed the bypass valve."
                  - "The project wouldn't have finished on schedule if the team hadn't automated data cleaning."
                  - "What could have happened if the grounding cable had been disconnected?"
                ejemplo: "Academic Register (CEFR B1.2): Clear, concise communication in Unimagdalena seminars."
              - numero: 6
                seccion: "MASTERY CHECK"
                titulo: "Self-Assessment & Oral Drill"
                puntos:
                  - "Rewrite as 3rd Conditional: 'We didn't clean the panels, so output dropped by 11%.'"
                  - "Fix: 'If you would have saved the file, you wouldn't of lost it.'"
                  - "Write 3 post-mortem lessons from a past exam or lab session."
                ejemplo: "Practice reading each model sentence aloud with natural stress and intonation."
          - numero_tema: 3
            corte: 1
            modalidad: "general"
            titulo: "Mixed Conditionals: Past Causes with Present Consequences"
            objetivo: "Conectar decisiones o eventos del pasado con sus efectos actuales mediante condicionales mixtos."
            concepto_clave_latex: ""
            ejemplo: "If we had calibrated the pyranometer this morning, our live readings would be accurate right now."
            bloque_sugerido: "Causal Reasoning 40 min • Linking historical energy choices to today's grid"
            slides:
              - numero: 1
                seccion: "CEFR B1.2 • CORE CONCEPT"
                titulo: "Mixed Conditionals: Past Causes with Present Consequences: Communicative Purpose"
                puntos:
                  - "Type A (Most Common — Past Condition -> Present Result): If + Past Perfect (had + V3), would / could + BASE verb (now!)."
                  - "Type B (Permanent Present State -> Past Result): If + Past Simple, would have + V3."
                  - "Signal words like 'now', 'today', 'currently' in the main clause reveal a Mixed Conditional!"
                ejemplo: "If we had calibrated the pyranometer this morning, our live readings would be accurate right now."
              - numero: 2
                seccion: "STRUCTURE & PATTERNS"
                titulo: "Core Grammatical Blueprint"
                puntos:
                  - "Past -> Present: 'If Colombia hadn't invested in hydro power decades ago, grid emissions would be much higher today.'"
                  - "Present -> Past: 'If copper weren't such a good conductor, engineers wouldn't have chosen it for those windings.'"
                  - "Verify the time reference of EACH half independently!"
                tabla:
                  - ["Mixed Pattern", "If-Clause Time", "Main Clause Time & Form"]
                  - ["Past -> Present", "Past (If + had + V3)", "Present (would + base verb now)"]
                  - ["Present -> Past", "General state (If + Past Simple)", "Past (would + have + V3)"]
              - numero: 3
                seccion: "QUESTIONS & NEGATION"
                titulo: "Interrogative, Negative & Short Answers"
                puntos:
                  - "Compare 3rd vs. Mixed: 'If I had taken Programming, I would have passed last year' (3rd: past result) vs. 'If I had taken Programming, I would know Python now' (Mixed: present state!)."
                ejemplo: "If silicon weren't abundant in Earth's crust, solar PV wouldn't have scaled so rapidly."
              - numero: 4
                seccion: "PRECISION & CONTRAST"
                titulo: "Key Distinctions & Common Pitfalls"
                puntos:
                  - "Watch time markers ('yesterday' vs. 'today') so you don't automatically default to 'would have + V3' when the consequence is happening RIGHT NOW."
                tabla:
                  - ["Time Clue in Result", "Choose Result Form", "Example"]
                  - ["...yesterday / in 2022", "would have + V3 (3rd)", "...costs would have fallen in 2022."]
                  - ["...today / right now", "would + base verb (Mixed)", "...costs would be lower today."]
              - numero: 5
                seccion: "CAMPUS & LAB CONTEXT"
                titulo: "Authentic Academic & Engineering Usage"
                puntos:
                  - "If we had calibrated the pyranometer this morning, our live readings would be accurate right now."
                  - "If silicon weren't abundant in Earth's crust, solar PV wouldn't have scaled so rapidly."
                  - "I wouldn't be in Semester 4 now if I hadn't passed Calculus I and II."
                ejemplo: "Academic Register (CEFR B1.2): Clear, concise communication in Unimagdalena seminars."
              - numero: 6
                seccion: "MASTERY CHECK"
                titulo: "Self-Assessment & Oral Drill"
                puntos:
                  - "Build a Mixed Conditional: 'We installed LED lighting last year -> our bill is 35% lower today.'"
                  - "Identify time frames in: 'If she spoke German, she would have applied for the Munich internship.'"
                  - "Write 2 Past->Present mixed conditionals about technology history."
                ejemplo: "Practice reading each model sentence aloud with natural stress and intonation."
          - numero_tema: 4
            corte: 2
            modalidad: "general"
            titulo: "Passive Voice II (All Tenses, Modals & Impersonal It is said that...)"
            objetivo: "Dominar construcciones pasivas avanzadas con tiempos continuos, perfectos, verbos modales y estructuras impersonales."
            concepto_clave_latex: ""
            ejemplo: "A new microgrid laboratory is currently being equipped at Unimagdalena."
            bloque_sugerido: "Academic Style Lab 45 min • Impersonal reporting & modal passives in papers"
            slides:
              - numero: 1
                seccion: "CEFR B1.2 • CORE CONCEPT"
                titulo: "Passive Voice II (All Tenses, Modals & Impersonal It is said that...): Communicative Purpose"
                puntos:
                  - "Universal Passive Formula: Subject + [any tense/modal of BE] + Past Participle (V3)."
                  - "Continuous Passive: is/are/was/were + BEING + V3 ('Smart meters are being deployed across the coast')."
                  - "Perfect & Modal Passive: has/have/had + BEEN + V3 | must/can/should + BE + V3 ('Hydrogen can be stored in tanks')."
                ejemplo: "A new microgrid laboratory is currently being equipped at Unimagdalena."
              - numero: 2
                seccion: "STRUCTURE & PATTERNS"
                titulo: "Core Grammatical Blueprint"
                puntos:
                  - "Modal Passive in standards: 'All enclosures must be grounded.' / 'Losses can be minimized by...'"
                  - "Impersonal Reporting Pattern 1: 'It is estimated / reported / expected that + clause'."
                  - "Impersonal Reporting Pattern 2: 'Subject + is estimated / known + to V (or to have V3)'!"
                tabla:
                  - ["Active Structure", "Advanced Passive Formula", "Academic Example"]
                  - ["are installing", "are being installed", "New chargers are being installed."]
                  - ["have validated", "has been validated", "The model has been validated."]
                  - ["must verify", "must be verified", "Safety limits must be verified."]
              - numero: 3
                seccion: "QUESTIONS & NEGATION"
                titulo: "Interrogative, Negative & Short Answers"
                puntos:
                  - "Dual impersonal upgrade: 'Experts expect solar costs to fall' -> (1) 'It is expected that solar costs will fall' OR (2) 'Solar costs are expected to fall'."
                  - "For prior actions in Pattern 2, use perfect infinitive: 'The fault is believed to have started in Bus 4.'"
                ejemplo: "Harmonic distortion must be kept below 5% according to IEEE 519."
              - numero: 4
                seccion: "PRECISION & CONTRAST"
                titulo: "Key Distinctions & Common Pitfalls"
                puntos:
                  - "Don't confuse 'being' (continuous) with 'been' (perfect): 'is being tested' (now) vs. 'has been tested' (already done)!"
                  - "Avoid awkward triple-auxiliary passives like *will have been being tested* -> rewrite cleanly."
                tabla:
                  - ["Impersonal Pattern", "Syntax", "Research Paper Sentence"]
                  - ["It + passive + that", "It is shown that S + V", "It has been shown that tilt affects yield."]
                  - ["S + passive + to-inf", "S is shown to + V", "Tilt angle has been shown to affect yield."]
              - numero: 5
                seccion: "CAMPUS & LAB CONTEXT"
                titulo: "Authentic Academic & Engineering Usage"
                puntos:
                  - "A new microgrid laboratory is currently being equipped at Unimagdalena."
                  - "Harmonic distortion must be kept below 5% according to IEEE 519."
                  - "Offshore wind capacity is projected to grow substantially by 2035."
                ejemplo: "Academic Register (CEFR B1.2): Clear, concise communication in Unimagdalena seminars."
              - numero: 6
                seccion: "MASTERY CHECK"
                titulo: "Self-Assessment & Oral Drill"
                puntos:
                  - "Transform: 'People believe that the short circuit started at dawn' (both impersonal ways)."
                  - "Choose: 'The code (is being / has been) compiled right now' -> 'is being'."
                  - "Rewrite 3 active RETIE/IEEE safety rules into Modal Passive."
                ejemplo: "Practice reading each model sentence aloud with natural stress and intonation."
          - numero_tema: 5
            corte: 2
            modalidad: "general"
            titulo: "Reported Speech I: Statements & Shifts in Tense/Time"
            objetivo: "Reportar afirmaciones, hallazgos de autores y declaraciones técnicas aplicando backshift y ajustes deícticos."
            concepto_clave_latex: ""
            ejemplo: "The lead engineer reported that the inverter had reached 98.2% peak efficiency."
            bloque_sugerido: "Citation & Reporting 40 min • Summarizing speaker statements accurately"
            slides:
              - numero: 1
                seccion: "CEFR B1.2 • CORE CONCEPT"
                titulo: "Reported Speech I: Statements & Shifts in Tense/Time: Communicative Purpose"
                puntos:
                  - "When the reporting verb is in the past (said, stated, reported, explained), shift the original verb ONE step back ('backshift')."
                  - "Backshift chain: Present Simple -> Past Simple; Present Continuous -> Past Continuous; Past Simple / Present Perfect -> Past Perfect; will -> would; can -> could."
                  - "NO backshift needed when reporting timeless scientific truths ('Fourier proved that heat flows from hot to cold')!"
                ejemplo: "The lead engineer reported that the inverter had reached 98.2% peak efficiency."
              - numero: 2
                seccion: "STRUCTURE & PATTERNS"
                titulo: "Core Grammatical Blueprint"
                puntos:
                  - "'Say' vs. 'Tell': 'say (that)...' (no personal object) vs. 'tell + SOMEONE (that)...' ('She told us that the test passed')."
                  - "Deictic shifts: today -> that day, yesterday -> the day before, tomorrow -> the next/following day, here -> there, this -> that."
                  - "Academic citation often uses Present Reporting ('Çengel states that entropy increases') with zero backshift."
                tabla:
                  - ["Direct Speech", "Reported Speech (Past)", "Example"]
                  - ["Present -> Past", "am/is -> was", "'It is ready' -> He said it was ready."]
                  - ["Pres. Perf. -> Past Perf.", "have tested -> had tested", "'We've tested it' -> They said they had tested it."]
                  - ["Will -> Would", "will rise -> would rise", "'Load will rise' -> She noted load would rise."]
              - numero: 3
                seccion: "QUESTIONS & NEGATION"
                titulo: "Interrogative, Negative & Short Answers"
                puntos:
                  - "'Must' (obligation) shifts to 'had to'; 'must' (logical deduction) stays 'must'; 'should / might / could / would' stay unchanged!"
                ejemplo: "Professor Martínez told the class that the midterm would cover Chapters 1 to 4."
              - numero: 4
                seccion: "PRECISION & CONTRAST"
                titulo: "Key Distinctions & Common Pitfalls"
                puntos:
                  - "NEVER write 'He said me that...' -> either 'He told me that...' OR 'He said (to me) that...'."
                  - "Update pronouns and possessives logically to match the reporter's perspective."
                tabla:
                  - ["Verb Error", "Correction", "Rule"]
                  - ["She said us the results", "She told us the results", "tell + indirect object"]
                  - ["He told that it failed", "He said / stated that it failed", "'tell' requires a listener"]
              - numero: 5
                seccion: "CAMPUS & LAB CONTEXT"
                titulo: "Authentic Academic & Engineering Usage"
                puntos:
                  - "The lead engineer reported that the inverter had reached 98.2% peak efficiency."
                  - "Professor Martínez told the class that the midterm would cover Chapters 1 to 4."
                  - "Thermodynamics establishes that energy cannot be created or destroyed."
                ejemplo: "Academic Register (CEFR B1.2): Clear, concise communication in Unimagdalena seminars."
              - numero: 6
                seccion: "MASTERY CHECK"
                titulo: "Self-Assessment & Oral Drill"
                puntos:
                  - "Report: 'We are calibrating the wind sensor today,' the team said."
                  - "Fix: 'The technician told that the valve was closed' -> 'said that / told us that'."
                  - "Report 3 findings from a scientific lecture."
                ejemplo: "Practice reading each model sentence aloud with natural stress and intonation."
          - numero_tema: 6
            corte: 2
            modalidad: "general"
            titulo: "Reported Speech II: Questions, Commands & Requests"
            objetivo: "Reportar preguntas técnicas, instrucciones operativas y solicitudes formales sin inversión interrogativa."
            concepto_clave_latex: ""
            ejemplo: "The reviewer asked whether we had validated the CFD mesh independence."
            bloque_sugerido: "Q&A Reporting 40 min • Turning interview questions & SOPs into formal prose"
            slides:
              - numero: 1
                seccion: "CEFR B1.2 • CORE CONCEPT"
                titulo: "Reported Speech II: Questions, Commands & Requests: Communicative Purpose"
                puntos:
                  - "Reported Questions become STATEMENTS: drop 'do/does/did', drop the question mark, and use normal S + V word order!"
                  - "Yes/No Questions use 'if' or 'whether' ('He asked if/whether the grid was stable')."
                  - "Wh- Questions keep the Wh- word + Subject + Verb ('She asked what the cutoff frequency was')."
                ejemplo: "The reviewer asked whether we had validated the CFD mesh independence."
              - numero: 2
                seccion: "STRUCTURE & PATTERNS"
                titulo: "Core Grammatical Blueprint"
                puntos:
                  - "Commands / Instructions: tell / order / instruct + object + (NOT) + TO-infinitive ('The manual warns users not to open the case')."
                  - "Polite Requests: ask + object + (NOT) + TO-infinitive ('She asked me to share the dataset')."
                  - "Reporting verbs with patterns: advise/remind + obj + to V; suggest/recommend + V-ing (or that S + base V)."
                tabla:
                  - ["Direct Utterance", "Reported Structure", "Model Sentence"]
                  - ["'Are the sensors online?'", "asked if/whether + S + V", "He asked whether the sensors were online."]
                  - ["'Where did voltage drop?'", "asked + Wh- + S + V", "She asked where voltage had dropped."]
                  - ["'Do not touch Bus A!'", "warned + obj + not to V", "He warned us not to touch Bus A."]
              - numero: 3
                seccion: "QUESTIONS & NEGATION"
                titulo: "Interrogative, Negative & Short Answers"
                puntos:
                  - "Prefer 'whether' over 'if' in formal academic prose, especially before 'or not' ('We investigated whether humidity affected yield or not')."
                ejemplo: "The lab coordinator reminded students not to leave power supplies switched on."
              - numero: 4
                seccion: "PRECISION & CONTRAST"
                titulo: "Key Distinctions & Common Pitfalls"
                puntos:
                  - " #1 EXAM TRAP: keeping question inversion! NEVER say *He asked where was the lab* -> say 'He asked where the lab was'!"
                  - "Place 'not' BEFORE 'to' in negative commands: 'told us NOT to disconnect', never *to not* in formal tests."
                tabla:
                  - ["Word-Order Trap", "Incorrect", "Correct Statement Order"]
                  - ["Wh- + Be", "She asked what was V_oc.", "She asked what V_oc was."]
                  - ["Auxiliary 'did'", "He asked when did it stop.", "He asked when it had stopped."]
              - numero: 5
                seccion: "CAMPUS & LAB CONTEXT"
                titulo: "Authentic Academic & Engineering Usage"
                puntos:
                  - "The reviewer asked whether we had validated the CFD mesh independence."
                  - "The lab coordinator reminded students not to leave power supplies switched on."
                  - "A classmate asked how the DownloadQueueService handled twenty concurrent users."
                ejemplo: "Academic Register (CEFR B1.2): Clear, concise communication in Unimagdalena seminars."
              - numero: 6
                seccion: "MASTERY CHECK"
                titulo: "Self-Assessment & Oral Drill"
                puntos:
                  - "Report: 'How much power does the pump consume?' the auditor asked."
                  - "Report: 'Please upload your slides in PDF format,' the professor told us."
                  - "Fix: 'They asked if did the prototype pass' -> 'They asked whether the prototype had passed.'"
                ejemplo: "Practice reading each model sentence aloud with natural stress and intonation."
          - numero_tema: 7
            corte: 2
            modalidad: "general"
            titulo: "Future Continuous & Future Perfect (By 2030, we will have achieved...)"
            objetivo: "Proyectar metas acumuladas a una fecha límite (Future Perfect) y procesos en curso en el futuro (Future Continuous)."
            concepto_clave_latex: ""
            ejemplo: "By the end of Cuatrimestre 12, you will have completed 162 academic credits."
            bloque_sugerido: "Roadmap Projection 35 min • Writing 2030–2050 Net-Zero milestone statements"
            slides:
              - numero: 1
                seccion: "CEFR B1.2 • CORE CONCEPT"
                titulo: "Future Continuous & Future Perfect (By 2030, we will have achieved...): Communicative Purpose"
                puntos:
                  - "Future Continuous (will be + V-ing): an action that will be IN PROGRESS at a specific future moment or part of a natural future trajectory."
                  - "Future Perfect Simple (will have + V3): an action that will be COMPLETED BEFORE a future deadline ('By 2030, ...')."
                  - "Future Perfect Continuous (will have been + V-ing): duration up to a future milestone ('By June, she will have been researching H2 for two years')."
                ejemplo: "By the end of Cuatrimestre 12, you will have completed 162 academic credits."
              - numero: 2
                seccion: "STRUCTURE & PATTERNS"
                titulo: "Core Grammatical Blueprint"
                puntos:
                  - "Signal 'At this time tomorrow / In 2035': Future Continuous ('Grids will be operating with smart inverters')."
                  - "Signal 'By + future date / By the time + Present Simple': Future Perfect ('By Friday, we will have tested all 12 samples')."
                  - "Remember: time clauses after 'by the time' use PRESENT SIMPLE, not 'will'!"
                tabla:
                  - ["Tense", "Formula", "Key Time Marker & Meaning"]
                  - ["Future Continuous", "will be + V-ing", "At 10 a.m. tomorrow (in progress)"]
                  - ["Future Perfect", "will have + V3", "By 2030 / By next month (completed)"]
                  - ["Future Perf. Cont.", "will have been + V-ing", "By May, ...for 3 years (duration)"]
              - numero: 3
                seccion: "QUESTIONS & NEGATION"
                titulo: "Interrogative, Negative & Short Answers"
                puntos:
                  - "Polite non-intrusive inquiry: 'Will you be using the spectrum analyzer this afternoon?' (asking about someone's existing plans)."
                ejemplo: "This time next week, our group will be defending our CDIO project."
              - numero: 4
                seccion: "PRECISION & CONTRAST"
                titulo: "Key Distinctions & Common Pitfalls"
                puntos:
                  - "Distinguish 'in 2030' (at that year -> will / will be V-ing) vs. 'by 2030' (at or before that deadline -> will have V3)!"
                  - "Never write *by the time you will arrive* -> 'by the time you arrive, the simulation will have finished'."
                tabla:
                  - ["Preposition", "Meaning", "Correct Tense"]
                  - ["BY 2030", "No later than 2030 (cumulative)", "Colombia will have expanded wind farms."]
                  - ["IN 2030", "During the year 2030", "Many plants will be producing green H2."]
              - numero: 5
                seccion: "CAMPUS & LAB CONTEXT"
                titulo: "Authentic Academic & Engineering Usage"
                puntos:
                  - "By the end of Cuatrimestre 12, you will have completed 162 academic credits."
                  - "This time next week, our group will be defending our CDIO project."
                  - "By 2040, battery storage will have transformed peak-load management worldwide."
                ejemplo: "Academic Register (CEFR B1.2): Clear, concise communication in Unimagdalena seminars."
              - numero: 6
                seccion: "MASTERY CHECK"
                titulo: "Self-Assessment & Oral Drill"
                puntos:
                  - "Complete: 'By 5:00 p.m., the solver ___ (converge)' -> 'will have converged'."
                  - "Complete: 'Don't call at 9:00; I ___ (take) my Thermodynamics exam' -> 'will be taking'."
                  - "Write 3 'By 2030 / By graduation...' roadmaps using Future Perfect."
                ejemplo: "Practice reading each model sentence aloud with natural stress and intonation."
          - numero_tema: 8
            corte: 3
            modalidad: "general"
            titulo: "Causative Verbs (Have/Get something done, Make, Let, Help)"
            objetivo: "Expresar servicios técnicos delegados (have/get something done) y relaciones de causa, permiso o asistencia."
            concepto_clave_latex: ""
            ejemplo: "The university had fifty solar modules installed on the parking canopy."
            bloque_sugerido: "Maintenance & Control 35 min • Delegated engineering services & causal verbs"
            slides:
              - numero: 1
                seccion: "CEFR B1.2 • CORE CONCEPT"
                titulo: "Causative Verbs (Have/Get something done, Make, Let, Help): Communicative Purpose"
                puntos:
                  - "Passive Causative: 'have / get + OBJECT + Past Participle (V3)' means commissioning a specialist/service to perform an action for you ('We had the pyranometer calibrated at IDEAM')."
                  - "Active Causatives: 'make + obj + bare V' (force/cause), 'let + obj + bare V' (allow), 'have + person + bare V' (assign), 'get + person + TO V' (persuade)."
                  - "'Help + obj + (to) V' accepts either bare infinitive or to-infinitive."
                ejemplo: "The university had fifty solar modules installed on the parking canopy."
              - numero: 2
                seccion: "STRUCTURE & PATTERNS"
                titulo: "Core Grammatical Blueprint"
                puntos:
                  - "Have/Get + object + V3 adapts to any tense: 'We get the filters replaced quarterly' / 'They are having the roof reinforced.'"
                  - "Passive of 'make' restores 'to': 'The gas is made TO expand' (vs. active 'Heat makes the gas expand')."
                  - "Formal alternative to 'let': 'allow / permit + object + TO V'."
                tabla:
                  - ["Causative Pattern", "Syntax", "Engineering Meaning"]
                  - ["Service (Passive)", "have/get + thing + V3", "We had the transformer rewound."]
                  - ["Force / Cause", "make + obj + bare V", "Friction makes bearings heat up."]
                  - ["Assign vs. Persuade", "have sb V / get sb TO V", "Have Luis check it / Get him to help."]
              - numero: 3
                seccion: "QUESTIONS & NEGATION"
                titulo: "Interrogative, Negative & Short Answers"
                puntos:
                  - "Watch word order in Passive Causative: 'had + OBJECT + V3' ('We had the inverter repaired') vs. Past Perfect active ('We had repaired the inverter' = we fixed it ourselves!)."
                ejemplo: "Smart thermostats help households reduce cooling electricity bills."
              - numero: 4
                seccion: "PRECISION & CONTRAST"
                titulo: "Key Distinctions & Common Pitfalls"
                puntos:
                  - "Never use bare infinitive after 'get + person': say 'get the vendor TO send the datasheet', NOT *get the vendor send*."
                  - "Don't forget 'to' after 'allow/enable/cause': 'enable the system TO track'."
                tabla:
                  - ["Order Contrast", "Who Did the Work?", "Sentence"]
                  - ["had + V3 + object", "WE did it earlier (Past Perf.)", "We had calibrated the meter before class."]
                  - ["had + object + V3", "A SPECIALIST did it for us", "We had the meter calibrated at the lab."]
              - numero: 5
                seccion: "CAMPUS & LAB CONTEXT"
                titulo: "Authentic Academic & Engineering Usage"
                puntos:
                  - "The university had fifty solar modules installed on the parking canopy."
                  - "Smart thermostats help households reduce cooling electricity bills."
                  - "A check valve lets fluid flow in one direction and prevents backflow."
                ejemplo: "Academic Register (CEFR B1.2): Clear, concise communication in Unimagdalena seminars."
              - numero: 6
                seccion: "MASTERY CHECK"
                titulo: "Self-Assessment & Oral Drill"
                puntos:
                  - "Rewrite with causative: 'A certified lab tested our oil samples' -> 'We had our oil samples tested.'"
                  - "Choose: 'High voltage makes current (flow / to flow)' -> 'flow' (active) vs. 'Current is made (to flow)' (passive)."
                  - "Write 3 maintenance sentences using 'have/get something done'."
                ejemplo: "Practice reading each model sentence aloud with natural stress and intonation."
          - numero_tema: 9
            corte: 3
            modalidad: "general"
            titulo: "Quantifiers & Determiners (Both, Either, Neither, Each, Every, All)"
            objetivo: "Seleccionar determinantes distributivos y duales con concordancia verbal exacta en textos técnicos."
            concepto_clave_latex: ""
            ejemplo: "Each photovoltaic string is protected by its own DC fuse."
            bloque_sugerido: "Determiner Precision 35 min • Dual vs. plural quantifiers in technical specs"
            slides:
              - numero: 1
                seccion: "CEFR B1.2 • CORE CONCEPT"
                titulo: "Quantifiers & Determiners (Both, Either, Neither, Each, Every, All): Communicative Purpose"
                puntos:
                  - "DUAL (exactly 2 items): 'both' (A + B -> plural verb), 'either' (A or B -> singular noun/verb), 'neither' (not A and not B -> singular verb in formal English)."
                  - "DISTRIBUTIVE (2+ or 3+ items): 'each' (individual items, 2 or more -> singular) vs. 'every' (whole group collectively, 3 or more -> singular)."
                  - "TOTALITY: 'all / whole' ('all the data', 'the whole circuit', 'no + noun' = zero)."
                ejemplo: "Each photovoltaic string is protected by its own DC fuse."
              - numero: 2
                seccion: "STRUCTURE & PATTERNS"
                titulo: "Core Grammatical Blueprint"
                puntos:
                  - "Paired correlatives: 'both A and B', 'either A or B', 'neither A nor B' (verb agrees with the CLOSER subject B in formal prose!)."
                  - "With 'of the': 'both (of) the pumps', 'each of the sensors IS...', 'neither of the models CONVERGES' (formal singular)."
                  - "Notice: 'every' CANNOT be followed directly by 'of' -> use 'every one of the cells'!"
                tabla:
                  - ["Determiner", "Set Size", "Noun & Verb Agreement"]
                  - ["both (of the)", "2 items", "Plural noun + Plural verb"]
                  - ["either / neither", "2 items", "Singular noun + Singular verb (+ of plural)"]
                  - ["each / every", "2+ / 3+ items", "Singular noun + Singular verb"]
              - numero: 3
                seccion: "QUESTIONS & NEGATION"
                titulo: "Interrogative, Negative & Short Answers"
                puntos:
                  - "'None' = 0 out of 3 or more items ('None of the 12 trials failed'), whereas 'neither' = 0 out of 2 items ('Neither of the 2 backups failed')!"
                  - "'All' vs. 'Whole': 'all day / the whole day' (singular countable), 'all electricity' (uncountable — 'whole' doesn't go directly with uncountables)."
                ejemplo: "Neither the primary inverter nor the backup unit was damaged by the surge."
              - numero: 4
                seccion: "PRECISION & CONTRAST"
                titulo: "Key Distinctions & Common Pitfalls"
                puntos:
                  - "Avoid double negatives with 'neither': say 'Neither sensor worked' OR 'Either sensor didn't work' -> NEVER *Neither sensor didn't work*!"
                  - "Never write *every of the panels* -> write 'each of the panels' or 'every panel'."
                tabla:
                  - ["Count of Items", "100% Affirmative", "0% Negative"]
                  - ["Exactly 2", "Both turbines are online.", "Neither turbine is online."]
                  - ["3 or more", "All (five) turbines are online.", "None of the turbines is/are online."]
              - numero: 5
                seccion: "CAMPUS & LAB CONTEXT"
                titulo: "Authentic Academic & Engineering Usage"
                puntos:
                  - "Each photovoltaic string is protected by its own DC fuse."
                  - "Neither the primary inverter nor the backup unit was damaged by the surge."
                  - "Both designs meet efficiency targets, so either option is acceptable."
                ejemplo: "Academic Register (CEFR B1.2): Clear, concise communication in Unimagdalena seminars."
              - numero: 6
                seccion: "MASTERY CHECK"
                titulo: "Self-Assessment & Oral Drill"
                puntos:
                  - "Choose (2 batteries): '(Neither / None) of the two batteries was fully charged' -> 'Neither'."
                  - "Fix: 'Every of the equations was verified' -> 'Each of the equations was verified.'"
                  - "Write 3 sentences comparing two prototypes using both, either...or, and neither...nor."
                ejemplo: "Practice reading each model sentence aloud with natural stress and intonation."
          - numero_tema: 10
            corte: 3
            modalidad: "general"
            titulo: "Reading Strategies for Academic Abstracts & Technical Articles"
            objetivo: "Extraer con rapidez objetivos, metodología, resultados numéricos y conclusiones de abstracts científicos en inglés."
            concepto_clave_latex: ""
            ejemplo: "This paper investigates the thermal performance of a hybrid PV-thermal collector."
            bloque_sugerido: "IEEE Abstract Lab 45 min • Skimming, scanning & unpacking dense noun phrases"
            slides:
              - numero: 1
                seccion: "CEFR B1.2 • CORE CONCEPT"
                titulo: "Reading Strategies for Academic Abstracts & Technical Articles: Communicative Purpose"
                puntos:
                  - "Every standard engineering abstract mirrors 4–5 micro-moves (~150–250 words): (1) Background/Gap, (2) Objective ('This paper proposes/investigates...'), (3) Methodology ('Using a 3D CFD model...'), (4) Key Quantitative Results ('achieving a 14.2% reduction'), (5) Conclusion/Impact."
                  - "Skimming = reading title, headings, first/last sentences for global gist in 60 seconds."
                  - "Scanning = hunting rapidly for specific numbers, units, equations, acronyms, or benchmarks."
                ejemplo: "This paper investigates the thermal performance of a hybrid PV-thermal collector."
              - numero: 2
                seccion: "STRUCTURE & PATTERNS"
                titulo: "Core Grammatical Blueprint"
                puntos:
                  - "Tense map in abstracts: Background/Gap -> Present Simple / Present Perfect; Objective -> Present Simple ('This study evaluates'); Methods & Specific Results -> Past Simple Passive ('was simulated'); Implications -> Present / Modals ('can accelerate')."
                  - "Gap-signaling words: 'However, little attention has been paid to...', 'remains challenging', 'limited data exist on...'."
                tabla:
                  - ["Abstract Move", "Typical Signal Phrase", "Dominant Tense"]
                  - ["1–2. Gap & Aim", "However,... This study proposes...", "Present Perfect / Present"]
                  - ["3–4. Method & Result", "...was modeled using... reached 94%", "Past Simple (often Passive)"]
                  - ["5. Conclusion", "These findings demonstrate that...", "Present Simple / Modal"]
              - numero: 3
                seccion: "QUESTIONS & NEGATION"
                titulo: "Interrogative, Negative & Short Answers"
                puntos:
                  - "Dense Noun Compounds in English read RIGHT-TO-LEFT: 'a grid-connected solar photovoltaic power plant' -> core noun is 'plant', modified leftward!"
                  - "Track reference words (this, these, such, the former, the latter, respectively) to decode numerical mappings accurately!"
                ejemplo: "Peak efficiencies of 19.4% and 62.0% were achieved for electrical and thermal outputs, respectively."
              - numero: 4
                seccion: "PRECISION & CONTRAST"
                titulo: "Key Distinctions & Common Pitfalls"
                puntos:
                  - "Pay special attention to 'respectively': 'Peak outputs for Units A and B were 12 kW and 18 kW, respectively' (A = 12 kW, B = 18 kW)."
                  - "Don't translate word-by-word; parse the main verb first, then unpack prepositional phrases."
                tabla:
                  - ["Cohesive Device", "Function", "Technical Example"]
                  - ["the former / the latter", "1st item / 2nd item", "Between PV and wind, the latter runs at night."]
                  - ["respectively", "1-to-1 ordered mapping", "V and I were 48 V and 5 A, respectively."]
              - numero: 5
                seccion: "CAMPUS & LAB CONTEXT"
                titulo: "Authentic Academic & Engineering Usage"
                puntos:
                  - "This paper investigates the thermal performance of a hybrid PV-thermal collector."
                  - "Peak efficiencies of 19.4% and 62.0% were achieved for electrical and thermal outputs, respectively."
                  - "These results suggest that phase-change materials can mitigate overheating."
                ejemplo: "Academic Register (CEFR B1.2): Clear, concise communication in Unimagdalena seminars."
              - numero: 6
                seccion: "MASTERY CHECK"
                titulo: "Self-Assessment & Oral Drill"
                puntos:
                  - "Unpack the noun phrase: 'high-voltage direct-current transmission line losses'."
                  - "Identify the 5 abstract moves in a sample 150-word IEEE abstract."
                  - "Write a 4-sentence mini-abstract for an Unimagdalena course project."
                ejemplo: "Practice reading each model sentence aloud with natural stress and intonation."
          - numero_tema: 11
            corte: 3
            modalidad: "general"
            titulo: "Inversion with Negative & Restrictive Adverbials in Engineering Writing"
            objetivo: "Utilizar la inversión sintáctica (Auxiliar + Sujeto + Verbo) tras adverbios negativos y restrictivos (Rarely, Seldom, Not only, Under no circumstances) para enfatizar condiciones críticas de seguridad y rendimiento."
            concepto_clave_latex: ""
            ejemplo: "Under no circumstances should the high-voltage disconnect switch be operated under load, nor should maintenance personnel enter the enclosure without grounding the busbars."
            bloque_sugerido: "Speaking Drill 30 min • Negative inversion in technical manuals & safety warnings"
            slides:
              - numero: 1
                seccion: "CEFR B2 • COMMUNICATIVE PURPOSE"
                titulo: "Inversion for Rhetorical & Safety Emphasis"
                puntos:
                  - "Standard word order is inverted to create a dramatic, formal, or authoritative tone."
                  - "Frequently used in IEEE journal conclusions, patent documentation, and critical industrial operating instructions."
                  - "Draws immediate listener/reader attention to exceptional events or strict prohibitions."
                ejemplo: "Seldom has a combined-cycle power facility achieved an overall thermal efficiency exceeding sixty-three percent."
              - numero: 2
                seccion: "STRUCTURE & PATTERNS"
                titulo: "Morphological Blueprint"
                puntos:
                  - "Formula: Negative Adverbial + Auxiliary / Modal Verb + Subject + Main Verb."
                  - "Rarely do renewable microgrids experience complete blackouts when equipped with battery storage."
                  - "Not only did the inverter mitigate voltage sags, but it also eliminated harmonic distortion."
              - numero: 3
                seccion: "KEY RESTRICTIVE ADVERBIALS"
                titulo: "High-Frequency Technical Markers"
                puntos:
                  - "'Hardly had the steam turbine synchronized when the bearing temperature alarm activated.'"
                  - "'Only after conducting a dielectric oil analysis can the transformer be safely re-energized.'"
                  - "'At no time must the combustible gas concentration exceed ten percent of the lower explosive limit.'"
              - numero: 4
                seccion: "COMMON ERRORS & PITFALLS"
                titulo: "Auxiliary Insertion & Word Order"
                puntos:
                  - "Incorrect: 'Rarely the generator trips' -> Correct: 'Rarely does the generator trip.'"
                  - "Do not forget subject-auxiliary inversion after 'Only when / Only after' clauses: 'Only after the engineers verified the telemetry did they open the valve.'"
                  - "Avoid double negatives."
              - numero: 5
                seccion: "AUTHENTIC COMMISSIONING DIALOGUE"
                titulo: "Grid Tie-in Safety Briefing"
                puntos:
                  - "Chief Inspector: 'Under no circumstances are technicians to bypass the interlock mechanism.'"
                  - "Commissioning Lead: 'Understood. Not until the lockout-tagout log is fully signed will the main breaker close.'"
              - numero: 6
                seccion: "ORAL DRILL"
                titulo: "Inversion Transformation Drill"
                puntos:
                  - "Prompt: 'We have never witnessed such severe cavitation.' -> 'Never have we witnessed such severe cavitation in a Francis runner.'"
                  - "Prompt: 'The solar farm not only generated surplus power, but it also stabilized local grid frequency.' -> 'Not only did the solar farm generate surplus power, but it also stabilized local grid frequency.'"
          - numero_tema: 12
            corte: 3
            modalidad: "general"
            titulo: "Advanced Cleft Sentences (It-Clefts & Wh-Clefts) to Focus Technical Arguments"
            objetivo: "Estructurar oraciones hendidas (cleft sentences) para aislar variables determinantes y destacar hallazgos experimentales específicos en presentaciones académicas."
            concepto_clave_latex: ""
            ejemplo: "It was the degradation of the ethylene-vinyl acetate encapsulant that triggered the accelerated delamination in the photovoltaic modules."
            bloque_sugerido: "Speaking Drill 30 min • Cleft sentences in scientific presentations"
            slides:
              - numero: 1
                seccion: "CEFR B2 • COMMUNICATIVE PURPOSE"
                titulo: "Focalizing Key Engineering Variables"
                puntos:
                  - "Cleft sentences split a single clause into two parts to highlight the most critical piece of technical information."
                  - "Answers the implicit question: 'What was the exact root cause of the observation?'"
                  - "Essential for defending research hypotheses and answering inquisitor panels during thesis defenses."
                ejemplo: "What the CFD simulation revealed was an unexpected recirculation vortex near the nozzle throat."
              - numero: 2
