                seccion: "SERVICIOS AUXILIARES DE SISTEMA"
                titulo: "Inercia Síncrona y Arranque en Negro"
                puntos:
                  - "Aporte de inercia física real y capacidad masiva de arranque autógeno (Black Start) para levantar la red nacional tras un apagón."
                  - "Capacidad de transición de modo bombeo a modo turbinado en menos de 90 a 120 segundos."
                  - "Herramienta crítica para absorber el vertimiento masivo (curtailable power) de parques solares durante el mediodía."
          - numero_tema: 26
            corte: 3
            modalidad: "teorico"
            titulo: "Conversión de Energía a Gas (Power-to-Gas / P2X): Electrólisis, Metanación y Almacenamiento Químico"
            objetivo: "Modelar plantas P2G (Power-to-Gas) integrando electrolizadores de baja y alta temperatura (PEM, Alcalinos y SOEC) con reactores catalíticos de metanación de Sabatier."
            concepto_clave_latex: "\\text{CO}_2 + 4\\text{H}_2 \\rightleftharpoons \\text{CH}_4 + 2\\text{H}_2\\text{O} \\quad ; \\quad \\Delta H_{298}^\\circ = -165.0 \\text{ kJ/mol} \\quad ; \\quad \\eta_{P2G} = \\frac{\\dot{m}_{CH_4} \\cdot \\text{LHV}_{CH_4}}{\\dot{W}_{electrica}}"
            ejemplo: "Problema 1: Una planta de Power-to-Gas (P2G) instalada junto a un parque eólico marino aprovecha 100 MW de excedentes de electricidad para alimentar un electrolizador PEM (eficiencia de celda del 68% en base HHV, consumo específico de 50 kWh por cada kg de H2 producido). Producción de hidrógeno verde: dot{m}_H2 = 100,000 kW / 50 kWh/kg = 2000 kg/hora (1000 kmol/h de H2). El hidrógeno producido se introduce en un reactor catalítico de metanación termoquímica de Sabatier con lecho fijo de níquel a 350 °C y 15 bar, junto con una corriente purificada de dióxido de carbono capturado de una planta de biogás. La estequiometría de Sabatier exige 1 mol de CO2 por cada 4 moles de H2. Flujo de CO2 requerido: dot{n}_CO2 = 1000 / 4 = 250 kmol/h = 250 * 44 = 11,000 kg/h = 11.0 toneladas/hora de CO2 capturado y neutralizado. Suponiendo una selectividad y conversión del 98%: Producción de metano sintético (SNG): dot{n}_CH4 = 250 * 0.98 = 245 kmol/h = 245 * 16.04 = 3930 kg/h de metano renovable. Con LHV_CH4 = 50.0 MJ/kg (13.89 kWh/kg), la potencia química del gas sintético inyectable a la red es: P_SNG = 3930 * 13.89 kWh = 54,588 kW = 54.59 MW. Eficiencia global Power-to-Methane de la planta: eta_P2M = 54.59 MW / 100 MW = 54.59%. Calor exotérmico de la reacción de Sabatier recuperado a 300 °C: Q_exo = 245,000 mol/h * 165,000 J/mol / 3.6 * 10^9 = 11.23 MW_th. Al utilizar este calor en una red distrital, la eficiencia global de aprovechamiento de la planta se eleva al 65.82%. Problema 2: Los electrolizadores de óxido sólido de alta temperatura (SOEC a 800 °C) reducen el consumo eléctrico a 38-40 kWh/kg de H2 utilizando calor de desecho industrial para vaporizar el agua."
            bloque_sugerido: "Power-to-Gas 45 min • Cinética de Sabatier y balances de electrolizadores PEM/SOEC"
            slides:
              - numero: 1
                seccion: "ALMACENAMIENTO QUÍMICO MOLECULAR"
                titulo: "Electrólisis y Metanación Catalítica"
                puntos:
                  - "Permite desacoplar estacionalmente la energía: almacenar excedentes renovables de primavera/verano para consumirlos en invierno."
                  - "El metano sintético (e-metano) es químicamente idéntico al gas natural convencional (drop-in fuel)."
                  - "Se transporta y almacena directamente utilizando la red de gasoductos e instalaciones subterráneas de gas existentes."

                seccion: "ECONOMÍA CIRCULAR DEL CARBONO"
                titulo: "Captura y Utilización de Carbono (CCU)"
                puntos:

                  - "Sustenta la producción de e-combustibles para la aviación (e-kerosene) y el transporte marítimo (e-metanol)."
                  - "El factor crítico de viabilidad económica es acceder a electricidad renovable de bajo costo (< 25 USD/MWh) y alto factor de carga."
          - numero_tema: 27
            corte: 3
            modalidad: "teorico"
            titulo: "Confiabilidad y Seguridad de Redes de Energía: Análisis N-1, LOLP y Confiabilidad Compuesta"
            objetivo: "Calcular la probabilidad de pérdida de carga (LOLP), la energía esperada no suministrada (EENS) y la seguridad de red N-1 bajo fallas fortuitas en generadores y líneas de transmisión."
            concepto_clave_latex: "\\text{LOLP} = \\sum_{j} P(C_j) \\cdot t_j \\quad [\\text{días/año}] \\quad ; \\quad \\text{FOR}_i = \\frac{\\text{FOH}_i}{\\text{SH}_i + \\text{FOH}_i} \\quad ; \\quad \\text{EENS} = \\sum (D_j - C_j) P_j"
            ejemplo: "Problema 1: Un sistema de potencia aislado tiene una demanda diaria constante de 80 MW durante un año y cuenta con cuatro unidades generadoras térmicas idénticas de 30 MW cada una (capacidad instalada total = 120 MW). La tasa de salidas forzadas fortuitas (Forced Outage Rate - FOR) de cada unidad es p = 0.08, con disponibilidad q = 1 - p = 0.92. Se construye la Tabla de Probabilidad de Capacidad de Salida (COPT) mediante la distribución binomial: 1) Estado 0 unidades fuera (Capacidad disponible = 120 MW > 80 MW, déficit = 0): P_0 = (0.92)^4 = 0.71639. 2) Estado 1 unidad fuera (Capacidad disponible = 90 MW > 80 MW, déficit = 0): P_1 = 4 * (0.08)^1 * (0.92)^3 = 0.24918. 3) Estado 2 unidades fuera (Capacidad disponible = 60 MW < 80 MW, déficit = 20 MW): P_2 = 6 * (0.08)^2 * (0.92)^2 = 0.03250. 4) Estado 3 unidades fuera (Capacidad disponible = 30 MW < 80 MW, déficit = 50 MW): P_3 = 4 * (0.08)^3 * (0.92)^1 = 0.00188. 5) Estado 4 unidades fuera (Capacidad disponible = 0 MW, déficit = 80 MW): P_4 = (0.08)^4 = 0.00004. Pérdida de carga ocurre si fallan 2 o más unidades (capacidad < 80 MW): Probabilidad de déficit: P_falla = P_2 + P_3 + P_4 = 0.03250 + 0.00188 + 0.00004 = 0.03442. Índice LOLP en horas por año: LOLP = 0.03442 * 8760 horas/año = 301.52 horas/año. Energía Esperada No Suministrada (EENS): EENS = [20 MW * 0.03250 + 50 MW * 0.00188 + 80 MW * 0.00004] * 8760 = [0.6500 + 0.0940 + 0.0032] * 8760 = 0.7472 MW * 8760 h = 6545.47 MWh/año. Con un costo de energía no servida (Value of Lost Load - VOLL) de 2500 USD/MWh, el costo social de la no confiabilidad del sistema es de 16,363,675 USD anuales, justificando sobradamente la adición de una quinta unidad de reserva N-1. Problema 2: El criterio de seguridad estática N-1 en redes malladas exige que el disparo imprevisto de cualquier línea de transmisión no sobrecargue los transformadores restantes más allá de su capacidad de emergencia."
            bloque_sugerido: "Confiabilidad de Sistemas de Potencia 45 min • Construcción de COPT y cálculo de LOLP/EENS"
            slides:
              - numero: 1
                seccion: "PROBABILIDAD APLICADA A REDES ELÉCTRICAS"
                titulo: "Índices Cuantitativos de Adecuación"
                puntos:
                  - "LOLP (Loss of Load Probability): Mide el número esperado de días u horas al año en que la demanda excede la capacidad de generación disponible."
                  - "El estándar internacional clásico exige un LOLP inferior a '1 día en 10 años' (0.1 días/año = 2.4 horas/año)."
                  - "EENS (Expected Energy Not Served): Cuantifica los megavatios-hora reales que no podrán abastecerse, clave para el análisis costo-beneficio."
              - numero: 2
                seccion: "CRITERIO DETERMINÍSTICO N-1"
                titulo: "Seguridad Operativa y Redundancia"
                puntos:
                  - "Exige que la red continúe operando de forma segura y sin cortes tras la pérdida intempestiva del elemento más crítico."
                  - "Análisis de Contingencias AC rápido: Evalúa en milisegundos las sobretensiones y sobrecargas ante disparos de interruptores."
                  - "Regulado estrictamente por el CNO (Consejo Nacional de Operación) y XM en el Sistema Interconectado Nacional de Colombia."
          - numero_tema: 28
            corte: 3
            modalidad: "teorico"
            titulo: "Evaluación de Impacto Ambiental y Factores de Emisión Marginales en Redes Eléctricas"
            objetivo: "Calcular los factores de emisión marginales horarios (MEF) y el balance de ciclo de vida (LCA) de GEI en redes eléctricas con alta penetración renovable."
            concepto_clave_latex: "\\text{MEF}_t = \\frac{\\Delta \\text{Emisiones}_t}{\\Delta \\text{Demanda}_t} \\quad \\left[\\frac{\\text{kg CO}_2\\text{e}}{\\text{MWh}}\\right] \\quad ; \\quad \\text{GHG}_{LCA} = \\sum_i E_i \\cdot \\text{EF}_{LCA,i}"
            ejemplo: "Problema 1: En una red eléctrica regional interconectada, la demanda promedio en horas de la madrugada (02:00 h) es de 4200 MW, cubierta por 2500 MW de hidroeléctricas de pasada (EF = 0 kg/MWh), 1000 MW de eólica (EF = 0 kg/MWh) y 700 MW de una planta termoeléctrica de carbón que actúa como unidad marginal de rampa (consumo específico = 10,200 kJ/kWh, factor de emisión de carbón = 94.6 kg CO2/GJ ==> EF_carbon = 0.965 kg CO2/kWh = 965 kg CO2/MWh). El Factor de Emisión Promedio en la red a esa hora es: AEF = (700 * 965 + 3500 * 0) / 4200 = 675,500 / 4200 = 160.83 kg CO2/MWh. Sin embargo, si una flota de 10,000 vehículos eléctricos decide cargar sus baterías a las 02:00 h incrementando la demanda en Delta_D = 50 MW, la única unidad técnica con capacidad de subir su potencia es la central térmica de carbón. El Factor de Emisión Marginal es: MEF = Delta_Emisiones / Delta_Demanda = (50 MW * 965 kg/MWh) / 50 MW = 965 kg CO2/MWh. Por tanto, calcular el beneficio ambiental de los vehículos usando el factor promedio (160.8 kg/MWh) subestimaría las emisiones reales inducidas en casi 6 veces. A las 12:00 h del mediodía, con saturación y vertimiento de energía solar fotovoltaica, la unidad marginal es el vertimiento renovable (MEF = 0 kg CO2/MWh), demostrando que la carga diurna es infinitamente más limpia. Problema 2: El análisis de ciclo de vida (LCA) 'cuna a tumba' de paneles solares fotovoltaicos revela que sus emisiones integradas oscilan entre 25 y 45 g CO2e/kWh, generadas principalmente durante la purificación del silicio cuarzo a 1800 °C en hornos de arco."
            bloque_sugerido: "Sostenibilidad y Emisiones 45 min • Cálculo de factores de emisión marginales horarios MEF"
            slides:
              - numero: 1
                seccion: "HUELLA DE CARBONO EN SISTEMAS ENERGÉTICOS"
                titulo: "Factor Promedio vs Factor Marginal"
                puntos:
                  - "Factor Promedio (AEF): Divide las emisiones totales de la red entre la generación total; útil únicamente para contabilidad de huella corporativa retroactiva."
                  - "Factor Marginal (MEF): Identifica la planta específica que arranca o frena cuando la demanda varía en 1 MWh adicional."
                  - "Cualquier política de eficiencia energética o electrificación de transporte debe evaluarse obligatoriamente con el MEF."
              - numero: 2
                seccion: "ANÁLISIS DE CICLO DE VIDA (LCA)"
                titulo: "Metodología Cuna-a-Tumba (ISO 14040/44)"
                puntos:
                  - "Evalúa las emisiones indirectas de fabricación, minería de materiales críticos (litio, cobre, neodimio), transporte y desmantelamiento."
                  - "Tiempo de Retorno de Carbono (Carbon Payback Time): Tiempo que tarda una tecnología limpia en evitar las emisiones emitidas en su propia construcción."
                  - "Los parques eólicos y solares modernos devuelven toda su energía de fabricación en menos de 10 a 14 meses de operación."
          - numero_tema: 29
            corte: 3
            modalidad: "teorico"
            titulo: "Modelación y Optimización de Redes Multi-Vectoriales usando Grafos Energéticos"
            objetivo: "Formular el flujo óptimo de energía multi-red (Multi-Energy Optimal Power Flow - ME-OPF) acoplando ecuaciones de flujo DC/AC con las ecuaciones hidráulicas no lineales de gas y calefacción mediante teoría de grafos."
            concepto_clave_latex: "\\min_{\\mathbf{x}} f(\\mathbf{x}) \\quad \\text{s.t.} \\quad \\mathbf{A}_e \\mathbf{f}_e = \\mathbf{P}_e \\quad ; \\quad \\mathbf{A}_g \\mathbf{f}_g = \\mathbf{P}_g \\quad ; \\quad \\mathbf{A}_h \\mathbf{f}_h = \\mathbf{P}_h \\quad ; \\quad g_k(\\mathbf{x}) \\le 0"
            ejemplo: "Problema 1: Un sistema multi-vectorial modelado como un grafo conexo G = (V, E) cuenta con 3 nodos donde coexisten infraestructura eléctrica y de gas natural. Nodo 1: Generador eólico de 80 MW y punto de inyección de gas a 60 bar. Nodo 2: Central de ciclo combinado CCGT (consume gas para generar electricidad) y compresor de gas accionado por motor eléctrico. Nodo 3: Centro de carga con demanda eléctrica L_e = 60 MW y demanda de gas L_g = 40,000 m^3/h. Las matrices de incidencia nodo-arista A_e y A_g describen la topología de las líneas de transmisión y tuberías. Cuando la línea eléctrica directa 1-3 alcanza su límite térmico de transmisión de 45 MW, se produce una congestión de red eléctrica. El despachador multi-vectorial ejecuta el algoritmo ME-OPF: en lugar de encender un generador diésel caro y contaminante en el Nodo 3, inyecta gas adicional en la tubería 1-2, utiliza la central CCGT del Nodo 2 para convertir gas en electricidad local y transporta el resto a través de la línea 2-3 (descongestión indirecta de la red eléctrica mediante la infraestructura de gasoductos). El algoritmo reduce las pérdidas combinadas del sistema en un 18.4% comparado con la operación desacoplada tradicional. Problema 2: En redes de calefacción distrital, el método de las matrices de lazo de grafo permite calcular simultáneamente la distribución no lineal de presiones de agua y la temperatura de llegada a cada subestación considerando el retardo de transporte por velocidad finita."
            bloque_sugerido: "Optimización Multi-Red 45 min • Formulación de flujos de carga multi-vector con grafos"
            slides:
              - numero: 1
                seccion: "TEORÍA DE GRAFOS APLICADA A LA ENERGÍA"
                titulo: "Topología Unificada de Flujos"
                puntos:
                  - "Representa cualquier red física (líneas eléctricas, tuberías de vapor, gasoductos, acueductos) mediante matrices de incidencia nodo-arista."
                  - "Aplica las leyes de Kirchhoff generalizadas: conservación de flujo en los vértices y caída de potencial en las aristas."
                  - "Facilita la formulación matemática de problemas complejos de optimización no lineal para solvers computacionales modernos."
              - numero: 2
                seccion: "BENEFICIOS DE LA OPERACIÓN ACOPLADA"
                titulo: "Descongestión y Redundancia Cruzada"
                puntos:
                  - "Permite 'eludir' cuellos de botella en la red eléctrica transportando energía a través de la red de gasoductos o redes térmicas."
                  - "Aumenta la resiliencia del suministro urbano ante eventos climáticos extremos o fallas en subestaciones eléctricas."
                  - "Base científica indispensable para el despliegue de las Ciudades Inteligentes (Smart Cities) y Distritos de Energía Neta Cero."
          - numero_tema: 30
            corte: 3
            modalidad: "teorico"
            titulo: "Planificación Energética a Largo Plazo hacia Emisiones Netas Cero: Modelos TIMES y OSeMOSYS"
            objetivo: "Diseñar planes de transición y expansión de sistemas energéticos a escala país con horizontes a 2050 evaluando trayectorias de costo mínimo hacia la neutralidad de carbono mediante modelos TIMES/OSeMOSYS."
            concepto_clave_latex: "\\min \\sum_{r,y} \\text{DiscountFactor}_{r,y} \\cdot \\left[ \\text{CapitalCost} + \\text{FixedCost} + \\text{VariableCost} + \\text{ImportCost} - \\text{SalvageValue} \\right]"
            ejemplo: "Problema 1: Un modelo de optimización energética de horizonte temporal de 30 años (2020 a 2050 en tramos quinquenales) evalúa la trayectoria de expansión de generación eléctrica de Colombia para alcanzar Net-Zero CO2 en 2050 bajo una tasa de descuento social r = 8%. La demanda eléctrica proyectada crece de 75 TWh/año en 2020 a 160 TWh/año en 2050 impulsada por la electrificación del transporte y la industria. En el año 2025, el modelo debe decidir entre instalar 5 GW de parques solares fotovoltaicos (CAPEX = 750 USD/kW, OPEX fijo = 12 USD/kW-año, factor de planta = 22%) o 3 GW de ciclos combinados de gas natural (CAPEX = 900 USD/kW, eficiencia = 60%, costo gas = 5.5 USD/GJ) con una penalización por impuesto al carbono que sube de 5 USD/tCO2 en 2025 a 80 USD/tCO2 en 2040. Función de minimización del Valor Presente Neto (VPN) de costos totales del sistema: A partir de 2030, la trayectoria de costo mínimo descarta toda nueva construcción fósil y fuerza la penetración de 22 GW de energía solar fotovoltaica, 14 GW de eólica marina y terrestre en La Guajira, 4 GW de hidroeléctricas reversibles y 3 GW de almacenamiento térmico CSP. El modelo demuestra que el costo nivelado de transición (LCOE del sistema) se reduce en un 24.6% comparado con el escenario inercial 'Business As Usual', neutralizando 45 millones de toneladas de CO2 anuales para el año 2050. Problema 2: En la metodología OSeMOSYS (Open Source Energy Modelling System), la ecuación de balance de actividad relaciona dinámicamente la extracción de recursos primarios, la transformación en refinerías y centrales, y el consumo final de servicios energéticos por sectores."
            bloque_sugerido: "Planificación Energética 45 min • Modelos de optimización de largo plazo TIMES y Net-Zero 2050"
            slides:
              - numero: 1
                seccion: "MODELACIÓN ENERGÉTICA MACROECONÓMICA"
                titulo: "Modelos Bottom-up vs Top-down"
                puntos:
                  - "Modelos Bottom-up (TIMES, MARKAL, OSeMOSYS): Describen explícitamente cientos de tecnologías energéticas con sus costos y eficiencias reales."
                  - "Modelos Top-down (CGE): Modelos macroeconómicos de equilibrio general que evalúan el impacto de las políticas en el PIB, empleo e inflación."
                  - "Permiten a los ministerios y entidades de planeación (UPME en Colombia) formular los Planes de Expansión de Referencia Generación-Transmisión."
              - numero: 2
                seccion: "LA RUTA HACIA EL NET-ZERO 2050"
                titulo: "Culminación del Ingeniero Energético"
                puntos:
                  - "Integración holística de termodinámica, electrotecnia, economía, regulación y sostenibilidad ambiental."
                  - "Planifica la sustitución ordenada de combustibles fósiles garantizando la seguridad de abastecimiento y la soberanía energética."
                  - "El egresado de Ingeniería Energética de la Universidad del Magdalena lidera la transformación hacia una matriz limpia y equitativa."
  - cuatrimestre: 6
    creditos_totales: 13
    asignaturas:
      - codigo: "01021806"
        nombre: "General English V"
        creditos: 2
        obligatoria: true
        categoria: "FORMACION_GENERAL"
        color: "#8E8E93"
        temas:
          - numero_tema: 1
            corte: 1
            modalidad: "general"
            titulo: "Inversion with Negative Adverbials (Not only... but also, Rarely, Seldom)"
            objetivo: "Aplicar inversión sujeto-auxiliar tras adverbios negativos y restrictivos para lograr énfasis retórico de nivel B2/C1."
            concepto_clave_latex: ""
            ejemplo: "Not only does cogeneration generate electricity, but it also recovers useful process heat."
            bloque_sugerido: "Rhetorical Emphasis 40 min • C1/B2 inversion in keynote openings & papers"
            slides:
              - numero: 1
                seccion: "CEFR B2 • CORE CONCEPT"
                titulo: "Inversion with Negative Adverbials (Not only... but also, Rarely, Seldom): Communicative Purpose"
                puntos:
                  - "When a negative or restrictive adverbial opens a sentence for rhetorical emphasis, INVERT the auxiliary and subject (just like a question!)."
                  - "Core triggers: Not only... but (also)..., Rarely, Seldom, Never (before), Little, Under no circumstances, Hardly... when, No sooner... than."
                  - "If no auxiliary is visible (Present/Past Simple), insert DO / DOES / DID + base verb!"
                ejemplo: "Not only does cogeneration generate electricity, but it also recovers useful process heat."
              - numero: 2
                seccion: "STRUCTURE & PATTERNS"
                titulo: "Core Grammatical Blueprint"
                puntos:
                  - "Not only: 'Not only DOES solar PV cut emissions, but it also lowers peak tariffs.'"
                  - "Rarely / Seldom: 'Rarely HAVE battery costs fallen so rapidly.'"
                  - "Only after / Only by + X (invert the MAIN clause!): 'Only by insulating the core CAN we prevent losses.'"
                tabla:
                  - ["Fronted Adverbial", "Inverted Pattern", "High-Impact Academic Example"]
                  - ["Not only...", "Not only + aux + S + V", "Not only did yield rise, but noise fell."]
                  - ["Rarely / Seldom", "Rarely + aux + S + V", "Seldom does efficiency exceed 60%."]
                  - ["Under no circumstances", "Under no... + modal + S + V", "Under no circumstances must fuses be bypassed."]
              - numero: 3
                seccion: "QUESTIONS & NEGATION"
                titulo: "Interrogative, Negative & Short Answers"
                puntos:
                  - "Pairs to memorize: 'Hardly / Scarcely had S + V3 WHEN...' vs. 'No sooner had S + V3 THAN...' ('No sooner had the fault occurred than the relay isolated it')."
                ejemplo: "Seldom do real thermodynamic cycles approach the theoretical Carnot limit."
              - numero: 4
                seccion: "PRECISION & CONTRAST"
                titulo: "Key Distinctions & Common Pitfalls"
                puntos:
                  - "Watch 'Only when / Not until': do NOT invert the subordinate clause itself — invert the MAIN clause that follows! ('Not until voltage stabilized DID we connect the load')."
                tabla:
                  - ["Trigger Type", "Where Inversion Happens", "Correct Sentence"]
                  - ["Immediate (Never/Rarely)", "Right after adverb", "Never have we observed zero lag."]
                  - ["Delayed (Only when + S+V)", "In the 2nd (main) clause", "Only when T drops DO fans stop."]
              - numero: 5
                seccion: "CAMPUS & LAB CONTEXT"
                titulo: "Authentic Academic & Engineering Usage"
                puntos:
                  - "Not only does cogeneration generate electricity, but it also recovers useful process heat."
                  - "Seldom do real thermodynamic cycles approach the theoretical Carnot limit."
                  - "Only through rigorous grid modeling can high renewable penetration remain stable."
                ejemplo: "Academic Register (CEFR B2): Clear, concise communication in Unimagdalena seminars."
              - numero: 6
                seccion: "MASTERY CHECK"
                titulo: "Self-Assessment & Oral Drill"
                puntos:
                  - "Invert: 'We have never recorded such high irradiance' -> 'Never have we recorded...'"
                  - "Invert: 'The solver converged only after reducing the step size' -> 'Only after reducing the step size did the solver converge.'"
                  - "Write 3 persuasive pitch openings using Not only, Rarely, and Under no circumstances."
                ejemplo: "Practice reading each model sentence aloud with natural stress and intonation."
          - numero_tema: 2
            corte: 1
            modalidad: "general"
            titulo: "Cleft Sentences for Emphasis (What we need is..., It was X that...)"
            objetivo: "Reestructurar oraciones mediante It-clefts y Wh-clefts para focalizar hallazgos, causas o soluciones técnicas."
            concepto_clave_latex: ""
            ejemplo: "What distinguishes green hydrogen from gray hydrogen is zero-carbon electrolysis."
            bloque_sugerido: "Pitch Focus Drill 35 min • Highlighting key findings with It- & Wh-clefts"
            slides:
              - numero: 1
                seccion: "CEFR B2 • CORE CONCEPT"
                titulo: "Cleft Sentences for Emphasis (What we need is..., It was X that...): Communicative Purpose"
                puntos:
                  - "Cleft ('split') sentences divide a single message into two clauses so the spotlight lands squarely on new or contrasting information."
                  - "It-Cleft: 'It is / was + [FOCUSED ELEMENT] + that / who + rest of clause.'"
                  - "Pseudo-Cleft (Wh-Cleft): 'What + S + V + is / was + [FOCUSED ELEMENT / (to) V].'"
                ejemplo: "What distinguishes green hydrogen from gray hydrogen is zero-carbon electrolysis."
              - numero: 2
                seccion: "STRUCTURE & PATTERNS"
                titulo: "Core Grammatical Blueprint"
                puntos:
                  - "Focusing a cause (It-cleft): 'It was harmonic distortion that triggered the inverter trip (not overvoltage).'"
                  - "Focusing an action/need (What-cleft): 'What stabilizes the microgrid is fast battery frequency response.'"
                  - "Noun-head clefts: 'The reason why...', 'The parameter that matters most is...'."
                tabla:
                  - ["Cleft Type", "Blueprint", "Focused Engineering Sentence"]
                  - ["It-cleft", "It is/was + X + that...", "It was in 2021 that Law 2099 took effect."]
                  - ["What-cleft (Noun)", "What + S + V + is + X", "What limits range is energy density."]
                  - ["What-cleft (Verb)", "What + S + do + is (to) V", "What MPPT does is track peak power."]
              - numero: 3
                seccion: "QUESTIONS & NEGATION"
                titulo: "Interrogative, Negative & Short Answers"
                puntos:
                  - "Agreement note: 'It is/was' stays singular even if X is plural ('It is transmission bottlenecks that delay projects')."
                  - "'All (that) S + V + is...' emphasizes simplicity: 'All the operator needs to do is press Reset.'"
                ejemplo: "It was the sudden reactive power imbalance that caused the voltage sag."
              - numero: 4
                seccion: "PRECISION & CONTRAST"
                titulo: "Key Distinctions & Common Pitfalls"
                puntos:
                  - "Do not use 'what' right after a noun (*The factor what limits...* -> 'The factor that limits...' OR 'What limits yield is...')."
                  - "Use clefts selectively (1–2 per section/slide) for maximum rhetorical contrast!"
                tabla:
                  - ["Neutral Sentence", "Focused Element", "Cleft Transformation"]
                  - ["Fouling reduced heat transfer.", "Fouling (the cause)", "It was fouling that reduced heat transfer."]
                  - ["We need grid-scale storage.", "Grid-scale storage", "What we need is grid-scale storage."]
              - numero: 5
                seccion: "CAMPUS & LAB CONTEXT"
                titulo: "Authentic Academic & Engineering Usage"
                puntos:
                  - "What distinguishes green hydrogen from gray hydrogen is zero-carbon electrolysis."
                  - "It was the sudden reactive power imbalance that caused the voltage sag."
                  - "What our CDIO prototype demonstrates is low-cost solar desalination for coastal towns."
                ejemplo: "Academic Register (CEFR B2): Clear, concise communication in Unimagdalena seminars."
              - numero: 6
                seccion: "MASTERY CHECK"
                titulo: "Self-Assessment & Oral Drill"
                puntos:
                  - "Focus 'thermal resistance' using an It-cleft: 'Thermal resistance governs heat flux.'"
                  - "Rewrite with 'What...': 'Smart inverters provide reactive voltage support.'"
                  - "Craft 3 punchy presentation takeaways using cleft structures."
                ejemplo: "Practice reading each model sentence aloud with natural stress and intonation."
          - numero_tema: 3
            corte: 1
            modalidad: "general"
            titulo: "Participle Clauses (-ing and -ed clauses for Concise Academic Writing)"
            objetivo: "Condensar cláusulas relativas, temporales y causales usando cláusulas de participio para escritura académica concisa."
            concepto_clave_latex: ""
            ejemplo: "Equipped with MPPT tracking, the rooftop array harvested 19% more daily energy."
            bloque_sugerido: "Concise Editing 40 min • Eliminating wordiness & dangling modifiers"
            slides:
              - numero: 1
                seccion: "CEFR B2 • CORE CONCEPT"
                titulo: "Participle Clauses (-ing and -ed clauses for Concise Academic Writing): Communicative Purpose"
                puntos:
                  - "Present Participle (-ing) carries ACTIVE meaning ('Operating at 600°C, the turbine achieves 44% efficiency')."
                  - "Past Participle (-ed / V3) carries PASSIVE meaning ('Connected in series, the twelve cells deliver 14.4 V')."
                  - "Perfect Participle ('Having + V3' / 'Having been + V3') marks a COMPLETED prior step ('Having validated the mesh, we ran transient cases')."
                ejemplo: "Equipped with MPPT tracking, the rooftop array harvested 19% more daily energy."
              - numero: 2
                seccion: "STRUCTURE & PATTERNS"
                titulo: "Core Grammatical Blueprint"
                puntos:
                  - "Replacing relative clauses: 'fluids flowing (= that flow) through pipes' / 'data collected (= that were collected) at noon'."
                  - "Expressing result at sentence end: 'Irradiance surged to 1050 W/m², boosting output to 5.2 kW.'"
                  - "With conjunctions: 'When heated,...', 'While charging,...', 'Once commissioned,...'."
                tabla:
                  - ["Participle Form", "Voice & Timing", "Concise IEEE-Style Sentence"]
                  - ["Verb-ing", "Active (simultaneous/cause)", "Using Python, we automated the fit."]
                  - ["V3 (-ed)", "Passive (condition/state)", "Cooled by water, the core stays at 320 K."]
                  - ["Having + V3", "Active (completed earlier)", "Having calibrated sensors, we began trials."]
              - numero: 3
                seccion: "QUESTIONS & NEGATION"
                titulo: "Interrogative, Negative & Short Answers"
                puntos:
                  - "CRITICAL RULE — Avoid Dangling Participles! The implied subject of the introductory participle MUST match the grammatical subject of the main clause!"
                ejemplo: "Having completed all 20 queue slots, DownloadQueueService buffered new tasks in FIFO order."
              - numero: 4
                seccion: "PRECISION & CONTRAST"
                titulo: "Key Distinctions & Common Pitfalls"
                puntos:
                  - "Dangling error: *Analyzing the graph, a peak appeared at 2 p.m.* (Graphs don't analyze themselves!) -> Fix: 'Analyzing the graph, WE observed a peak at 2 p.m.' OR 'When analyzed, the graph revealed a peak.'"
                tabla:
                  - ["Dangling Participle (Wrong!)", "Aligned Subject (Correct!)"]
                  - ["Testing the circuit, a fuse blew.", "Testing the circuit, we blew a fuse. / While the circuit was being tested, a fuse blew."]
                  - ["Heated to 500 K, we measured expansion.", "Heated to 500 K, the alloy expanded by 0.6%."]
              - numero: 5
                seccion: "CAMPUS & LAB CONTEXT"
                titulo: "Authentic Academic & Engineering Usage"
                puntos:
                  - "Equipped with MPPT tracking, the rooftop array harvested 19% more daily energy."
                  - "Having completed all 20 queue slots, DownloadQueueService buffered new tasks in FIFO order."
                  - "Driven by trade winds, turbines in La Guajira achieve capacity factors above 50%."
                ejemplo: "Academic Register (CEFR B2): Clear, concise communication in Unimagdalena seminars."
              - numero: 6
                seccion: "MASTERY CHECK"
                titulo: "Self-Assessment & Oral Drill"
                puntos:
                  - "Condense: 'Because the steam is superheated to 540°C, it prevents blade erosion.'"
                  - "Fix the dangling participle: 'Using Fourier's law, the heat flux was calculated.'"
                  - "Condense 3 wordy two-clause sentences into crisp IEEE participle clauses."
                ejemplo: "Practice reading each model sentence aloud with natural stress and intonation."
          - numero_tema: 4
            corte: 2
            modalidad: "general"
            titulo: "Subjunctive Mood & Formal Recommendations (It is essential that he be...)"
            objetivo: "Redactar recomendaciones normativas, criterios de diseño y cláusulas formales usando el modo subjuntivo mandativo."
            concepto_clave_latex: ""
            ejemplo: "It is essential that emergency backup power be restored within ten seconds."
            bloque_sugerido: "Policy & Standards Writing 35 min • Formal engineering recommendations"
            slides:
              - numero: 1
                seccion: "CEFR B2 • CORE CONCEPT"
                titulo: "Subjunctive Mood & Formal Recommendations (It is essential that he be...): Communicative Purpose"
                puntos:
                  - "Mandative Subjunctive uses the BARE INFINITIVE (be, remain, operate, NOT be -> 'not exceed') for ALL subjects (including he/she/it!) after 'that'."
                  - "Trigger Verbs: recommend, suggest, insist, demand, require, propose, stipulate."
                  - "Trigger Adjectives: essential, vital, imperative, crucial, mandatory, necessary ('It is imperative that frequency remain within ±0.2 Hz')."
                ejemplo: "It is essential that emergency backup power be restored within ten seconds."
              - numero: 2
                seccion: "STRUCTURE & PATTERNS"
                titulo: "Core Grammatical Blueprint"
                puntos:
                  - "Affirmative Subjunctive: 'IEEE standards require that every inverter BE tested for anti-islanding.'"
                  - "Negative Subjunctive ('not' + bare verb — NO 'do/does'!): 'We recommend that the PDF file NOT exceed 1.2 MB.'"
                  - "British/less formal alternative: 'should + base verb' ('recommend that the valve should be inspected')."
                tabla:
                  - ["Trigger", "Subjunctive Clause", "Key Observation"]
                  - ["insist / require that", "...the chassis BE grounded", "'be', NOT 'is'"]
                  - ["essential / vital that", "...pressure NOT exceed 8 bar", "'not exceed', NOT 'doesn't'"]
                  - ["propose / suggest that", "...each unit UNDERGO testing", "'undergo', NOT 'undergoes'"]
              - numero: 3
                seccion: "QUESTIONS & NEGATION"
                titulo: "Interrogative, Negative & Short Answers"
                puntos:
                  - "Fixed academic subjunctive expressions: 'Suffice it to say...', 'Be that as it may,...', 'If need be,...'"
                ejemplo: "The audit report recommends that the plant replace its steam traps immediately."
              - numero: 4
                seccion: "PRECISION & CONTRAST"
                titulo: "Key Distinctions & Common Pitfalls"
                puntos:
                  - "NEVER write *recommend us to install*! Use either 'recommend installing' OR mandative subjunctive 'recommend that the facility install...'!"
                tabla:
                  - ["Common B1 Error", "C1/B2 Mandative Subjunctive"]
                  - ["The code requires that voltage is stable.", "The code requires that voltage be stable."]
                  - ["They suggested that he doesn't change R.", "They suggested that he not change R."]
              - numero: 5
                seccion: "CAMPUS & LAB CONTEXT"
                titulo: "Authentic Academic & Engineering Usage"
                puntos:
                  - "It is essential that emergency backup power be restored within ten seconds."
                  - "The audit report recommends that the plant replace its steam traps immediately."
                  - "Safety protocols stipulate that no technician work on live high-voltage switchgear alone."
                ejemplo: "Academic Register (CEFR B2): Clear, concise communication in Unimagdalena seminars."
              - numero: 6
                seccion: "MASTERY CHECK"
                titulo: "Self-Assessment & Oral Drill"
                puntos:
                  - "Complete: 'It is crucial that total file size ___ (not surpass) 1.2 MB' -> 'not surpass'."
                  - "Rewrite formally: 'The committee advised the plant to monitor NOx hourly' (use 'recommend that...')."
                  - "Write 3 policy recommendations for campus sustainability using the subjunctive."
                ejemplo: "Practice reading each model sentence aloud with natural stress and intonation."
          - numero_tema: 5
            corte: 2
            modalidad: "general"
            titulo: "Advanced Modals in the Past (Should have, Could have, Must have been)"
            objetivo: "Evaluar retrospectivamente fallas, alternativas no ejecutadas y deducciones probables sobre eventos pasados."
            concepto_clave_latex: ""
            ejemplo: "The inverter tripped at noon; cloud-edge lensing must have caused a brief irradiance spike."
            bloque_sugerido: "Forensic Engineering 40 min • Retrospective fault deduction & design review"
            slides:
              - numero: 1
                seccion: "CEFR B2 • CORE CONCEPT"
                titulo: "Advanced Modals in the Past (Should have, Could have, Must have been): Communicative Purpose"
                puntos:
                  - "PAST DEDUCTION: 'must have + V3' (~95% sure it happened), 'may/might/could have + V3' (possible past cause), 'can't/couldn't have + V3' (impossible in the past)."
                  - "PAST EVALUATION / CRITIQUE: 'should (not) have + V3' / 'ought to have + V3' (something was advisable, but the opposite happened!)."
                  - "UNREALIZED PAST POTENTIAL: 'could have + V3' (had the capability/opportunity, didn't happen) & 'needn't have + V3' (did something unnecessary)."
                ejemplo: "The inverter tripped at noon; cloud-edge lensing must have caused a brief irradiance spike."
              - numero: 2
                seccion: "STRUCTURE & PATTERNS"
                titulo: "Core Grammatical Blueprint"
                puntos:
                  - "Continuous past deduction: 'must / might have been + V-ing' ('The sensor must have been drifting during Trial 2')."
                  - "Passive past modal: 'modal + have been + V3' ('Thermal paste should have been applied evenly')."
                  - "Contrast: 'didn't need to calibrate' (wasn't needed, so we didn't) vs. 'needn't have calibrated' (we calibrated it, then found out it was factory-calibrated!)."
                tabla:
                  - ["Past Modal", "Retrospective Function", "Engineering Diagnostic"]
                  - ["must have + V3", "Strong logical conclusion", "Arc marks show a surge must have hit."]
                  - ["can't have + V3", "Logical impossibility", "The pump can't have run; power was off."]
                  - ["should have + V3", "Missed best practice", "We should have logged ambient humidity."]
              - numero: 3
                seccion: "QUESTIONS & NEGATION"
                titulo: "Interrogative, Negative & Short Answers"
                puntos:
                  - "In peer reviews and incident reports, prefer impersonal passive ('A snubber circuit should have been included') over blaming individuals!"
                ejemplo: "In hindsight, a larger heat sink should have been selected for the MOSFET stage."
              - numero: 4
                seccion: "PRECISION & CONTRAST"
                titulo: "Key Distinctions & Common Pitfalls"
                puntos:
                  - "Pronunciation & writing reminder: 'must've, could've, should've' sound like /əv/ in speech, NEVER write 'of'!"
                tabla:
                  - ["Form", "Did the Action Happen?", "Example"]
                  - ["didn't have to / didn't need to", "Usually NO (not required)", "We didn't have to recompile."]
                  - ["needn't have + V3", "YES (done unnecessarily)", "We needn't have printed 30 copies."]
              - numero: 5
                seccion: "CAMPUS & LAB CONTEXT"
                titulo: "Authentic Academic & Engineering Usage"
                puntos:
                  - "The inverter tripped at noon; cloud-edge lensing must have caused a brief irradiance spike."
                  - "In hindsight, a larger heat sink should have been selected for the MOSFET stage."
                  - "That anomaly couldn't have originated in the battery pack because its breaker was open."
                ejemplo: "Academic Register (CEFR B2): Clear, concise communication in Unimagdalena seminars."
              - numero: 6
                seccion: "MASTERY CHECK"
                titulo: "Self-Assessment & Oral Drill"
                puntos:
                  - "Deduce past cause: 'The fuse is melted and smells burnt' (use 'must have')."
                  - "Critique politely in passive: 'Nobody grounded the shield cable' (use 'should have been')."
                  - "Explain 'could have exploded' vs. 'might have leaked' in an incident briefing."
                ejemplo: "Practice reading each model sentence aloud with natural stress and intonation."
          - numero_tema: 6
            corte: 2
            modalidad: "general"
            titulo: "Hedging & Academic Caution (Appears to, Tends to, Suggests that)"
            objetivo: "Modular afirmaciones científicas con cautela epistémica (hedging) para evitar generalizaciones absolutas no demostradas."
            concepto_clave_latex: ""
            ejemplo: "Our findings suggest that hybrid PV-wind sizing can lower LCOE in off-grid communities."
            bloque_sugerido: "Peer-Review Tone 35 min • Calibrating epistemic certainty in discussions"
            slides:
              - numero: 1
                seccion: "CEFR B2 • CORE CONCEPT"
                titulo: "Hedging & Academic Caution (Appears to, Tends to, Suggests that): Communicative Purpose"
                puntos:
                  - "Scientific integrity requires distinguishing PROVEN LAWS from EMPIRICAL INTERPRETATIONS using 'hedging' (epistemic caution)."
                  - "Lexical hedges: modal verbs (may, might, could), epistemic verbs (appear to, seem to, tend to, suggest, indicate), adverbs (arguably, plausibly, relatively, predominantly), and qualifiers (under tested conditions)."
                  - "Overstating claims ('This proves X solves all grid issues') triggers immediate peer-review rejection!"
                ejemplo: "Our findings suggest that hybrid PV-wind sizing can lower LCOE in off-grid communities."
              - numero: 2
                seccion: "STRUCTURE & PATTERNS"
                titulo: "Core Grammatical Blueprint"
                puntos:
                  - "Strong claim -> Hedged claim: 'Causes corrosion' -> 'Tends to accelerate corrosion under high salinity.'"
                  - "Reporting evidence: 'These results suggest / indicate that...' (softer than 'prove')."
                  - "Probability adjectives: 'It is likely / plausible / conceivable that...'."
                tabla:
                  - ["Device Category", "Hedge Expressions", "Academic Sentence"]
                  - ["Epistemic Verbs", "appear to, tend to, suggest", "Dust accumulation tends to lower yield."]
                  - ["Modal & Adverb", "may potentially, largely", "BESS may substantially curb curtailment."]
                  - ["Scope Limiter", "within this regime, preliminarily", "Preliminary data point to a 9% gain."]
              - numero: 3
                seccion: "QUESTIONS & NEGATION"
                titulo: "Interrogative, Negative & Short Answers"
                puntos:
                  - "Balance caution with confidence: do NOT double- or triple-hedge needlessly (*It might possibly perhaps seem to suggest* is weak); 1–2 precise hedges strike ideal IEEE tone."
                ejemplo: "Cell degradation tends to accelerate when operating temperatures consistently exceed 330 K."
              - numero: 4
                seccion: "PRECISION & CONTRAST"
                titulo: "Key Distinctions & Common Pitfalls"
                puntos:
                  - "Know WHEN NOT to hedge: established physical laws and your exact experimental actions take direct verbs ('We measured V every 2 s'; 'Energy is conserved')."
                tabla:
                  - ["Too Blunt / Absolute", "Balanced B2/C1 Academic Hedge"]
                  - ["This eliminates blackouts forever.", "This approach can significantly reduce outage risk."]
                  - ["Salt air destroys all inverters.", "Coastal salinity appears to accelerate enclosure degradation."]
              - numero: 5
                seccion: "CAMPUS & LAB CONTEXT"
                titulo: "Authentic Academic & Engineering Usage"
                puntos:
                  - "Our findings suggest that hybrid PV-wind sizing can lower LCOE in off-grid communities."
                  - "Cell degradation tends to accelerate when operating temperatures consistently exceed 330 K."
                  - "This discrepancy may be attributed to unmodeled parasitic capacitance."
                ejemplo: "Academic Register (CEFR B2): Clear, concise communication in Unimagdalena seminars."
              - numero: 6
                seccion: "MASTERY CHECK"
                titulo: "Self-Assessment & Oral Drill"
                puntos:
                  - "Hedge this overclaim: 'Electric vehicles will solve climate change.'"
                  - "Hedge an experimental anomaly explanation using 'may be attributed to' or 'appears to'."
                  - "Identify which sentences in a discussion section need hedging vs. direct statement."
                ejemplo: "Practice reading each model sentence aloud with natural stress and intonation."
          - numero_tema: 7
            corte: 2
            modalidad: "general"
            titulo: "Discourse Markers for Data Presentation & Trend Analysis"
            objetivo: "Describir gráficas, tendencias dinámicas, tasas de cambio y correlaciones durante ponencias y análisis de resultados."
            concepto_clave_latex: ""
            ejemplo: "As shown in Figure 3, wind generation climbs steeply above cut-in speed before plateauing at rated power."
            bloque_sugerido: "Data Commentary 40 min • Presenting figures & preposition accuracy (by/to/of/at)"
            slides:
              - numero: 1
                seccion: "CEFR B2 • CORE CONCEPT"
                titulo: "Discourse Markers for Data Presentation & Trend Analysis: Communicative Purpose"
                puntos:
                  - "Pair precise TREND VERBS (surge, climb, plateau, fluctuate, dip, plummet) with DEGREE ADVERBS (sharply, steadily, marginally, exponentially)."
                  - "Verb + Adverb pattern ('Demand rose sharply by 18%') = Adjective + Noun pattern ('There was a sharp 18% rise in demand')."
                  - "Preposition precision: rise FROM 10 TO 15 (span), increase BY 5 (delta!), peak AT 22 MW (point), an increase OF 5 MW (after noun!)."
                ejemplo: "As shown in Figure 3, wind generation climbs steeply above cut-in speed before plateauing at rated power."
              - numero: 2
                seccion: "STRUCTURE & PATTERNS"
                titulo: "Core Grammatical Blueprint"
                puntos:
                  - "Visual signposting in talks: 'As illustrated in Figure 2,...', 'Turning to the dashed curve,...', 'Notably, a plateau occurs between...'"
                  - "Contrast & correlation: 'In stark contrast,...', 'Conversely,...', 'Closely mirroring irradiance, output peaks at solar noon.'"
                tabla:
                  - ["Movement", "High-Precision Verbs", "Preposition Rule"]
                  - ["Rapid Upward", "surge, soar, jump, climb", "rose BY 14% / FROM 40 TO 46"]
                  - ["Stability / Peak", "level off, plateau, peak", "stabilized AT 60 Hz / peaked AT 9 MW"]
                  - ["Downward", "decline, drop, dip, plummet", "a drop OF 3.2 V (noun + of)"]
              - numero: 3
                seccion: "QUESTIONS & NEGATION"
                titulo: "Interrogative, Negative & Short Answers"
                puntos:
                  - "CRITICAL PREPOSITION CHECK: 'increased BY 12%' (= delta +12%) vs. 'increased TO 82%' (= final level 82%)! Mixing 'by' and 'to' changes the math completely!"
                ejemplo: "Between 12:00 and 14:00, campus cooling load peaked at 1.8 MW, whereas PV supplied 640 kW."
              - numero: 4
                seccion: "PRECISION & CONTRAST"
                titulo: "Key Distinctions & Common Pitfalls"
                puntos:
                  - "Avoid repetitive 'went up / went down' in formal talks -> vary between verb+adverb and 'saw/experienced a [adj] [noun]'."
                tabla:
                  - ["Verb Construction", "Equivalent Noun Construction"]
                  - ["LCOE fell dramatically by 70%.", "Solar PV experienced a dramatic 70% fall in LCOE."]
                  - ["Efficiency leveled off at 3000 rpm.", "A clear efficiency plateau was observed at 3000 rpm."]
              - numero: 5
                seccion: "CAMPUS & LAB CONTEXT"
                titulo: "Authentic Academic & Engineering Usage"
                puntos:
                  - "As shown in Figure 3, wind generation climbs steeply above cut-in speed before plateauing at rated power."
                  - "Between 12:00 and 14:00, campus cooling load peaked at 1.8 MW, whereas PV supplied 640 kW."
                  - "Battery state of charge declined steadily overnight by 42 percentage points."
                ejemplo: "Academic Register (CEFR B2): Clear, concise communication in Unimagdalena seminars."
              - numero: 6
                seccion: "MASTERY CHECK"
                titulo: "Self-Assessment & Oral Drill"
                puntos:
                  - "Convert to Noun Phrase: 'Grid demand rose steadily from 8 GW to 11 GW.'"
                  - "Choose preposition: 'Efficiency improved (by / to) 3.5%, reaching 96.5%' -> 'by'."
                  - "Deliver a 60-second spoken walkthrough of a daily solar duck-curve chart."
                ejemplo: "Practice reading each model sentence aloud with natural stress and intonation."
          - numero_tema: 8
            corte: 3
            modalidad: "general"
            titulo: "Structuring an IMRaD Research Paper (Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion)"
            objetivo: "Dominar la arquitectura retórica IMRaD, tiempos verbales por sección y transiciones de artículos científicos."
            concepto_clave_latex: ""
            ejemplo: "Section II details the governing thermodynamic equations and boundary conditions."
            bloque_sugerido: "IMRaD Blueprint 45 min • Drafting structured sections of an IEEE paper"
            slides:
              - numero: 1
                seccion: "CEFR B2 • CORE CONCEPT"
                titulo: "Structuring an IMRaD Research Paper (Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion): Communicative Purpose"
                puntos:
                  - "IMRaD = Introduction (Why did you do it?), Methods (How did you do it?), Results (What did you find?), and Discussion (What does it mean?)."
                  - "CARS Model (Swales) for Introductions: Move 1 Establish territory -> Move 2 Identify research niche/gap -> Move 3 Occupy the niche ('In this work, we present...')."
                  - "Hourglass flow: broad context (Intro) -> narrow reproducible specifics (Methods/Results) -> broad implications & limitations (Discussion/Conclusion)."
                ejemplo: "Section II details the governing thermodynamic equations and boundary conditions."
              - numero: 2
                seccion: "STRUCTURE & PATTERNS"
                titulo: "Core Grammatical Blueprint"
                puntos:
                  - "Methods = Past Simple Passive + exact parameters so peers can replicate ('A 10 kW inverter was tested under IEC 62116')."
                  - "Results = Past Simple for findings + Present Simple to refer to visuals ('Table 2 summarizes...', 'Output reached...')."
                  - "Discussion = interpret mechanisms, compare with literature ('consistent with [14]'), acknowledge limitations, propose future work."
                tabla:
                  - ["IMRaD Section", "Primary Communicative Goal", "Dominant Tenses"]
                  - ["Introduction", "Context -> Gap -> Contribution", "Present Perfect & Present Simple"]
                  - ["Methods", "Reproducible setup & equations", "Past Simple Passive"]
                  - ["Results", "Objective data & figures", "Past Simple (+ Present for Fig/Table)"]
                  - ["Discussion", "Interpretation, comparison, limits", "Present Simple + Hedging Modals"]
              - numero: 3
                seccion: "QUESTIONS & NEGATION"
                titulo: "Interrogative, Negative & Short Answers"
                puntos:
                  - "Keep Results & Discussion distinct when required: Results state WHAT happened ('Voltage dropped 4%'); Discussion explains WHY ('attributable to line inductance')."
                ejemplo: "As summarized in Table 1, the proposed controller outperformed PI tuning by 21%."
              - numero: 4
                seccion: "PRECISION & CONTRAST"
                titulo: "Key Distinctions & Common Pitfalls"
                puntos:
                  - "Never introduce brand-new raw experimental numbers for the first time in the Conclusion!"
                tabla:
                  - ["Section Signpost", "High-Utility Academic Phrase"]
                  - ["Gap (Intro)", "Nevertheless, few studies have addressed transient thermal coupling in..."]
                  - ["Limitation (Disc.)", "A limitation of the present model is the assumption of isotropic conductivity."]
              - numero: 5
                seccion: "CAMPUS & LAB CONTEXT"
                titulo: "Authentic Academic & Engineering Usage"
                puntos:
                  - "Section II details the governing thermodynamic equations and boundary conditions."
                  - "As summarized in Table 1, the proposed controller outperformed PI tuning by 21%."
                  - "Future work will extend this framework to unbalanced three-phase distribution feeders."
                ejemplo: "Academic Register (CEFR B2): Clear, concise communication in Unimagdalena seminars."
              - numero: 6
                seccion: "MASTERY CHECK"
                titulo: "Self-Assessment & Oral Drill"
                puntos:
                  - "Classify 6 sample sentences into I, M, R, or D based on verb tense and rhetoric."
                  - "Write a 3-sentence CARS Introduction (Territory -> Gap -> Contribution) for a renewable topic."
                  - "Draft 1 limitation sentence + 1 future-work sentence."
                ejemplo: "Practice reading each model sentence aloud with natural stress and intonation."
          - numero_tema: 9
            corte: 3
            modalidad: "general"
            titulo: "Pitching Projects & Defending Technical Proposals in English"
            objetivo: "Estructurar presentaciones ejecutivas de proyectos energéticos y responder preguntas críticas de jurados en inglés."
            concepto_clave_latex: ""
            ejemplo: "Good morning. Today we present a resilient solar-storage microgrid for rural health centers."
            bloque_sugerido: "Oral Defense Studio 45 min • 3-minute technical pitch & live Q&A simulation"
            slides:
              - numero: 1
                seccion: "CEFR B2 • CORE CONCEPT"
                titulo: "Pitching Projects & Defending Technical Proposals in English: Communicative Purpose"
                puntos:
                  - "High-impact technical pitch structure (3–5 minutes): (1) Quantified Problem Hook, (2) Proposed Engineering Solution, (3) Technical & Economic Feasibility (KPIs / LCOE / ROI), (4) Validation & Call to Action."
                  - "Signposting guides listeners effortlessly: 'I'll begin by outlining...', 'Moving on to our architecture,...', 'To wrap up,...'."
                  - "Handling tough Q&A: Acknowledge -> Bridge/Clarify -> Answer concisely with evidence!"
                ejemplo: "Good morning. Today we present a resilient solar-storage microgrid for rural health centers."
              - numero: 2
                seccion: "STRUCTURE & PATTERNS"
                titulo: "Core Grammatical Blueprint"
                puntos:
                  - "Delivery fundamentals: pause before key metrics, stress contrastive numbers ('NOT 12 megabytes, under ONE POINT TWO megabytes'), maintain eye contact instead of reading dense paragraphs."
                  - "Q&A buffers for complex questions: 'That's a crucial point regarding grid inertia. In our simulations,...'"
                  - "Honest boundary handling: 'While harmonic flicker was outside our current scope, preliminary checks suggest...'."
                tabla:
                  - ["Pitch / Q&A Stage", "Professional Phrase", "Purpose"]
                  - ["Hook", "Every year, coastal grids lose 14%...", "Establish urgency with data"]
                  - ["Transition", "Having sized the array, let's examine cost.", "Smooth logical bridge"]
                  - ["Q&A Defense", "That's an insightful question. Our data show...", "Composed, evidence-led reply"]
              - numero: 3
                seccion: "QUESTIONS & NEGATION"
                titulo: "Interrogative, Negative & Short Answers"
                puntos:
                  - "Rule of 6 on slides: concise bullet cues (like UM STUDIO's MinimalSlideViewer!), NEVER walls of text read verbatim."
                ejemplo: "From an economic standpoint, the system achieves payback in 4.2 years."
              - numero: 4
                seccion: "PRECISION & CONTRAST"
                titulo: "Key Distinctions & Common Pitfalls"
                puntos:
                  - "Avoid defensive fillers ('Eh, no, you didn't understand me') -> reframe diplomatically: 'Allow me to clarify Slide 4...'."
                tabla:
                  - ["Blunt / Informal Q&A", "Diplomatic B2/C1 Defense"]
                  - ["I don't know that number.", "I don't have the exact figure at hand, but it falls near 85%."]
                  - ["You're wrong about the cost.", "Actually, when O&M is factored in, life-cycle cost drops by 18%."]
              - numero: 5
                seccion: "CAMPUS & LAB CONTEXT"
                titulo: "Authentic Academic & Engineering Usage"
                puntos:
                  - "Good morning. Today we present a resilient solar-storage microgrid for rural health centers."
                  - "From an economic standpoint, the system achieves payback in 4.2 years."
                  - "Thank you for raising thermal derating — we accounted for 40°C ambient conditions in Santa Marta."
                ejemplo: "Academic Register (CEFR B2): Clear, concise communication in Unimagdalena seminars."
              - numero: 6
                seccion: "MASTERY CHECK"
                titulo: "Self-Assessment & Oral Drill"
                puntos:
                  - "Write a 45-second Problem-Solution-Impact elevator pitch for an energy project."
                  - "Practice 3 diplomatic Q&A responses to skeptical reviewer questions."
                  - "Deliver a 6-slide presentation aloud using signposting transitions."
                ejemplo: "Practice reading each model sentence aloud with natural stress and intonation."
          - numero_tema: 10
            corte: 3
            modalidad: "general"
            titulo: "Critical Synthesis, Paraphrasing & Avoiding Plagiarism in IEEE Style"
            objetivo: "Sintetizar múltiples fuentes académicas, parafrasear estructuralmente y citar rigurosamente bajo formato IEEE."
            concepto_clave_latex: ""
            ejemplo: "Recent studies [1]–[3] converge on green hydrogen as a viable seasonal storage vector."
            bloque_sugerido: "IEEE Synthesis Lab 45 min • Structural paraphrasing & multi-source literature synthesis"
            slides:
              - numero: 1
                seccion: "CEFR B2 • CORE CONCEPT"
                titulo: "Critical Synthesis, Paraphrasing & Avoiding Plagiarism in IEEE Style: Communicative Purpose"
                puntos:
                  - "True paraphrasing transforms BOTH vocabulary AND syntactic structure while preserving exact technical meaning AND citing the source [1]."
                  - "Patchwriting (swapping 2–3 synonyms while copying sentence skeleton) counts as plagiarism in international journals!"
                  - "IEEE Citation Style uses numbered square brackets in order of appearance: '[1]', '[2], [3]', '[4]–[7]' — placed BEFORE punctuation ('...as shown in [3].')."
                ejemplo: "Recent studies [1]–[3] converge on green hydrogen as a viable seasonal storage vector."
              - numero: 2
                seccion: "STRUCTURE & PATTERNS"
                titulo: "Core Grammatical Blueprint"
                puntos:
                  - "4-Step Paraphrase Technique: (1) Read & understand without looking, (2) Change voice/clause structure (Active <-> Passive, Clause <-> Nominalization), (3) Use accurate domain terminology (keep fixed terms like 'Rankine cycle'!), (4) Append '[N]' citation."
                  - "Integral citation (author as subject): 'As Sadiku [2] demonstrates,...' vs. Non-integral (data-focused): 'Losses rise quadratically with current [2].'"
                  - "Synthesis groups multiple studies by theme: 'While [1] and [4] favor Li-ion, [5] advocates flow batteries for >8 h storage.'"
                tabla:
                  - ["Citation Mode", "Focus", "IEEE Format Example"]
                  - ["Non-integral", "Finding / Process", "Perovskite stability has improved markedly [1], [2]."]
                  - ["Integral", "Author / Landmark work", "Çengel and Boles [3] formulate exergy destruction as..."]
                  - ["Numeric Treat", "Grammatical Noun", "In [4], a decentralized OPF algorithm is proposed."]
              - numero: 3
                seccion: "QUESTIONS & NEGATION"
                titulo: "Interrogative, Negative & Short Answers"
                puntos:
                  - " Notice IEEE bracket grammar: '[4]' can act as a noun ('In [4], the authors...' or 'contrary to [4]'), unlike APA '(Smith, 2024)'!"
                ejemplo: "Contrary to earlier assumptions in [4], dynamic line rating unlocked 18% extra capacity [5]."
              - numero: 4
                seccion: "PRECISION & CONTRAST"
                titulo: "Key Distinctions & Common Pitfalls"
                puntos:
                  - "Never translate a Spanish or English source word-for-word without citation (translation plagiarism is detected by cross-language similarity engines!)."
                tabla:
                  - ["Original Source Sentence", "Acceptable Paraphrase + IEEE Citation"]
                  - ["'High cell temperatures severely degrade PV module lifespan' (Duffie, 2020).", "Elevated operating temperatures have been shown to accelerate photovoltaic aging [1]."]
              - numero: 5
                seccion: "CAMPUS & LAB CONTEXT"
                titulo: "Authentic Academic & Engineering Usage"
                puntos:
                  - "Recent studies [1]–[3] converge on green hydrogen as a viable seasonal storage vector."
                  - "Contrary to earlier assumptions in [4], dynamic line rating unlocked 18% extra capacity [5]."
                  - "All external equations, datasets, and conceptual frameworks must be explicitly credited in IEEE references."
                ejemplo: "Academic Register (CEFR B2): Clear, concise communication in Unimagdalena seminars."
              - numero: 6
                seccion: "MASTERY CHECK"
                titulo: "Self-Assessment & Oral Drill"
                puntos:
                  - "Paraphrase structurally + cite [1]: 'Wind speed cubed governs the kinetic power available to a rotor.'"
                  - "Synthesize 2 contrasting findings ([2] = lower cost, [3] = shorter cycle life) in one sentence."
                  - "Check IEEE punctuation placement: '...efficiency reached 92% [6].' (period AFTER bracket!)."
                ejemplo: "Practice reading each model sentence aloud with natural stress and intonation."
          - numero_tema: 11
            corte: 2
            modalidad: "general"
            titulo: "Hedging and Cautious Language in Engineering Reports"
            objetivo: "Utilizar lenguaje tentativo y de matización (hedging) mediante verbos modales, adverbios de probabilidad y verbos epistémicos para calificar afirmaciones científicas según normas IEEE."
            concepto_clave_latex: ""
            ejemplo: "The experimental results appear to indicate a marginal increase in cell degradation under elevated ambient temperatures."
            bloque_sugerido: "Hedging Clinic 40 min • Transforming bold claims into cautious academic prose"
            slides:
              - numero: 1
                seccion: "CEFR C1 • CORE CONCEPT"
                titulo: "The Purpose of Hedging in Technical Writing"
                puntos:
                  - "Engineering claims must reflect appropriate levels of scientific certainty and experimental boundaries."
                  - "Overstating results ('This proves that...') weakens technical credibility and invites reviewer rejection."
                  - "Hedging distinguishes between established physical laws and plausible hypotheses or observed tendencies."
              - numero: 2
                seccion: "CEFR C1 • MODAL AUXILIARIES"
                titulo: "Graded Modals for Caution"
                puntos:
                  - "Certainty (100%): 'will produce', 'is determined by'."
                  - "High Probability (~80%): 'should reduce', 'is likely to mitigate'."
                  - "Possibility (~50%): 'may indicate', 'could contribute to'."
                  - "Low Probability (~25%): 'might suggest', 'would appear to follow'."
              - numero: 3
                seccion: "CEFR C1 • EPISTEMIC VERBS"
                titulo: "Distance-Creating Reporting Verbs"
                puntos:
                  - "'The data suggests that...' instead of 'The data proves that...'."
                  - "'The simulation tends to underestimate peak load by 4%.'"
                  - "'The algorithm appears to converge faster in meshed configurations.'"
                  - "'Preliminary measurements seem consistent with the proposed thermal model.'"
              - numero: 4
                seccion: "CEFR C1 • PROBABILITY ADVERBIALS"
                titulo: "Nuanced Adverbial Modifiers"
                puntos:
                  - "Frequency/Scope: 'predominantly', 'substantially', 'to a certain extent'."
                  - "Degree: 'marginally', 'moderately', 'noticeably higher'."
                  - "Belief: 'plausibly', 'reportedly', 'arguably the most efficient architecture.'"
                  - "Example: 'The efficiency gain was marginally lower than expected due to parasitic losses.'"
              - numero: 5
                seccion: "CEFR C1 • APPLICATION"
                titulo: "Sentence Transformation Drill"
                puntos:
                  - "Bold: 'Turbine vibration causes fatigue failure.'"
                  - "Hedged: 'Excessive turbine vibration appears to accelerate fatigue failure under cyclic aerodynamic loads.'"
                  - "Bold: 'Our converter is 100% stable.'"
                  - "Hedged: 'The proposed converter demonstrated robust stability across the evaluated operating envelope.'"
          - numero_tema: 12
            corte: 2
            modalidad: "general"
            titulo: "Complex Passives and Impersonal Reporting Structures"
            objetivo: "Redactar resúmenes ejecutivos y revisiones bibliográficas usando estructuras impersonales de nivel C1 ('It is widely acknowledged that...', 'The prototype is reported to have...')."
            concepto_clave_latex: ""
            ejemplo: "It has long been recognized that grid inertia declines as inverter-based resources replace synchronous generators."
            bloque_sugerido: "Impersonal Structures 40 min • Passive reporting verbs in state-of-the-art sections"
            slides:
              - numero: 1
                seccion: "CEFR C1 • CORE PATTERN"
                titulo: "Impersonal 'It' Construction"
                puntos:
                  - "Pattern: 'It is + [past participle] + that-clause'."
                  - "Used to state general consensus or collective research findings objectively."
                  - "Common verbs: acknowledged, argued, believed, estimated, hypothesized, observed."
                  - "Example: 'It is generally estimated that offshore wind capacity will quadruple by 2035.'"
              - numero: 2
                seccion: "CEFR C1 • PERSONAL PASSIVE"
                titulo: "Subject + Passive Verb + To-Infinitive"
                puntos:
                  - "Pattern: 'Subject + is/are + [past participle] + to + [infinitive]'."
                  - "More concise and dynamic than the dummy 'it' structure."
                  - "Example: 'The perovskite cell is reported to exceed 28% efficiency under laboratory conditions.'"
                  - "Past reference: 'The substation was reported to have tripped at 14:32 UTC.'"
              - numero: 3
                seccion: "CEFR C1 • ACADEMIC OBJECTIVITY"
                titulo: "Avoiding Personal Pronouns (I, We, You)"
                puntos:
                  - "Instead of: 'We found that harmonic distortion increased.'"
                  - "Use: 'Harmonic distortion was found to increase at high modulation indices.'"
                  - "Instead of: 'You can see the voltage drop in Figure 4.'"
                  - "Use: 'The voltage drop is clearly evidenced in Figure 4.'"
              - numero: 4
                seccion: "CEFR C1 • CONTINUOUS & PERFECT FORMS"
                titulo: "Advanced Passive Infinitives"
                puntos:
                  - "Continuous: 'The transformer is understood to be operating near its thermal limit.'"
                  - "Perfect: 'The gas turbine is believed to have undergone scheduled maintenance last month.'"
                  - "Passive infinitive: 'The policy is expected to be ratified by the energy commission in Q4.'"
              - numero: 5
                seccion: "CEFR C1 • EDITING PRACTICE"
                titulo: "Executive Summary Polish"
                puntos:
                  - "Draft: 'Engineers believe that hydrogen blending causes micro-cracking.'"
                  - "Revised: 'Hydrogen blending is hypothesized to induce micro-crack propagation in API 5L line pipes.'"
                  - "Maintain formal register, academic detachment, and concise flow throughout the document."
          - numero_tema: 13
            corte: 2
            modalidad: "general"
            titulo: "Mixed Conditionals in Engineering Failure Analysis and Risk Assessment"
            objetivo: "Construir oraciones condicionales mixtas para vincular hipótesis pasadas con consecuencias presentes en investigaciones de accidentes y análisis de causas raíz (RCA)."
            concepto_clave_latex: ""
            ejemplo: "If the protective relay had cleared the short circuit instantaneously, the transformer would not be out of service today."
            bloque_sugerido: "Root-Cause Conditionals 40 min • Mixed conditionals in failure investigation reports"
            slides:
              - numero: 1
                seccion: "CEFR C1 • LOGICAL RELATION"
                titulo: "Past Cause with Present Consequence (Type 3 + Type 2)"
                puntos:
                  - "Condition in the past (Past Perfect) -> Result in the present (Would + bare infinitive)."
                  - "Formula: 'If + had + V3, Subject + would/could/might + V1'."
                  - "Used to explain how a past omission or event directly causes an ongoing operational state."
                  - "Example: 'If the team had installed surge arresters, the inverter would not be offline now.'"
              - numero: 2
                seccion: "CEFR C1 • ALTERNATIVE MIX"
                titulo: "Present Permanent Trait with Past Consequence (Type 2 + Type 3)"
                puntos:
                  - "Condition is a permanent state or trait (Past Simple) -> Result was a past event (Would have + V3)."
                  - "Formula: 'If + Past Simple, Subject + would have + V3'."
                  - "Used when a permanent system limitation or design flaw caused a specific failure."
                  - "Example: 'If the battery chemistry were inherently non-flammable, thermal runaway would not have occurred.'"
              - numero: 3
                seccion: "CEFR C1 • FORMAL INVERSION"
                titulo: "Inverted Conditional Forms (Without 'If')"
                puntos:
                  - "Type 3: 'Had the operator checked the differential pressure, the filter rupture could have been avoided.'"
                  - "Type 2: 'Were the conductor diameter larger, joule losses would be significantly lower.'"
                  - "Type 1: 'Should the frequency drop below 59.5 Hz, under-frequency shedding will activate.'"
              - numero: 4
                seccion: "CEFR C1 • CONJUNCTIVE VARIANTS"
                titulo: "Provided that, Unless, and But for"
                puntos:
                  - "'Provided that cooling water flow is maintained, operating temperature remains stable.'"
                  - "'Unless the bypass valve opens, pipeline pressure will exceed safe operating limits.'"
                  - "'But for the backup diesel generator, the control center would have lost SCADA telemetry.'"
              - numero: 5
                seccion: "CEFR C1 • ROOT CAUSE ANALYSIS DRILL"
                titulo: "Drafting Post-Incident Reports"
                puntos:
                  - "Scenario: A blackout occurred because an aging insulator flashed over during rain."
                  - "Statement: 'Had thermal imaging inspections been performed last quarter, the degraded insulator would have been identified prior to failure.'"
                  - "Express precise causal links, counterfactual arguments, and preventive recommendations."
          - numero_tema: 14
            corte: 3
            modalidad: "general"
            titulo: "Nominalisation and Information Density in Technical Writing"
            objetivo: "Optimizar la densidad léxica y concisión estilística transformando estructuras verbales y oraciones subordinadas en sintagmas nominales complejos según estándares de Elsevier y Springer."
            concepto_clave_latex: ""
            ejemplo: "The rapid deployment of distributed battery storage facilitated peak shaving and feeder congestion relief."
            bloque_sugerido: "Lexical Density 40 min • Nominalisation techniques for high-impact journal abstracts"
            slides:
              - numero: 1
                seccion: "CEFR C1 • STYLISTIC PRINCIPLE"
                titulo: "What is Nominalisation?"
                puntos:
                  - "Converting verbs, adjectives, and entire clauses into noun phrases (e.g., 'to combust' -> 'combustion')."
                  - "Increases information density: packs more technical content into fewer words."
                  - "Creates thematic cohesion: previous sentence actions become subjects of subsequent sentences."
                  - "hallmark of professional peer-reviewed research papers and engineering standards."
              - numero: 2
                seccion: "CEFR C1 • VERB-TO-NOUN MAPPING"
                titulo: "Common Derivational Suffixes"
                puntos:
                  - "-tion / -sion: fluctuate -> fluctuation; convert -> conversion."
                  - "-ance / -ence: resist -> resistance; emit -> emittance / emission."
                  - "-ment: deploy -> deployment; degrade -> degradation."
                  - "-ity: conduct -> conductivity; unstable -> instability."
              - numero: 3
                seccion: "CEFR C1 • COMPLEX COMPOUND NOUNS"
                titulo: "Pre-modifying Noun Chains"
                puntos:
                  - "Clause: 'A system that monitors the temperature of batteries in real time.'"
                  - "Nominalised: 'A real-time battery temperature monitoring system.'"
                  - "Clause: 'When solar irradiation drops intermittently.'"
                  - "Nominalised: 'Intermittent solar irradiance attenuation.'"
              - numero: 4
                seccion: "CEFR C1 • AVOIDING PITFALLS"
                titulo: "Preventing 'Zombie Noun' Clutter"
                puntos:
                  - "Over-nominalisation can make prose dense, leaden, and difficult to comprehend."
                  - "Weak: 'The implementation of the algorithm was conducted by the research team.'"
                  - "Strong: 'The research team implemented the algorithm.'"
                  - "Rule: Nominalise to connect concepts and increase flow; keep active verbs for core methodology."
              - numero: 5
                seccion: "CEFR C1 • ABSTRACT REFACTORING"
                titulo: "Hands-on Density Exercise"
                puntos:
                  - "Verbose (28 words): 'Because the rotor rotated faster than normal, the bearings began to wear down and this caused the gearbox to fail unexpectedly.'"
                  - "Concise (14 words): 'Excessive rotor rotational speed accelerated bearing degradation, culminating in catastrophic gearbox failure.'"
                  - "Word count reduced by 50% while elevating academic rigor."
          - numero_tema: 15
            corte: 3
            modalidad: "general"
            titulo: "Structuring Oral Presentations, Keynote Addresses and Q&A Defense"
            objetivo: "Estructurar exposiciones orales para conferencias internacionales IEEE utilizando frases de señalización (signposting), manejo de preguntas difíciles y refutación diplomática."
            concepto_clave_latex: ""
            ejemplo: "That is an insightful observation; nevertheless, our sensitivity analysis demonstrates that the model remains robust against price fluctuations."
            bloque_sugerido: "Conference Keynote 40 min • Signposting phrases and handling peer-review Q&A gracefully"
            slides:
              - numero: 1
                seccion: "CEFR C1 • PRESENTATION ARCHITECTURE"
